AppShell.description: AppShell is the page shell for an application. It provides slots for top navigation, side navigation, banners, and main content. Use it as the root wrapper for every page. It handles responsive mobile navigation and skip-to-content automatically. Configure side nav collapse on SideNav with its collapsible prop.

practices.text: Choose the right height: use "fill" for dashboards with internal scrolling and "auto" for pages that grow with content.
Set `contentPadding` based on content type: 4 for forms and settings, 0 for tables and dashboards.
Give every nav slot an accessible name. AppShell renders TopNav and SideNav as separate navigation landmarks, and a screen reader lists them by name, so pass `label` to each one.
Start the page heading inside `children`. AppShell owns the skip link, the banner landmark and the main landmark, but it renders no heading, so the first heading in the content area is the page h1.

On phones, opt the page into the full screen with `viewport-fit=cover` in the viewport meta tag (`width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover`). AppShell then extends its header under the status bar and out to the screen sides, and keeps the header's items and the end of the content inside the device's safe area. An installed web app can also draw under the status bar with `<meta name="apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style" content="black-translucent">`. In landscape only the header is inset: an inline SideNav and the content's sides still reach under a notch, so keep content padding there. A shell with no header region or phone top bar keeps no top inset; keep top padding there.
Nest one AppShell inside another; it's the outermost layout frame.
Use for sub-page layouts; use Layout for content areas within AppShell.
Add your own skip link or <main> element. AppShell already renders both, and a second main landmark makes the first ambiguous.

props.name: children
props.description: Main content area, rendered inside a <main> element.

props.name: contentPadding
props.description: Padding for the main content area. Set based on the dominant content pattern: 4 (16px) for forms/settings/text, 0 for dashboards/maps/tables. Override individual sections with Section.

props.name: topNav
props.description: Top navigation slot, typically TopNav.

props.name: sideNav
props.description: Side navigation slot, typically SideNav.

props.name: mobileNav
props.description: Mobile navigation configuration. Accepts false (disable), a config object (tune auto behavior), or ReactNode (full custom drawer). The config object is {hasToggle?: boolean, isOpen?: boolean, onOpenChange?: (isOpen: boolean) => void, content?: ReactNode, breakpoint?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | '2xl' | 'none', defaultIsMobile?: boolean}; breakpoint defaults to 'md', resolves through the nearest Theme's widthBreakpoints, and switches to the wider layout at equality. 'none' is always non-mobile and ignores defaultIsMobile.

props.name: banner
props.description: Banner slot for system-wide announcements, placed above the topNav.

props.name: height
props.description: Height behavior: 'fill' makes the shell fill the viewport (100dvh) with independent scroll containers; 'auto' lets the shell grow with content and uses sticky positioning for nav.

props.name: variant
props.description: Navigation background style controlling how nav areas contrast with content. 'wash' uses wash background, 'surface' uses surface background, 'section' adds dividers between nav and content, 'elevated' uses wash nav with elevated surface content and border radius.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

AspectRatio.description: Maintains a fixed width-to-height ratio for its children as its container resizes. Use it for media containers like videos, images, thumbnails, or any content that needs consistent proportions. It takes its width from the container and derives its height from the ratio, so it needs an ancestor with a definite width.

practices.text: Express the ratio as a fraction for readability — `ratio={16 / 9}` rather than `ratio={1.78}`. It is a number, so the string form `ratio="16/9"` is a type error.
Use for media that needs consistent proportions across screen sizes.
Use `fit="cover"` for images and video so the component sizes the child; the child should not repeat `width`/`height`/`objectFit` styles.
Pass one child. With `fit` set, every direct child is stretched to fill the box, so put an overlay or caption inside a single wrapper child rather than passing it as a second child.
Describe media children with `alt`, or `alt=""` when the image is decorative. AspectRatio adds no role and no accessible name of its own, so the child carries the whole accessible description.

For a breakpoint-dependent ratio, override the ratio responsively: pass an `aspectRatio` rule via `xstyle` (StyleX), or override `aspect-ratio` from your own unlayered CSS under a `@media`/`@container` rule; component styles live in the `astryx-base` cascade layer, so unlayered consumer CSS wins. Give an `xstyle` rule a `default` branch alongside the conditional one (`{default: 3, '@container ...': '3 / 2'}`); with only the conditional branch the ratio is unset outside the query and the box collapses.
Use for general layout containers; use standard layout components instead.
Nest AspectRatio containers; one level is sufficient.
Constrain the height on its own. The width comes from the container, so a `height` or `maxHeight` by itself clamps the box off ratio; pair it with `width: "auto"` to size from the height instead.
Place it in a shrink-to-fit parent such as `inline-flex`, `width: fit-content` or a floated box. It contributes no intrinsic width there and collapses to zero.

props.name: ratio
props.description: Aspect ratio as width/height (e.g. 16/9, 1). Emitted as a class-level declaration (never inline), so `xstyle` rules or unlayered consumer CSS can override it responsively.

props.name: shape
props.description: Container shape. Both respect the `ratio`. `ellipse` clips to an oval (a circle when `ratio={1}`).

props.name: fit
props.description: How the child is sized inside the ratio box. `cover` fills and crops media, `contain` fills and letterboxes, `center` keeps the natural size centered. When omitted, the child styles itself.

props.name: children
props.description: Content positioned absolutely to fill the container.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

Avatar.description: Avatar represents a person or team with a profile photo, initials, or a default icon. Use it in comment headers, contact lists, chat messages, user cards, and anywhere you need to identify someone visually.

practices.text: Always pass a name so the avatar can show initials if the photo fails to load, and so screen readers can announce who it represents.
Pick a size that matches the context: xsm or sm for inline mentions, md or lg for lists and cards, xl for profile headers.
Add a status dot when knowing someone's availability matters, like in chat or team views.
When wrapping an Avatar in your own Tooltip or HoverCard, set tooltip={false} so the built-in name tooltip does not overlap yours.
Give every interactive avatar (href or onClick) a name or alt. It is the control's accessible name, and it warns in development when it is missing.
Rely on a status label to name an interactive avatar. "Online" says nothing about where the link goes.
Use Avatar for logos, product images, or anything that isn't a person or team. Use an image or icon instead.
Use xstyle or className to override shape. Use the shape prop instead so themes can control it globally.

props.name: src
props.description: Primary image source URL.

props.name: fallbackSrc
props.description: Fallback image when primary fails.

props.name: name
props.description: User name for initials and alt text.

props.name: alt
props.description: Alt text (falls back to name).

props.name: size
props.description: Avatar size: named sizes are 'xsm' (20px), 'sm' (24px), 'md' (36px), 'lg' (48px), and 'xl' (128px); numeric sizes must be one of the pixel values listed in the type. Inside an AvatarGroup, the group's size always overrides this prop, including when the group uses its default size.

props.name: shape
props.description: Shape variant of the avatar. 'circle' (default) stays fully round. 'rounded' uses the element radius token so it matches UI corner rounding and can be set globally via theme. 'square' has no radius. Status dot positioning adapts automatically: 4-o'clock on circle, bottom-right corner on rounded/square.

props.name: status
props.description: Corner content for status indicators. AvatarStatusDot reports its `label` to the avatar, which composes it into the accessible name (e.g. "Jane Doe, Online") so screen readers announce the status. Reporting goes through context, so it still works when the dot sits inside a wrapper component of your own.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Tooltip shown on hover and keyboard focus. Omitted or true shows the avatar's name; a string shows that text instead; false shows no tooltip. Not auto-disabled when wrapped in your own Tooltip/HoverCard. Set tooltip={false} if you supply your own overlay. No tooltip is shown when tooltip is true/omitted and there is no name.

props.name: href
props.description: When set, the avatar renders as an interactive link (`<a>` or a custom link component) pointing here. This follows the same element-swap rule as Button. Requires a meaningful accessible name via `alt` or `name`: an interactive avatar without one warns in development. Inside an AvatarGroup, interactive avatars share a single Tab stop and are reached with arrow keys.

props.name: as
props.description: Custom link component used when `href` is set (e.g. `next/link`). Overrides the provider-level LinkProvider default. Only applies with `href`.

props.name: target
props.description: Link target attribute. Only applies with `href`.

props.name: rel
props.description: Link rel attribute. Only applies with `href`.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler. When set without `href`, the avatar renders as a focusable `<button type="button">`. Requires a meaningful accessible name via `alt` or `name`: an interactive avatar without one warns in development.

AvatarGroup.description: AvatarGroup displays multiple avatars in an overlapping row with an optional overflow indicator. Uses a compositional API: pass Avatar children directly so each avatar can carry its own props (status dots, click handlers, etc.).

practices.text: Slice the list yourself and pass only the avatars you want visible; 3-5 is typical. The group renders exactly the children it is given and never slices for you.
Use AvatarGroupOverflow for custom overflow content like a popover trigger or "add member" button.
Pass status dots, click handlers, or tooltips directly on each Avatar child.
Wrap an Avatar child in HoverCard or Tooltip to show more on hover; the avatars still overlap. Set tooltip={false} on the wrapped Avatar so its built-in name tooltip does not compete.

Make avatars interactive with href or onClick to link to profiles. Interactive avatars share a single Tab stop; arrow keys move between them, and the group announces a keyboard hint to assistive tech. This follows the WAI-ARIA APG roving tabindex technique for managing focus in a composite: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#kbd_roving_tabindex
Don't nest AvatarGroups; use a single group with all avatars.
Don't set size on the child avatars. The group's size wins over each child's own size prop, including when the group leaves size at its default, so a child's size is silently ignored inside a group.

props.name: children
props.description: Avatar children, optionally followed by one AvatarGroupOverflow. Consumers handle slicing to the desired visible count.

props.name: size
props.description: Size applied to all avatars: named sizes are 'xsm' (20px), 'sm' (24px), 'md' (36px), 'lg' (48px), and 'xl' (128px); numeric sizes must be one of the pixel values listed in the type. The group's size always overrides each child Avatar's size, including when the group uses its default size.

props.name: shape
props.description: Shape applied to all avatars via context, overriding each avatar's own shape prop. Also applied to AvatarGroupOverflow's "+N" indicator.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the root element.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

AvatarGroupOverflow.description: AvatarGroupOverflow appears at the end of an AvatarGroup to summarize people who are not shown individually. Use it when a group is sliced to a small number of visible avatars but the hidden count still matters.

practices.text: Pass the real hidden count to `count` so the accessible label matches the visible indicator.
Use short custom text such as `+12` or `99+`. The indicator is circular for short counts and grows into a pill for wider counts so the number always fits.
Provide `onClick` when the overflow opens a member list, popover, or detail view.
Do not pass custom text that disagrees with `count`; `count` continues to provide the accessible label.
Do not use long labels inside the indicator; place longer participant details next to the group instead.

props.name: count
props.description: The number of hidden avatars. Used for the default `+N` label and the accessible label.

props.name: children
props.description: Optional custom count text rendered inside the indicator. Omit to use the default `+N` label.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Callback fired when the overflow indicator is clicked. When provided, the indicator renders as a focusable button.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the overflow indicator element.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: stylex.create() value — not an inline style object.

props.name: variant
props.description: Semantic variant pairing colour with a distinct shape: success = filled green dot, neutral = grey ring, error = red dot with a minus bar.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label describing the status. Inside an Avatar it is composed into the avatar's accessible name (e.g. "Jane Doe, Online"); the Avatar root is role="img", which prunes child semantics, so the composed name is how the status reaches assistive tech. Standalone dots expose role="img" with this label directly.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon centered inside the dot (hidden at tiny sizes). A rendered icon replaces the built-in shape glyph, so use a different icon per status.

Badge.description: Badge highlights a status or category at a glance. Use it sparingly: only when a value represents a distinct state (Active, Failed) or a grouping tag (Engineering, Design). Most metadata (dates, durations, counts, descriptions) should be plain description text, not badges.

practices.text: Every status badge steals attention. Only badge states where the user needs to notice or act: errors, warnings, items requiring follow-up. If no action is needed, plain text is fine.
Use success, warning, and error variants only for system status that demands attention: "Failed", "Degraded", "Action Required". These have bold solid backgrounds designed to stand out.
Use color variants (blue, purple, teal, etc.) for category tags that group or classify items: team names, content types, priority levels.
Keep labels to one or two words. If you need more detail, put it in surrounding text instead of the badge.
Add an icon when it helps identify the badge type quickly, but always include a text label alongside it.

Apply a "success" badge to every healthy/active/normal item. If all rows show green "Active" badges, none stand out; the badge adds noise, not information. Show only the states that need user attention (errors, warnings, pending actions).
Use badges for metadata. Durations ("6h window"), counts ("12 trigger types"), dates, and descriptions are not statuses or categories; use description text (Text with type="supporting") instead.
Use semantic status variants (success, warning, error, info) for categories or informational content. These are visually loud and should only indicate system state.

Repeat the same badge in every row of a table or list. If the same value appears in most rows, it's not adding information; use plain text for common states and reserve badges for the exceptional ones.
Make badges clickable; they are read-only indicators. Use a button or link if the user needs to take action.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual style variant. Semantic variants (neutral, info, success, warning, error) use solid backgrounds. Non-semantic color variants use tinted backgrounds with colored text for categorization and tagging.

props.name: label
props.description: Badge text content. A badge is one line and at least as tall as that line of its label, so it grows with its text (a larger text size); a label wider than the space available is cut with an ellipsis rather than escaping its container; a string or number label is also set as the badge's title so the full text stays reachable on hover.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional leading icon.

Banner.description: Banner shows a persistent message at the top of a page or section. Use it for form errors, system updates, maintenance notices, or success confirmations that the user needs to see until they act on it.

practices.text: Pick a status that matches the message: info for updates, warning for caution, error for problems, success for confirmations.
Use the card container inside page content and the section container for full-width messages that span the entire page.
Make info and success banners dismissable. Keep error banners visible until the user fixes the issue.
Keep titles short and scannable: "Payment failed" not "There was a problem processing your most recent payment."
Use Banner for short-lived messages that disappear on their own; use Toast instead.
Stack multiple banners with the same status; combine related messages into one banner.

Set collapsible={false} when the user needs the content to act on the message, like the list of fields that failed validation. Keep the default toggle when the detail is long enough to bury the banner's own message.

Banner status controls color and icon only; it does not create a live region. Announce async outcomes from the transition handler with useAnnounce. Pass role="alert" only for an urgent message the person must act on now: Banner puts it on the title and description, so controls, endContent and supporting content are not read as part of the alert. Do not also announce that message with useAnnounce.
Rely on the status color or icon alone to carry meaning; say which status it is in the title text, because the icon is decorative to a screen reader.

props.name: status
props.description: Status type controlling icon and color.

props.name: title
props.description: Title text or ReactNode displayed in the header.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text rendered below the title in the header.

props.name: icon
props.description: Override the default status icon.

props.name: isDismissable
props.description: Whether the banner can be dismissed by the user.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Called when the dismiss button is clicked; banner hides itself regardless of whether this is provided.

props.name: dismissLabel
props.description: Accessible name and visible tooltip for the dismiss button (pass it already translated). Defaults to "Dismiss <title>" for a string title, so stacked banners are distinguishable; set it when the title is a ReactNode.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Action content rendered in the header area, end-aligned. Wraps to its own row below the text when the header is too narrow to hold both.

props.name: container
props.description: Container type: card has border-radius; section is full-width with no border-radius for page-level use.

props.name: elevation
props.description: Resting shadow depth. Use for a floating banner that hovers above content; `none` is the default inline banner. A `card`-container banner rounds its shadow to match.

props.name: children
props.description: Content rendered in the card-background area below the colored header. Sits behind an expand/collapse toggle unless `collapsible={false}`.

props.name: collapsible
props.type: boolean | {defaultIsOpen?: boolean; isOpen?: boolean; onOpenChange?: (isOpen: boolean) => void}
props.description: Whether the content area (children) sits behind an expand/collapse toggle in the header. On by default, starting collapsed. `false` opts out: children are always visible with no toggle. `{defaultIsOpen: true}` starts open; `{isOpen, onOpenChange}` is controlled. Takes the same CollapsibleConfig as Collapsible.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

Blockquote.description: A quotation block with a rule on its inline-start edge and secondary text color. Use to highlight quoted content, testimonials, or excerpts. The rule and padding are logical, so they move to the right edge in right-to-left locales.

practices.text: Use for quoted text, testimonials, or highlighted excerpts from external sources.
Provide a cite prop when the source of the quote is known.
Pass the source through cite rather than typing it into children, so it renders as a semantic <cite> element that assistive technology can distinguish from the quotation.
Use for callout boxes or informational notes; use Banner for those.
Wrap the attribution in your own <footer>. A <footer> inside a <blockquote> becomes a contentinfo document landmark, and a page with several quotes then reports several page footers.

props.name: children
props.description: Content of the blockquote.

props.name: cite
props.description: Optional attribution for the quote. Rendered in a <cite> element after the quoted content.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

BottomSheet.description:
A mobile touch surface for filters, actions, forms, and detail views that should rise from the bottom of the viewport. For a multi-step flow, give each step its own sheet and one state value that names the open step (see Replacing a sheet); open a second sheet over the first when a step should stay visible beneath it.

Stacking. Every sheet keeps its own isOpen. Open a sheet while another scrim sheet is open and it stacks on top: the sheet beneath stays mounted with its scroll position and inputs, recedes behind the new one (the nearest covered sheet shrinks to 0.96 and lifts 8px, deeper ones to 0.92 and 16px), and is blocked from pointer, keyboard, and assistive technology by the top sheet's modal dialog. The sheets can be siblings, live in separate components, sit inside another sheet's content, or sit inside a BottomSheetSwitcher step; a whole switcher is one level, and switching its step in place does not change its position. Nothing moves in the DOM: each sheet's dialog stays where it is written, and no wrapper component is needed.

Order is open order. The top sheet is the one presented most recently that is still open; a sheet that closes and reopens comes back on top. When several sheets open in one update (a deep link into a flow), there is no open order between them, so tree order decides: a sheet below the sheets rendered in its content, siblings in the order they are written. That order is right in the first painted frame.

One scrim. Only the bottom sheet's backdrop dims the page; the backdrops of the sheets above it are transparent, so a stack never darkens per level. The dim holds steady while sheets push and pop, and if the bottom sheet closes while sheets remain above it, the next sheet's backdrop takes over in the same frame.

Dismissal. Escape, a tap on the scrim, a downward swipe, and a platform close request (Android back, a close watcher) reach only the top sheet, through that sheet's own onOpenChange, and that sheet's purpose applies: required blocks all of them, form blocks the scrim and the swipe. Nothing closes a whole stack at once; set every sheet closed in one update when a flow is done and they leave together.

Closing a covered sheet from code. Sheets rendered inside the closing sheet's content are part of it: they are presented only while it is open and leave with it. Their isOpen stays yours, as with a Dialog rendered in a closed Dialog: nothing is written to it, and a nested sheet that is still open when its host reopens is presented again, on top. Set it closed yourself when the flow is done. Sheets above the closing sheet that are not in its content stay open and keep their order; the closing sheet slides out from beneath them, and if it owned the scrim, the sheet above takes it over.

Replacing a sheet. Close the top sheet and open another in the same update (one state value that names the open step does this) and the new sheet replaces it instead of stacking on it: the new sheet rises above the one it replaces; if the replaced sheet is taller it moves down to meet the new sheet's top edge at the same time; the replaced sheet fades only after both motions finish, and is inert and hidden from assistive technology from the start. The scrim holds steady throughout, with no dip; focus moves into the new sheet; and when the flow closes, focus returns to the element that opened its first sheet, whichever sheet closed last. This is the handoff the deprecated BottomSheetSwitcher ran between its steps; a multi-step flow needs no switcher: give each step its own BottomSheet and one state value. A replace happens only when exactly one sheet closes and one opens in the update, the closing sheet was the top sheet of its stack, and the move was made from inside it (the control last pressed, or with no recent press the focused element, was in the closing sheet, as a step's own Continue or Back button is); a covered sheet closing while a sheet opens, a close and an open in different updates, or a close and an open driven from a control outside the closing sheet (two unrelated owners acting at once) keep the ordinary push and pop motion and their own focus return. A replace over an open stack runs one level up and leaves the sheets beneath covered. Non-modal sheets (hasScrim={false}) replace each other the same way, with no scrim: they are hosted in the browser top layer as manual popovers, so the entering step orders above the retained one with no page-level z-index, and toasts raised before or while the sheet is open stay above it. Below the Popover API support floor (Tier 2 in the browser support guide) the sheet falls back to show() in page stacking order: usable, but with no promise over later page content. A non-modal sheet returns focus to its opener on close only while focus is still inside it; focus taken elsewhere on the live page stays there.

Focus. Opening a sheet, modal or not, focuses its data-autofocus field (a TextInput with hasAutoFocus) in every browser. Without one, focus goes wherever the engine's native dialog focusing steps land: the panel in Chromium, the first focusable control in Firefox. A step entering as a replacement also focuses a data-autofocus descendant first, so a flow that opens on a field keeps the keyboard on it. Closing the top sheet returns focus into the sheet it reveals: to the control that opened it when that control is still there, otherwise to the revealed sheet's panel. When the last sheet closes, the standalone rules apply: finalFocusRef, else the element that opened the sheet, with a focus ring only after keyboard input. When every sheet of a stack closes in one update, focus returns once, to the bottom sheet's finalFocusRef or opener, after the last dialog has closed.

Caveats. A Dialog, AlertDialog, or Popover opened from a sheet paints above the sheet and does not make it recede; a sheet opened from inside that Dialog paints above the Dialog and stacks over the sheet beneath. Sheets with hasScrim={false} stay out of the stack entirely (they replace each other, but never stack, recede, or take the scrim). A sheet React hides (a suspended Suspense boundary, Activity mode="hidden") leaves the stack and closes its dialog; when it is shown again it is presented again, on top. Only sheets rendered in the same document stack; a sheet inside an iframe is its own stack.

practices.text: Use for mobile-first surfaces (filters, share sheets, quick actions) where the content should rise from the bottom edge.

For a drill-in, open the next sheet over the current one and keep each sheet's isOpen where its data lives; a detail sheet can sit inside the list sheet that opens it, right next to the row. Close every sheet in one update to close the whole flow.
Pick the starting height that fits the content: 'hug' for short bounded content, 'capped' for lists, and 'tall' for forms or streaming/resizing content.
Use purpose='form' to protect entered data from scrim clicks and swipes while keeping Escape available; reserve purpose='required' for flows that must end through an explicit action.
Don't make the sheet content overly long. Break it into steps, each its own sheet, with one state value naming the open step; moving on replaces one with the next.

Don't stack more than two or three sheets: deeper sheets share the second recede step and the user has to pop them one at a time. Replace steps instead (close one, open the next in one update) when they do not need to stay visible.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Whether a standalone sheet is open. Fully controlled; pair with onOpenChange. Omitted only inside the deprecated BottomSheetSwitcher, which drives its steps itself.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: For a standalone sheet, called when it requests an open-state change. Automatic calls follow purpose: info dismisses on Escape, scrim click, or swipe; form dismisses on Escape only; required never dismisses implicitly. Omitted only inside the deprecated BottomSheetSwitcher, which drives its steps itself.

props.name: finalFocusRef
props.description: Optional explicit focus-return target for a standalone sheet. Use when the opener can remount or the active element is not a reliable trigger, such as an adaptive presentation switch. Always focused when the sheet closes on its own or last; when a modal sheet is still open beneath, focus returns into that sheet (to this element if it is inside it, else the revealed panel). Omitted only inside the deprecated BottomSheetSwitcher, which drives its steps itself.

props.name: purpose
props.description: Controls implicit dismissal behavior, matching Dialog. info allows Escape, scrim click, and swipe-to-dismiss. form protects entered data by blocking scrim click and swipe while allowing Escape. required blocks every implicit dismissal path and uses role='alertdialog'. Explicit controls may still update the controlled state. Works for standalone and BottomSheetSwitcher-managed sheets.

props.name: sheetId
props.description: Deprecated with BottomSheetSwitcher: give each step its own standalone sheet with isOpen instead. Still works as released: the unique ID of this sheet inside a BottomSheetSwitcher, which opens it when activeSheet matches; omit isOpen and onOpenChange when sheetId is used.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the sheet. Required; the sheet has no built-in heading to derive a name from.

props.name: children
props.description: Sheet content in a scrollable area. The named body is keyboard reachable while overflowing. Forward Tab entry may move directly to the first native link or button; input controls, composite widgets, and nested scroll areas retain the body stop. Shift+Tab from a delegated first child skips the body. Fitting content adds no body stop. The internal observed content box preserves block flow and percentage heights. If it includes a text-entry control that can bring up the mobile keyboard, use height='tall' and keep the sheet fully expanded while editing.

props.name: padding
props.description: Internal padding of the sheet content using the spacing scale, matching Dialog. When omitted, uses the theme default for bottom sheets (--spacing-4 unless the theme sets padding on bottom-sheet). A lone Section child escapes the padding, and bleed children such as Table and Divider compensate against it. Use 0 for edge-to-edge content that supplies its own inset. Whatever the padding, the block-start inset is never less than the grab bar's height (--spacing-6), so resting content starts below the bar.

props.name: height
props.description: How tall the sheet is. Named budgets: 'hug' fits its content up to 92% of the viewport, 'capped' is a scrolling mid-height panel (~62%), and 'tall' is a pinned near-full panel (~92%) for content that streams in. Or pass a number (px) / CSS length for a custom budget. Give snapPoints to let the user drag between heights. On shorter viewports the sheet fills the available height. Only a fully expanded 'tall' sheet provides mobile-keyboard accommodation: it stays put and scrolls each focused control above the keyboard. Hug, Capped, numeric and CSS-length heights never do, and a Tall sheet stops doing it the moment the user drags it to a shorter detent, resuming when they drag it back. Outside that state the sheet neither moves nor adds keyboard scroll space, and the browser's own focus reveal is left in place; on iOS that reveal can shift the whole page. This accommodation applies where the visual viewport shrinks for the keyboard, as in Safari on iOS, Firefox for Android and Chrome on Android, where the sheet places the focused control just above the keyboard as it comes up, and the control rides the rest of Gboard’s slide up, and the slide down after it loses focus; a hide Chrome reports late, such as Back, rides down from Chrome’s report (`astryx docs browser-support`).

props.name: snapPoints
props.description: Extra heights the sheet can rest at when dragged; its own height is always the tallest stop, and omitting this gives a sheet that only opens and closes. Each stop is the sheet's visible height: a number is a viewport fraction (0.5 is half the screen), '50%' the same in CSS, '320px' an absolute length. A stop of a quarter of the sheet or less is a peek: it slides away instead of reflowing, and thins the scrim.

props.name: hasScrim
props.description: For a standalone BottomSheet, whether to render a scrim, the semi-transparent overlay that covers and blocks the background. true (default) uses showModal(): top layer, native focus containment, ::backdrop scrim, body scroll lock, and tap-scrim-to-dismiss when purpose='info', with the background inert. A scrim sheet also takes part in stacking (see Stacking below). false presents the sheet in the top layer as a manual popover (below the Popover API support floor, show() in page stacking order as a reduced fallback) with no scrim, no focus trap and no scroll lock, leaving the page behind interactive and scrollable; a no-scrim sheet neither stacks nor is stacked on, but no-scrim steps replace each other with the same handoff. A no-scrim sheet shown while a modal (a scrim sheet or a Dialog) that does not contain it is open is inert under that modal and stays beneath it (show(), no page-level z-index) until that modal has gone, then enters the top layer; a modal mid-exit counts as gone, and rendered inside the modal the sheet enters the top layer at once. In a multi-step flow, set hasScrim the same on every step.

BottomSheetSwitcher.description:
Deprecated: write each step as its own BottomSheet with isOpen, controlled by one state value that names the open step. Closing the top sheet and opening the next in the same update, from a control inside the open step, runs the same replace handoff (see BottomSheet, Replacing a sheet), with no sheetId and no switcher; a step changed from a control outside the flow (a page control, or code after focus left the step) closes and opens with ordinary push and pop motion. BottomSheetSwitcher keeps working until a future minor release removes it: a flow used on its own behaves as released (with three fixes: a toast raised from a step renders above the flow and can be pressed, under reduced motion its steps follow the reduced-motion rule, and a step with a hasAutoFocus field opens on that field in every browser), and a flow stacked with other sheets is one level of the stack (it recedes and is blocked when covered, shares the one scrim, and stands down from dismissal while covered). Modal and hasScrim={false} flows migrate the same way. Set activeSheet to a nested BottomSheet's sheetId to open or switch steps, and to null to close.

Stacking. A scrim flow is one level in the stack of open sheets (see BottomSheet, Stacking). Open it while a standalone sheet is open and the flow sits on top of that sheet, which recedes and is blocked; open a standalone sheet while the flow is open, from a step's content or from anywhere else, and that sheet sits on top while the whole flow recedes as one. Switching the step in place never changes the flow's position. Escape, the scrim, a swipe, and a platform close request reach only the top level: the flow's onActiveSheetChange(null) when the flow is on top, the standalone sheet's onOpenChange(false) when that sheet is. A standalone sheet rendered inside a step's content is presented only while that step is the active one: it leaves when the flow switches step or closes, its isOpen stays yours, and it is presented again, on top, if the step returns while it is still open. Only the bottom level's backdrop dims the page. A no-scrim flow stays out of the stack.

practices.text: Prefer one standalone BottomSheet per step with one state value naming the open step; the replace handoff is the same and nothing has to be nested under a switcher.

Migrate an existing flow in place: replace activeSheet / onActiveSheetChange with one step value, give each step isOpen={step === id} and a guarded onOpenChange (clear the step only if it is still the open one) in place of sheetId, remove the wrapper and move its hasScrim onto every step. Map the other switcher props: onCancel becomes a guarded onOpenChange on each step (ignore false while the flow must stay open) — a standalone sheet reports Escape, the platform close, the scrim tap and the swipe all as onOpenChange(false) with no reason, so the guard holds the step against all of them while it applies, and a veto of Escape alone has no equivalent; the only per-path lever is purpose (form keeps Escape and blocks the scrim tap and the swipe; required blocks all three and exposes the step as an alertdialog). A consumer aria-label or aria-labelledby becomes each step label, which names its dialog. ref, id, data-testid, className, style, xstyle and the other dialog props have no dialog-level equivalent: a standalone sheet sends its ref and base props to the panel div and its dialog is implementation, so a test or anchor that needs the dialog queries the panel closest("dialog"), and dialog-level styling is dropped.
Don't split information across sheets when people need to compare it; use a full-page layout that keeps the relevant content visible together instead.
Don't use a step flow when multiple panels must stay interactive or visible together; a flow intentionally selects one interactive step.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref resolved to the native dialog hosting the flow: the active sheet's dialog, which changes to the next sheet's on a handoff; the exiting sheet's through its exit; and, while the flow is closed, the dialog that hosted it last (or the first mounted sheet's). It is never null while a sheet is mounted, from the first commit on. id and data-testid render on this dialog only: a flow that mounts open carries them on the active sheet's dialog in server markup too; a flow that mounts closed carries them from the first commit's synchronous re-render on, and its server markup carries them on no element. Other dialog props apply to every sheet dialog.

props.name: onCancel
props.description: Called before the switcher handles a native cancel request (Escape or the platform close). Attached to every sheet dialog; the browser raises cancel on the dialog it is presenting, the active sheet's. Calling preventDefault() keeps the controlled flow open.

props.name: activeSheet
props.description: ID of the interactive BottomSheet, or null when the flow should close. Match a nested BottomSheet's unique sheetId; the previous sheet may remain visually present and inert while the new sheet enters, simultaneously align downward behind a shorter step, then fade away.

props.name: onActiveSheetChange
props.description: Called with null when the active sheet dismisses according to its purpose. Child BottomSheets may use purpose='form' or purpose='required' to limit implicit dismissal while flow controls can still use the same state setter to switch sheets or close the flow.

props.name: hasScrim
props.description: Whether the sheet dialogs are modal. true presents each sheet with showModal() for a native ::backdrop, native focus containment, one body scroll lock held for the whole flow, and click-to-dismiss when the active BottomSheet has purpose='info'; only one backdrop paints at a time. false uses show() with no backdrop and leaves the page interactive; avoid transformed, contained, or clipping ancestors because a non-modal dialog remains in its containing context.

props.name: children
props.description: BottomSheets identified by unique sheetId values.

BreadcrumbItem.description: BreadcrumbItem represents one destination, action, current location, or sibling-menu trigger inside a Breadcrumbs trail.

props.name: children
props.description: Label content for the breadcrumb item.

props.name: href
props.description: URL the breadcrumb links to; omit for non-navigable items.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler for the breadcrumb item.

props.name: isCurrent
props.description: Marks this item as the current page, applying aria-current="page". When omitted, the last item is auto-detected if no item is explicitly current; pass false to opt out.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon rendered before the item label.

props.name: menu
props.description: Menu opened when the item is activated, using the same item API as DropdownMenu/MoreMenu/ContextMenu (a DropdownMenuOption[] array or composed DropdownMenuItem children). Renders a link-styled menu trigger with a chevron and aria-haspopup="menu". Takes precedence over href/onClick.

props.name: menuSize
props.description: Size passed to the menu items. Defaults from the breadcrumb variant ('supporting' → 'sm', otherwise 'md').

props.name: as
props.description: Custom link component to render instead of <a>. Overrides the provider-level default from LinkProvider. Only applies to non-current items.

Breadcrumbs.description: Breadcrumbs show a trail of links from the root to the current page. Use them at the top of detail pages, settings panels, or anywhere the user needs to see where they are and navigate back up.

practices.text: Place breadcrumbs above the page heading so the user sees their location before reading the content.
Keep labels short and match the page titles they link to: "Settings" not "Application Settings Page".
Use the supporting variant in dense UIs like admin panels or sidebars where the breadcrumb should be subtle.
Make the last item plain text, not a link; it represents the current page. The component does this automatically when you set isCurrent.

The component implements the WAI-ARIA APG Breadcrumb pattern: a labelled nav landmark wrapping an ordered list, with aria-current="page" on the current item. A crumb with a menu additionally implements the APG Menu Button pattern, opening on Enter, Space or ArrowDown and closing on Escape.
Give each trail its own label when a page renders more than one, so the nav landmarks stay distinguishable in a screen reader landmark list.
Use breadcrumbs as the primary navigation. They supplement a sidebar or top nav, not replace it.
Show breadcrumbs on top-level pages that have no parent; they add clutter without helping the user.
Let the trail grow beyond 5 levels. If you need more, consider simplifying the page hierarchy instead.
The built-in slash separator mirrors automatically in RTL. For a custom separator, leave Unicode-mirrored angle quotes such as › alone; mirror arrows and Icon separators once with rtlStyles.mirror.

Mirror a separator the bidi algorithm already mirrors. An angle-quote glyph such as › is Bidi_Mirrored, so it flips under RTL on its own and rtlStyles.mirror would flip it back. An arrow glyph such as → and any Icon separator are not, so those do need rtlStyles.mirror through xstyle.

props.name: children
props.description: BreadcrumbItem elements to render inside the breadcrumb trail.

props.name: separator
props.description: Separator rendered between breadcrumb items. The built-in slash mirrors automatically in RTL.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual variant: supporting is smaller with secondary text styling.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the nav landmark (aria-label).

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

Button.description: Button triggers an action when clicked. Use it for form submissions, confirmations, navigation, or any interaction that needs a clear call to action.

practices.text: Reserve primary for the single most important action in the view. Use secondary or ghost for everything else based on emphasis.
Write labels that describe the action ("Save changes", "Delete account", "Send invite"), not vague labels like "OK" or "Click here".
Show a loading state for actions that take time, like saving or submitting, so the user knows it is working.
Always provide a label for icon-only buttons so screen readers can announce what the button does. Add a tooltip for sighted users.
For a dedicated icon-only button, use IconButton from '@astryxdesign/core/IconButton'. It is a separate component, not exported from '@astryxdesign/core/Button'.
Place more than one primary button in the same view; this dilutes the visual hierarchy.
Use the destructive variant without a confirmation step for irreversible actions like deleting data.
Use a button for navigation. If it only takes the user to another page, use a link instead. Buttons are for actions like saving, deleting, or submitting.

Restyle Button's `::before` (through `xstyle` or a `className` rule) and expect it to hold through a touch press: under a coarse primary pointer, while a press is on or fading, Button paints the press on that pseudo-element (`z-index: -1`, its opacity animated), so your styles merge into the press layer for that moment. At rest Button adds nothing there. Style a child element instead.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label. Rendered as visible text by default; used as aria-label when isIconOnly is true.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual style variant.

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant.

props.name: elevation
props.description: Resting shadow depth for floating buttons (e.g. a FAB). `none` is the default flat button; `low`/`med`/`high` map to the shadow token scale. Ignored inside a ButtonGroup, where elevation is owned by the group.

props.name: type
props.description: HTML button type attribute.

props.name: name
props.description: HTML name attribute for form submission.

props.name: value
props.description: HTML value attribute for form submission.

props.name: form
props.description: Associates the button with a form element by ID.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Shows a loading spinner and blocks re-activation while staying focusable (aria-busy + aria-disabled, not native disabled, so keyboard focus is never dropped mid-action). Announces "Loading" via a live region.

props.name: isInterruptible
props.description: Keep the button clickable while a clickAction is pending: the spinner and aria-busy still show, but the button is not disabled and the action is not deduped, so a re-click lands and interrupts the in-flight action with a fresh one.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the button. Uses aria-disabled instead of native disabled so the button stays focusable.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon element rendered before the label text. An Astryx Icon with no explicit size defaults to sm for sm/md buttons and md for lg buttons.

props.name: isIconOnly
props.description: When true, renders as a square icon-only button with label as aria-label. Requires icon. Tip: for a dedicated icon-only button component, use IconButton from '@astryxdesign/core/IconButton' instead.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the button. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is (e.g., '100%' for a full-width button). By default the button sizes to its content, never grows past its container, and truncates its label with an ellipsis when a row is too narrow; icon-only buttons stay square.

props.name: children
props.description: Optional override for visible text. When provided, displayed instead of label, but label is still required (it provides the accessible name). For most cases, just use label alone: <Button label="Save" />.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Trailing icon or badge rendered after the label. Ignored when isIconOnly is true. Color is inherited from the button variant.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Tooltip text shown on hover.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Standard click handler (passed through from ButtonHTMLAttributes).

props.name: clickAction
props.description: Async click handler. Shows loading state while the returned promise is pending.

props.name: href
props.description: When provided, renders the button as a link element (<a> or custom link component). The destination follows the shared navigation rule described on the Link `href` prop.

props.name: as
props.description: Custom link component to use when href is provided (e.g. Next.js Link).

props.name: target
props.description: HTML target attribute when rendered as a link (e.g. "_blank").

props.name: rel
props.description: HTML rel attribute when rendered as a link (e.g. "noopener noreferrer").

ButtonGroup.description: ButtonGroup joins related actions into a single connected control. Use it when multiple buttons represent related choices or operations that belong together visually, like copy/cut/paste, or undo/redo.

practices.text: Group buttons that perform related actions on the same object, like copy, cut, paste on selected text.
Use the same variant for all buttons in a group so they look like a single connected unit.
Keep groups small (2–4 buttons). For more actions, use a Toolbar or DropdownMenu instead.
Don't mix wildly different actions. A Save button next to a Delete button in the same group is confusing.
Don't use ButtonGroup for navigation. Use SegmentedControl or TabList for switching between views.
Don't nest ButtonGroups. If you need multiple groups, place them side by side with a gap.
Name the group for what its buttons act on. The label is the group's accessible name and a screen reader reads it before each member.

Keep the group a single Tab stop. Arrow keys move between members along the orientation, and Home/End jump to the ends. This is the WAI-ARIA APG roving tabindex technique: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#kbd_roving_tabindex
Don't disable the group to show that an action is in flight. Leave the group enabled and show progress on the button that started the work.

props.name: children
props.description: Button or IconButton children.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the group (aria-label).

props.name: orientation
props.description: Layout direction of the button group.

props.name: size
props.description: Default size for buttons in the group. Individual buttons can override.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether all buttons in the group are disabled.

props.name: elevation
props.description: Resting shadow depth for the whole group. The connected buttons share one surface, so the shadow lifts them as a unit. Use for a group that floats above content.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the root element.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

IconButton.description: A button that shows only an icon with no visible text. Use IconButton in toolbars, table rows, and compact UI where space is tight and the icon is universally understood.

practices.text: Make the aria-label specific: a trash icon labeled "Delete conversation" is clearer than just "Delete" for screen readers.
Add a tooltip: even a gear icon can mean Settings, Preferences, or Configure.
Use ghost in toolbars and dense areas to reduce visual clutter.
Use IconButton if the action isn't obvious from the icon alone; use Button with text.
Skip the tooltip; label only reaches screen readers, sighted users need the hover hint.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label. Used as aria-label (not rendered as visible text).

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon element rendered inside the button. An Astryx Icon with no explicit size defaults to sm for sm/md buttons and md for lg buttons.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual style variant.

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant.

props.name: elevation
props.description: Resting shadow depth. The most common FAB shape is an icon-only button, so raise it with `low`/`med`/`high` for a floating action button. `none` is the default flat button.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Shows a loading spinner and blocks re-activation while staying focusable (aria-busy + aria-disabled, not native disabled).

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the button. Uses aria-disabled instead of native disabled so the button stays focusable.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Tooltip text shown on hover and keyboard focus. It also describes the button, unless it repeats the button's accessible name.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Standard click handler.

props.name: clickAction
props.description: Async click handler with automatic loading state.

props.name: isInterruptible
props.description: Keep the button clickable while a clickAction is pending: the spinner and aria-busy still show, but the button is not disabled and the action is not deduped, so a re-click lands and interrupts the in-flight action with a fresh one. Use it for interruptible actions, not fire-once actions (submit, save, pay).

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the button. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is. Without it the button keeps its icon-only aspect, square by default; with it the button takes that width.

props.name: type
props.description: HTML button type attribute.

props.name: name
props.description: HTML name attribute for form submission.

props.name: value
props.description: HTML value attribute for form submission.

props.name: form
props.description: Associates the button with a form element by ID.

props.name: href
props.description: When provided, renders the button as a link element (<a> or custom link component). A disabled IconButton still renders a <button>.

props.name: as
props.description: Custom link component to use when href is provided (e.g. Next.js Link).

props.name: target
props.description: HTML target attribute when rendered as a link (e.g. "_blank").

props.name: rel
props.description: HTML rel attribute when rendered as a link (e.g. "noopener noreferrer").

ToggleButton.description: ToggleButton switches between selected and unselected states to represent a persistent on/off choice. Use it standalone for binary actions like bold, mute, or favorite, or inside a ToggleButtonGroup for single-select or multi-select toolbar controls.

practices.text: Use a filled or colored icon for the pressed state so users can see the current state at a glance: an outline star vs a solid star, for example.
Keep the label identical between pressed and unpressed states. Let the visual treatment (icon, weight, background) communicate the change.
Wrap related toggles in a ToggleButtonGroup with an accessible label so screen readers announce them as a connected set.
Don't use a ToggleButton for one-time actions like "Submit" or "Delete"; those are regular Buttons, not toggles.
Don't mix ToggleButtons with regular Buttons inside the same group; use only ToggleButtons in a ToggleButtonGroup.
Don't use a ToggleButton for on/off settings that persist across sessions; use a Switch instead, which better communicates "setting" semantics.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the button. Used as visible text, or as aria-label for icon-only buttons.

props.name: isPressed
props.description: Whether the button is currently pressed. Ignored for a ToggleButtonGroup member with a value.

props.name: onPressedChange
props.description: Called synchronously when pressed state should change. Receives the next state and the click event; call event.preventDefault() to skip pressedChangeAction. Without an Action, the callback produces no Action-pending feedback. Ignored for a ToggleButtonGroup member with a value.

props.name: pressedChangeAction
props.description: Action handler for API- or navigation-backed toggles, run in a transition after the synchronous onPressedChange callback unless that callback calls event.preventDefault(). Works without onPressedChange. Shows an optimistic pressed state and a spinner while pending, and remains interruptible by re-clicks. Omit it for callback-only toggles with no Action-pending feedback. Ignored for a ToggleButtonGroup member with a value.

props.name: size
props.description: Button size. Defaults to group size when inside a group.

props.name: elevation
props.description: Resting shadow depth for floating (FAB-style) toggle buttons, mirroring Button. `none` is the default flat button; `low`/`med`/`high` map to the shadow token scale. Applies inside a ToggleButtonGroup as well — grouped children retain their own elevation.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the button is disabled.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Whether the button shows a loading spinner.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon element. When provided without children, button becomes icon-only with tooltip from label.

props.name: isIconOnly
props.description: When true, renders as a square icon-only button with `label` as the aria-label and an automatic tooltip from the label.

props.name: pressedIcon
props.description: Icon shown when pressed. Falls back to icon if not provided.

props.name: children
props.description: Visible content. If omitted with icon, button becomes icon-only.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Tooltip text shown on hover.

props.name: value
props.description: Value identifier when used inside ToggleButtonGroup. Required in groups.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

props.name: children
props.description: ToggleButton children. Give each member a value; the group owns its pressed state and ignores its isPressed, onPressedChange, and pressedChangeAction props. Member activation calls the group’s onChange without starting a member Action transition.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the group (aria-label).

props.name: type
props.description: Selection mode. Single allows one active button, multiple allows many.

props.name: value
props.description: Currently selected value(s). Type depends on selection mode.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when selection changes.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Layout direction of the button group.

props.name: size
props.description: Default size for buttons in the group. Individual buttons can override.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether all buttons in the group are disabled.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

Calendar.description: Calendar lets the user pick a date or date range from a month grid. Use it in booking flows, scheduling UIs, date filters, or anywhere the user needs to see surrounding dates for context.

practices.text: Set min and max dates to limit selection to a valid window, like only future dates for a booking or the current quarter for a report.
Use range mode when the user needs to pick a start and end date, like a trip or a time-off request.
Use dateConstraints to disable specific dates like weekends or holidays, and explain why they are unavailable.
Show two months side by side when the user frequently selects dates that span a month boundary.

For a custom month view, use useCalendarNavigation and useCalendarDays from @astryxdesign/core/Calendar. To show another calendar system, pass the same calendar to both and feed visibleCalendarMonths into useCalendarDays. The hooks default to gregory and never read the InternationalizationProvider calendar.
Use a calendar for dates far in the past or future like a birth date. A text input is faster for open-ended entry.
Disable large blocks of dates without context. The user should understand why dates are unavailable.

props.name: mode
props.description: Selection mode.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled selected value. Use null for no selection; omit value or pass undefined for uncontrolled mode.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Uncontrolled default value.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Selection callback.

props.name: numberOfMonths
props.description: Number of months to display.

props.name: min
props.description: Minimum selectable date.

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum selectable date.

props.name: dateConstraints
props.description: Custom constraint functions.

props.name: maxRangeSpan
props.description: Range mode: max days a range may span, both endpoints counted (7 = a 7-day window). Caps the window from the picked start; before a start is picked every day stays selectable.

props.name: minRangeSpan
props.description: Range mode: min days a range must span, both endpoints counted (2 forbids a single-day range). Clicking the start again commits a one-day range when allowed, or cancels the in-progress selection when the minimum is longer. Default 1.

props.name: focusDate
props.description: Controlled visible month. Unset, the calendar opens on the selected date, else on today clamped into the min/max window.

props.name: onFocusDateChange
props.description: Navigation callback.

props.name: handleRef
props.description: Imperative handle for calendar navigation, including navigateTo().

props.name: hasOutsideDays
props.description: Show days from adjacent months.

props.name: hasWeekNumbers
props.description: Show ISO 8601 week numbers. They are ISO 8601 week numbers in every calendar system.

props.name: hasVariableRowCount
props.description: Give each month only the rows it needs. The default fixed 6-row grid keeps the same height from month to month; a variable row count trades that fixed height for a more compact grid.

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.description: First day of week. Accepts a number (0=Sunday) or a three-letter day name (e.g. "mon").

props.name: calendar
props.description: Calendar system the grid shows, such as 'persian', 'hebrew', or 'islamic-umalqura'. It sets the months, their names, and month and year navigation. value, min, max, focusDate, and every callback stay Gregorian ISO dates. Calendars other than gregory, iso8601, buddhist, roc, and japanese need Temporal; where the runtime lacks it, load a polyfill such as temporal-polyfill/full/global on the server and in the browser, or the grid shows Gregorian months. Month starts in the Chinese and Dangi calendars come from the runtime's Temporal, and some polyfills start a few months one day apart from native Temporal; when server and browser markup must match, use one implementation on both sides, such as installImplementation() from temporal-polyfill/full/shim, which replaces a native Temporal.

Card.description: Card is a bordered, elevated container for discrete, self-contained items: things you could reorder, remove, or interact with independently. Cards are NOT the default layout tool. Most content groups don't need a container at all; spacing and alignment create visual grouping naturally. Only reach for a Card when items need clear interaction boundaries or visual comparison in a grid.

practices.text: Ask "could I reorder or remove this independently?" If yes, it's a card. If no, it's just a section of the page: use a heading + Stack or Section.
Use cards for discrete items: a single user profile, a single notification, a single metric, a product in a grid. Each card represents one "thing" with clear interaction boundaries.
Spacing and alignment alone create visual grouping. Not everything needs a container; try removing the card and see if the grouping is still clear from whitespace and typography.
Keep padding consistent across sibling cards so they align visually in a grid or list.
Pair a card with Layout when you need a structured header, scrollable content, and footer with actions.

Let cards share a row or grid on a phone: a card shrinks to fit its track and clips content that cannot wrap at its edge. Truncate long IDs, hashes, and URLs with Text maxLines={1} (the full value shows in a tooltip), and give wide content its own scroll region: Table scrolls by itself; put code or other wide content in a ScrollableArea.
Default to cards for visual grouping. A heading + Stack with proper spacing creates hierarchy without adding borders everywhere. Cards should be the exception, not the default.
Wrap page sections in cards. "General Settings", "Notification Preferences", form groups: these are page regions, use Section or heading + stack.
Create identical card grids (icon + heading + text, repeated). Vary the layout or question whether cards are needed at all.
Nest cards inside other cards; flatten the hierarchy or use spacing and dividers instead.
Use color variants for status; use Banner or Badge for that. Color cards are for categorization.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the card (number = pixels, string = used as-is). In a flex row or grid track this is the preferred width: the card shrinks below it when the row is narrower. To hold the width in a flex row, wrap the card in StackItem (static by default) and let the row wrap or scroll. In Grid, set a consumer minWidth on the Card and size the track accordingly.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the card (number = pixels, string = used as-is).

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: Maximum width of the card.

props.name: minHeight
props.description: Minimum height of the card.

props.name: children
props.description: Content to render inside the card.

props.name: padding
props.default: the theme's card padding (spacing step 4 with no theme)
props.description: Internal padding using the spacing scale. Omit it and the card takes the theme's card padding rather than a step, so passing a step is a decision to override the theme, not a way to restate the default.

props.name: variant
props.description: Background color variant. `default` uses the standard card background. `transparent` drops the background entirely. `muted` uses the muted background for de-emphasised cards. The non-semantic variants use the corresponding `--color-background-<name>` token.

props.name: elevation
props.description: Resting shadow depth. `none` is flat; `low`/`med`/`high` map to the shadow token scale. Raise a card only when it needs to float above surrounding content.

ClickableCard.description: An interactive card for navigation or action targets. Nested interactive elements work independently.

practices.text: Use for cards that navigate to a detail page or trigger a single action.
Nest buttons or links freely inside; they handle their own events.
Use for toggling selection; use SelectableCard for that.

Use with a transparent variant and no padding only to borrow the press model for a surface that owns its own box. Compose the chrome-free recipe in the useClickableContainer docs instead: it adds no Card styles to the page.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessibility label.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler: fires on card surface only.

props.name: href
props.description: Navigation URL. Plain, new-tab, Cmd/Ctrl-click, and middle-click activation all follow the shared navigation rule described on the Link `href` prop.

props.name: target
props.description: Link target.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the card and removes a link destination; the card keeps its tab stop and is announced as disabled.

props.name: children
props.description: Card content.

props.name: padding
props.description: Inner padding.

props.name: variant
props.description: Background color variant.

props.name: elevation
props.description: Resting shadow depth. Often raised to signal the whole card is clickable.

props.name: width
props.description: Card width.

props.name: height
props.description: Card height.

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: Maximum card width.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

SelectableCard.description: A card that toggles between selected and unselected states with an accent border. For navigation use ClickableCard.

practices.text: Use for multi-select choices: filter chips, feature add-ons, or option grids where several can be on.
Use for multi-select groups; track the selected IDs in a Set.
When focused, toggle selection with Space or Enter.
Use for navigation; use ClickableCard for that.
Use for a single-select group: each card is a checkbox, so assistive technology announces a multi-select group with one tab stop per card.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessibility label.

props.name: isSelected
props.description: Controlled selection state.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when toggled.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the card.

props.name: children
props.description: Card content.

props.name: padding
props.description: Inner padding.

props.name: variant
props.description: Background color variant.

props.name: elevation
props.description: Resting shadow depth. The selection ring composes on top, so a selected card keeps its shadow.

props.name: width
props.description: Card width.

props.name: height
props.description: Card height.

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: Maximum card width.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

Carousel.description: Carousel scrolls a row of items horizontally when they overflow the available width. Use it for card grids, image galleries, product lists, or any set of items that should be browsable without taking up the full page.

practices.text: Enable scroll-snap when each item should land precisely at the start edge, like a gallery or product list.

For iOS paging under a finger and on a trackpad swipe, pass hasSnap={useSnapPaging()} from @astryxdesign/core/SnapPaging. A flick moves one view, or one item with useSnapPaging({pages: 'item'}). A mouse wheel keeps native snapping. Only a carousel given it loads the paging code.
Reach for hasLoop on small, cyclable sets like a photo gallery, where wrapping past the last item back to the first feels natural.
Always provide an aria-label that describes what the carousel contains, like "Featured products" or "Team members".

Carousel implements the WAI-ARIA APG carousel pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/carousel/) without auto-rotation: the region is labelled and carries aria-roledescription="carousel", each item is a group named "Slide N of M", and the scroll container is a tab stop while its content overflows, so keyboard users can pan it with the arrow keys; while everything fits it stays out of the tab order.
Use a consistent gap and item width so the carousel looks intentional, not like content overflowing by accident.
Trust the built-in navigation: trackpad users can swipe horizontally, and mouse users can hold Shift while scrolling the wheel to move through items.
Use a carousel for content every user must see. Not everyone scrolls horizontally, so put critical content above the fold.
Auto-advance items. Let the user scroll at their own pace.
Nest carousels. A carousel inside a carousel is confusing and breaks keyboard navigation.

props.name: children
props.description: Carousel items rendered in a horizontal scroll container.

props.name: gap
props.description: Gap between items using the spacing token scale.

props.name: hasButtons
props.description: Show prev/next navigation buttons when content is scrollable.

props.name: hasEdgeFade
props.description: Show a gradient edge-fade mask when content overflows, signalling that more items exist off-screen.

props.name: hasLoop
props.description: Wrap-around scrolling: next at the end scrolls to the start, prev at the start scrolls to the end. Buttons stay visible at both edges. Only engages when content overflows.

props.name: hasSnap
props.description: Snap each child to the start edge. hasSnap uses native CSS scroll snap. hasSnap={useSnapPaging()} adds iOS paging under a finger and on a trackpad swipe, on the same stops: a flick moves one view, or one item with useSnapPaging({pages: 'item'}). Only that value loads the paging code.

props.name: padding
props.description: Inline padding inside the scroll container, with matching scroll-padding so snap points align to the content edge.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible label for the carousel region.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the root element.

props.name: handleRef
props.description: Imperative handle exposing scrollNext(), scrollPrev(), scrollTo(index), canScrollNext(), and canScrollPrev() for programmatic scroll control.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the root element. Prefer xstyle.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

ChatComposer.description: ChatComposer is the message-entry shell for a chat surface. It coordinates a controlled or uncontrolled draft, provides a default token-capable input and send/stop action, and arranges optional drawer, header, footer, and status content. Custom inputs and send controls can join the same value, submission, disabled, stop, and focus contract through useChatComposerContext().

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Called when the user submits a message.

props.name: onStop
props.description: Called when the user requests to stop generation.

props.name: isStopShown
props.description: Whether the stop button is shown instead of the send button.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled input value.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Change handler for controlled mode.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when the input is empty.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the composer.

props.name: density
props.description: Visual density.

props.name: elevation
props.description: Resting elevation of the composer body. `low` (the default) keeps today's raised look: low at rest, bumping to med on hover / focus. `none` flattens it and draws a border. Keyboard focus in the editor adds the shared focus ring in either presentation; pointer focus does not add that ring.

props.name: drawer
props.description: Slot: collapsible drawer above the input: attachments, context chips, etc. Use ChatComposerDrawer.

props.name: headerActions
props.description: Slot: left-aligned header actions (attach, mention buttons). Use icon-only size="sm" buttons.

props.name: headerContext
props.description: Slot: right-aligned contextual info in the header (context window usage, ProgressBar, supporting text).

props.name: input
props.description: Slot: custom input element. Replaces the default input. Use ChatComposerInput for trigger menus/tokens, or wire any input (plain textarea, rich editor) to the composition contract via useChatComposerContext(): read value/onChange/onSubmit/canSend and register a focus control on inputControlRef so body-click-to-focus works.

props.name: footerActions
props.description: Slot: left-aligned footer actions (model selector, etc).

props.name: sendActions
props.description: Slot: actions to the left of the send button.

props.name: sendButton
props.description: Slot: custom send button. Replaces the default send/stop button.

props.name: status
props.description: Status message rendered below (or above) the composer.

props.name: statusPosition
props.description: Where to render the status.

ChatComposerDrawer.description: Use ChatComposerDrawer in the ChatComposer drawer slot for supplementary content such as attachments, context chips, or previews. Provide count only when people should be able to collapse that content.

practices.text: Give label a concrete plural noun such as "Attachments" so the expand and collapse actions have a useful accessible name.
Use controlled isCollapsed with onCollapsedChange when another part of the page owns drawer state; otherwise use defaultIsCollapsed.
Put primary composer actions in the drawer; use ChatComposer footer or send-action slots so those controls remain available when the drawer is collapsed.

props.name: children
props.description: Content to render inside the drawer: tokens, chips, previews, or any React elements.

props.name: count
props.description: Total item count shown in the collapsed badge. When provided, the drawer gains a collapse/expand toggle.

props.name: label
props.description: Label shown next to the count in the default collapsed summary and used to name the expand/collapse action.

props.name: collapsedSummary
props.description: Visual content for the complete Collapsed summary anatomy part. When count enables collapse, this replaces the default neutral Badge and label while the component retains disclosure behavior and accessible naming.
