props.name: isCollapsed
props.description: Controlled collapsed state. Use with `onCollapsedChange` for external control.

props.name: defaultIsCollapsed
props.description: Initial collapsed state for uncontrolled usage.

props.name: onCollapsedChange
props.description: Callback fired when the user toggles the drawer.

ChatComposerInput.description: Pass ChatComposerInput to ChatComposer's input slot when the draft needs trigger menus, inline tokens, history recall, dictation insertion, or file intake.

practices.text: Use handleRef for programmatic text or token insertion; inserted text follows the same onChange pipeline as typing.
Use onFiles for files pasted or dropped onto the editor, and keep file validation and upload progress in the product layer.
Use custom token rendering for ordinary mentions or commands; prefer the structured badge form so tokens remain predictable and themeable.

props.name: handleRef
props.description: Imperative handle for programmatic control: insertToken, expandToken, insertText, focus, and getValue.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled input value. Pair with onChange for two-way binding.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when the input value changes. The serialized string includes token placeholders.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when the input is empty.

props.name: maxRows
props.description: Maximum visible rows before the input scrolls. Use a lower value in compact layouts.

props.name: triggers
props.description: Trigger definitions for typeahead menus. Each trigger specifies a character (@ or /), a search source, and an onSelect handler that returns the token to insert. Set hasMultiWordQuery: true when suggestions contain spaces (people, topics): the query then runs to a line break or about 64 characters instead of ending at the first space. Per-trigger emptySearchText (ReactNode) is the message when the query matched nothing.

props.name: debounceMs
props.description: Debounce delay for async search sources to avoid excessive network requests.

props.name: hasHistory
props.description: Enable ArrowUp/Down to recall previously submitted messages.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label announced by screen readers.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the input. Use during streaming or when a prerequisite is unmet.

props.name: onPaste
props.description: Called when plain text is pasted. Return true after handling the text yourself; otherwise ChatComposerInput inserts it or applies paste-as-token behavior.

props.name: pasteAsToken
props.description: Paste-as-token behavior. By default, plain-text pastes over 200 characters become expandable tokens. Pass false to keep every text paste inline, or provide useChatPasteAsToken() to customize the conversion.

props.name: onFiles
props.description: Called when files are pasted or dropped onto the input. Use to handle attachments.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Called when the user presses Enter without Shift. The serialized value includes token placeholders.

props.name: onKeyDown
props.description: Key-down handler invoked before the built-in Enter/history behavior (after any open trigger menu). The seam for platform-specific keys: call event.preventDefault() to suppress the default submit (e.g. newline on a touch keyboard), or act on the event yourself to add behavior (e.g. submit on Cmd/Ctrl+Enter). IME composition is always respected; Enter never submits mid-composition.

props.name: enterKeyHint
props.description: What the Return key of a touch keyboard says (the native enterkeyhint). Enter sends the message, so it defaults to send and iOS shows its Send key. When onKeyDown makes Enter insert a line break on touch keyboards, pass enter so the key shows Return again.

ChatDictationButton.description: ChatDictationButton is a toggle button that starts and stops voice dictation inside a chat composer. It pairs with useChatDictation to show a microphone icon when idle and animated frequency bars when listening. Place it in the sendActions slot of ChatComposer.

practices.text: Place the dictation button in the sendActions slot of ChatComposer so it sits next to the send button where users expect voice input controls.
Pass an inputRef to useChatDictation so interim transcripts appear as ghost text in the composer input while the user speaks.
Enable hasSounds on useChatDictation to give users audio feedback when dictation starts and stops. This is especially helpful when the button's visual change is subtle.
Don't use the dictation button outside a chat composer context. It's designed for the composer's send-action layout, not as a standalone recording control.
Don't forget to handle the unsupported case. The button hides itself by default when the browser lacks SpeechRecognition, but you should still design the composer to work without it.

props.name: dictation
props.description: The return value from useChatDictation or useSpeechRecognition. Controls all button state: listening, volume, bands, and toggle.

props.name: size
props.description: Button size. Matches ChatComposer density.

props.name: isHiddenWhenUnsupported
props.description: When true, renders nothing if the browser does not support SpeechRecognition. When false, keeps the button visible but disabled.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label override. Defaults to "Start dictation" or "Stop dictation" based on state.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

ChatLayout.description: ChatLayout is the layout shell for full-page chat interfaces. It renders messages in normal page flow and docks the composer to the bottom with a frosted glass blur layer. Set the density prop to control spacing; it defaults to balanced. Use it to wrap ChatMessageList and ChatComposer for a complete chat experience with built-in auto-scroll and a scroll-to-bottom button.

practices.text: Pass ChatMessageList as children and ChatComposer as the composer prop for a complete chat interface.
Provide an emptyState so new conversations show a prompt instead of a blank screen.
Use scrollRef when the chat is embedded in a page where a parent element handles scrolling.

Give a full-page ChatLayout a container 100dvh tall, not 100vh: where a phone browser's toolbar collapses, 100vh is the viewport with the toolbar hidden, so the composer would start below the screen's edge.
Markdown prose keeps its 680px measure, while code blocks and tables span the message column. To give a reply one right edge, pass contentWidth="100%" to its Markdown.
Don't apply a fixed height on the layout; let it fill its container with flex: 1.
Don't render multiple ChatLayout instances in the same scroll container; each expects to own its scroll context.

props.name: children
props.description: Message content: typically ChatMessageList. Flows naturally in the page and scrolls with the container.

props.name: composer
props.description: Composer element: typically ChatComposer. Fixed to the bottom with a frosted glass dock.

props.name: emptyState
props.description: Content shown when children is empty. Centered vertically in the message area.

props.name: scrollButton
props.description: Scroll-to-bottom button rendered above the composer. Defaults to ChatLayoutScrollButton with auto-scroll integration. Pass null to hide.

props.name: scrollRef
props.description: External scroll container ref. When provided, auto-scroll and scroll-to-bottom target this element instead of the layout root. Use when the chat is embedded in a page where a parent element or the document body scrolls.

props.name: density
props.description: Visual density: controls dock padding, message-area max-width and inline padding, and the height of the frosted glass blur layer.

props.name: isVisible
props.description: Whether the button is visible. Bind to a scroll-position check so the button only appears when the user has scrolled up.

props.name: label
props.description: Optional label that expands the button (e.g. "New messages"). Use to signal unread content below the fold.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler: typically scrolls to bottom and dismisses the new message indicator.

props.name: sender
props.description: Who sent this message: controls alignment and layout.

props.name: children
props.description: Free-form content: bubbles, asset lists, tool calls, images. Custom (non-bubble) children render flush with the message edge; wrap them in a ghost ChatMessageBubble to align them with the bubble text column.

props.name: avatar
props.description: Avatar element rendered beside the message. Typically Avatar. `null`, booleans, and empty strings create no slot; any other content that renders nothing collapses its slot.

props.name: name
props.description: Sender name rendered above the message body; it labels the message. `null`, booleans, and empty strings create no slot, and any other content that renders nothing collapses its slot; either way the message is labelled by the translated sender fallback. Use when the first child is raw content (not a bubble). If the first child is a bubble, put the name on the bubble's `name` prop instead.

props.name: metadata
props.description: Metadata rendered below the message body. `null`, booleans, and empty strings create no slot; any other content that renders nothing collapses its slot. Use when the last child is raw content (not a bubble). If the last child is a bubble, put metadata on the bubble's `metadata` prop instead.

props.name: density
props.description: Visual density. Inherited from list context if not set.

props.name: children
props.description: Bubble content: text, Markdown, or any ReactNode.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual variant. 'filled' renders sender-colored background (default). 'ghost' renders transparent background but keeps padding for alignment.

props.name: name
props.description: Sender name rendered above the bubble, aligned with bubble text padding. Use on the first bubble in a message. Non-rendering scalar values (null, undefined, booleans, and the empty string) omit the aligned wrapper; numeric 0 remains aligned. If the first content is raw (no bubble), use ChatMessage's `name` prop instead.

props.name: metadata
props.description: Metadata content rendered below the bubble, aligned with bubble text padding. Use on the last bubble in a message. Non-rendering scalar values (null, undefined, booleans, and the empty string) omit the aligned wrapper; numeric 0 remains aligned. If the last content is raw (no bubble), use ChatMessage's `metadata` prop instead.

props.name: group
props.description: Position within a multi-bubble group. Controls corner radius reduction on the sender side. Leave unset for standalone bubbles (full radius).

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the bubble (number = pixels, string = used as-is). When set, replaces the default max(80%, 280px) width cap. Combine with variant="ghost" to let custom content (an artifact card, attachments) span the full message column.

props.name: children
props.description: Message elements: typically ChatMessage or ChatSystemMessage.

props.name: emptyState
props.description: Content shown when the list has no messages.

props.name: scrollToTopAction
props.description: Async action fired when user scrolls to top. Use for loading older messages. Wrapped in useTransition: shows a spinner at the top while pending.

props.name: density
props.description: Visual density: flows to child messages via context.

props.name: gap
props.description: Gap between top-level message rows. Defaults to the selected density; override for LLM event streams or independent rows that need different spacing from density.

props.name: align
props.description: Vertical alignment when the list is shorter than its container. 'bottom' fills free space with a spacer so short conversations sit above the composer; 'top' omits the spacer so messages start at the top. Only affects a non-full list; overflowing lists scroll identically, preserving auto-scroll-to-bottom.

props.name: isStreaming
props.description: Whether an assistant message is actively streaming. Marks the log aria-busy so screen readers wait and announce the completed message once instead of re-announcing partial text on every token.

ChatMessageMetadata.description: Place ChatMessageMetadata below a message or in the last ChatMessageBubble metadata slot to show a timestamp, footer content, and optional delivery status. Non-rendering scalar slots (booleans and empty strings) create no separator; numeric zero remains visible. Composite React content remains caller-owned.

practices.text: Put metadata in the last bubble metadata slot when the message uses bubbles, so it follows the bubble content.
Pass timestamp and footer content independently; separators are omitted for non-rendering scalar slots. Composite React nodes are used as supplied.
Do not supply footer actions without their own accessible names and interaction behavior; the metadata row does not own those controls.
Do not put the same metadata on both a bubble and its enclosing message.

props.name: timestamp
props.description: Timestamp content: a string or Timestamp component.

props.name: footer
props.description: Footer content: model info, reaction buttons, copy button.

props.name: status
props.description: Message delivery status. Shows icon + label.

ChatSendButton.description: Use ChatSendButton as ChatComposer’s send control when the action should switch between sending and stopping. Inside ChatComposer it reads readiness, streaming state, and action callbacks from context; standalone usage supplies those values explicitly.

practices.text: Place ChatSendButton inside ChatComposer when its readiness and send or stop lifecycle should follow composer context.
For standalone use, provide the state and matching onSend or onStop callback explicitly.
Keep the translated Send or Stop accessible name intact when supplying custom icon artwork; the icon is decorative and must not be the only name source.
Do not render the stop state without a working onStop callback from props or ChatComposer context.
Do not expect isDisabled to disable the stop action; it applies only to the send state.

props.name: isStopShown
props.description: Whether the stop button is shown. Defaults to context value.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the send button is disabled. Defaults to !canSend from context.

props.name: onSend
props.description: Called when the user clicks send. Defaults to context onSubmit.

props.name: onStop
props.description: Called when the user clicks stop during streaming. Defaults to context onStop.

props.name: sendIcon
props.description: Custom icon for the send state. Defaults to arrowUp from icon registry.

props.name: stopIcon
props.description: Custom icon for the stop state. Defaults to stop from icon registry.

props.name: size
props.description: Button size.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

ChatSystemMessage.description: Use ChatSystemMessage for concise, non-sender content inside a chat transcript. Choose the default variant for factual status notices and the divider variant for date or section breaks. Long default content wraps within the available width. It carries no live role: inside a ChatMessageList, the log announces new notices. The divider branch includes a labelled separator.

practices.text: Keep the visible message concise and self-contained so it remains understandable without an icon.
Use the divider variant for temporal or section boundaries and the default variant for factual status notices.
Use ChatSystemMessage for sender-authored content; use ChatMessage and ChatMessageBubble instead.
Use caller-provided icon artwork as the only source of meaning; the visible message must carry the same information.

props.name: children
props.description: System message content: factual text or React content such as a date, join/leave notice, or status change. Long default content wraps within the available width.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual variant. 'default' renders centered text. 'divider' adds horizontal lines on each side via Divider: use for date separators and section breaks.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional caller-provided icon content. Rendered before the message in the default variant; the divider variant currently does not render it. Wrap in Icon for consistent sizing.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

ChatTokenizedText.description: Use ChatTokenizedText inside a chat message when stored plain text contains serialized token values that should be projected as inline badges or caller-rendered token content. Unmatched text is preserved exactly and empty token values are ignored so rendering always finishes.

practices.text: Reuse the same token definitions for composer insertion and message rendering so serialized values and visible labels stay aligned.
Use non-empty, stable serialized values so every definition identifies real message text.
Use token labels as a substitute for the surrounding message text; the complete message must remain understandable in reading order.
Put component-owned interaction or accessibility behavior inside a custom token renderer; custom token content remains caller owned.

props.name: children
props.description: The plain text message containing serialized token values. Patterns matching a token's value are replaced with inline token content.

props.name: tokens
props.description: Token definitions using the same type as composer input. Each non-empty value is matched literally. Empty values are ignored. Structured tokens render a Badge, while custom tokens render caller content.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the root text wrapper. Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

ChatToolCalls.description: ChatToolCalls displays tool or function call invocations from an LLM response. Pass an array of calls and the component handles the rest: a single call renders inline, while multiple calls collapse into a summary with the latest call visible at the surface. Use it anywhere an AI agent shows what actions it took.

practices.text: Include a target string on every call so the user can see what the tool acted on: a file path, a shell command, or a search query.
Show a duration on completed calls so users can judge which tools are slow and understand why a response took time.
Provide a group label when the automatic count does not explain what the calls represent.
Provide resultDetail with a code block for calls that produce output (diffs for edits, terminal output for shell commands) so users can inspect results inline.
Set a unique key on each call item when streaming so React can animate additions without re-mounting completed rows.
Don't omit the status field. Without it the call defaults to complete, which is misleading for calls that are still running or have failed.
Don't display tool calls outside a chat message context; they are designed to sit inside an assistant message, not as standalone UI.
Don't use custom wrappers around individual calls; the component handles single vs. grouped layout automatically based on the array length.

props.name: calls
props.description: Array of tool call data. Each item has name, status, target, duration, node, additions, deletions, stats, errorMessage, resultDetail, key, and data. status is one of 'pending', 'running', 'complete', or 'error' (defaults to 'complete').

props.name: label
props.description: Custom summary label shown for an expanded group. The translated call count is used when omitted.

props.name: isExpanded
props.description: Controlled expanded state for the group.

props.name: defaultIsExpanded
props.description: Default expanded state when uncontrolled.

props.name: onExpandedChange
props.description: Callback fired when the expanded state changes.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

CheckboxInput.description: CheckboxInput toggles a single on/off value. Use it for settings like "Enable notifications", terms acceptance, or opt-in choices. For multiple checkboxes in a group, use CheckboxList instead.

practices.text: Always provide a visible label so the user knows what they are toggling. Use isLabelHidden only when surrounding context makes it obvious.
Add a description for choices that need extra context, like explaining what "Share usage data" actually shares.
Use the indeterminate state for "select all" checkboxes when only some items in a group are selected.
Use a checkbox for mutually exclusive choices; use RadioList when only one option can be selected.
Use a checkbox for actions that take effect immediately; use a toggle switch or button instead.
Wrap a disabled checkbox in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the underlying <input> element.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the checkbox (always rendered for accessibility).

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Whether to visually hide the label (still accessible to screen readers).

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed below the label.

props.name: value
props.description: Whether the checkbox is checked, unchecked, or indeterminate.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the checkbox state changes.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action on change. Fires after onChange if not prevented. Shows loading spinner while pending.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Whether the checkbox is in a loading state. Shows spinner and prevents interaction.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the checkbox is disabled.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: The HTML name attribute for the underlying checkbox input, useful for form submissions (submits "on" when checked).

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the checkbox is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the checkbox focusable via aria-disabled (toggling stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled CheckboxInput in Tooltip. Disabled controls swallow the hover events an external Tooltip needs.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: Whether the checkbox is read-only. Displays the current state at full opacity but prevents interaction. Unlike `isDisabled`, read-only checkboxes are not visually dimmed.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Whether the field is optional. Mutually exclusive with isRequired.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Whether the checkbox is required. Mutually exclusive with isOptional.

props.name: size
props.description: The size of the checkbox. sm for compact layouts, md for default. Under a coarse pointer a labelled checkbox’s target grows toward 44 px through an invisible hit area. It never shrinks below the row and stops at half the gap to a closer neighbour; nothing changes size.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Callback fired when the checkbox receives focus.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Callback fired when the checkbox loses focus.

props.name: labelIcon
props.description: Semantic icon name or custom content displayed before the label text. See `astryx docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator. Displays a colored message box below the checkbox and sets aria-invalid for errors.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

CheckboxList.description: CheckboxList shows a small group of checkboxes so users can turn several options on or off at once. Place it in settings pages, filter panels, or forms where every choice should be visible without scrolling. For a single standalone checkbox (like "I agree to the terms"), use CheckboxInput instead. If only one option can be picked, use RadioList. If the list is long enough to need searching or scrolling, use MultiSelector instead.

practices.text: Keep the list short: three to seven options is the sweet spot. Beyond that, switch to MultiSelector which adds search and scrolling.
Turn on dividers (hasDividers) when items have helper text underneath; without them the labels and descriptions blur together.
Write a group label that says what the choices represent: "Export formats" tells users more than "Options".
Show a CheckboxList when the user can only pick one thing; that is what RadioList is for.
Put buttons or links inside the trailing slot (endContent); the whole row is already tappable, so a nested button creates two competing click targets.
Wrap a disabled CheckboxList in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the checkbox group (always rendered for accessibility).

props.name: children
props.description: CheckboxListItem elements.

props.name: value
props.description: The currently selected values (collection mode).

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the selected values change.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action on change with optimistic updates. While the promise is pending, the toggled item shows a spinner inside its checkbox and is marked aria-busy.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Whether to visually hide the label.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed below the label.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Whether the group is optional. Shows the optional indicator after the group label, unless a surrounding FormLayout already makes fields optional by default.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Whether the group needs at least one checked box. Shows the required indicator after the group label by the same rules as every input field. While no box is checked, the browser blocks submit and moves focus to the first box that is neither disabled nor read-only, with its own message. A disabled or read-only group requires nothing. Show your own error text through status. Mutually exclusive with isOptional.

props.name: density
props.description: Spacing density for list items.

props.name: hasDividers
props.description: Whether to show dividers between items.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether all checkbox items are disabled.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the group is disabled. Applies to the whole-group disabled state (isDisabled), not per item. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the checkboxes focusable via aria-disabled (toggling stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled CheckboxList in Tooltip. Disabled controls swallow the hover events an external Tooltip needs.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: Whether all checkbox items are read-only. Displays the current state at full opacity but prevents interaction. Unlike isDisabled, read-only checkboxes are not visually dimmed.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator ({ type, message }).

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the element that paints the border and background and holds icons and end controls. Never the native input.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Class name for the visual control box.

props.name: controlStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the visual control box.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary text label for the item. Rich labels may contain links or buttons, which keep their own behavior without toggling the item. A ReactNode label names the checkbox from its visible text; pass aria-label only when that text is absent, or include all visible label words in the override.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Plain-text accessible name for the checkbox, replacing the one derived from label. Applied to the checkbox control. Use it when a rich label has no visible text; otherwise the value must retain every visible label word.

props.name: value
props.description: Identity key. Required when the parent CheckboxList has a value array; the item throws without it there.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary content below the label. String or ReactNode. Exposed as the checkbox's accessible description through aria-describedby, so assistive technology can tell it is the explanation for that choice.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content rendered after the label area.

props.name: align
props.description: Vertical alignment of the start and end content against the label, passed through to Item unchanged. `first-line` keeps a small mark (a checkbox) level with the first line of a wrapped label. See Item.align.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether this individual item is disabled.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Whether this item is loading. Shows a spinner inside the checkbox and blocks interaction on this item. In collection mode, the toggled item also shows this automatically while the parent changeAction is pending.

props.name: isChecked
props.description: Direct checked state in standalone mode: inside List, or inside a CheckboxList without value (for example, a select-all item). Ignored when the parent CheckboxList has a value array.

props.name: onCheck
props.description: Direct check handler in standalone mode: inside List, or inside a CheckboxList without value. Ignored when the parent CheckboxList has a value array; that list's onChange receives the change.

Citation.description: Citations display inline references to external sources. Use them to attribute information within AI-generated responses, articles, or anywhere provenance and source links are needed.

practices.text: Use the label variant when the source title adds meaningful context for the reader.
Use the number variant for compact inline references within body text, like footnotes.
Mix label and number variants in the same paragraph. Pick one style per context for visual consistency.

props.name: source
props.description: The citation source object containing title, url, an optional image src, and an optional icon node. The url follows the shared navigation rule described on the Link `href` prop; rejected destinations leave the citation visible without navigation. Image src uses separate resource handling.

props.name: number
props.description: The display index for this citation.

props.name: variant
props.description: Display style: a label chip showing the source title or a compact numbered badge.

Code.description: Code marks short inline references such as function names, variables, file paths, and command-line flags. Use CodeBlock for standalone or multi-line snippets.

practices.text: Use Code for short technical terms inside prose, such as a function name, prop, file path, or command-line flag.
Set size to 'inherit' when inline code should match the surrounding text size and line height.
Use Code for multi-line or standalone snippets. Use CodeBlock instead so readers get appropriate block formatting and syntax support.
Use Code as an interactive copy or navigation control. Pair it with the appropriate Button or Link when an action is required.

props.name: children
props.description: The inline code content.

props.name: color
props.description: Text color. Use 'inherit' to take the surrounding text color.

props.name: size
props.description: Set to 'inherit' to take the surrounding font size and line height. Omit it to use the code type-scale size.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the semantic code element.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the root element. Prefer xstyle for StyleX-optimized styling.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

CodeBlock.description: CodeBlock renders syntax-highlighted code with line numbers, a copy button, and optional collapsible sections. Use CodeBlock for multi-line snippets like source files, terminal commands, and configuration examples. Use Code for inline references to function names, variables, or CLI flags within body text.

practices.text: Set the language prop to match the code content so syntax highlighting is accurate. Use "plaintext" when the language is unknown.
Add a title when the code represents a file. It gives readers context and appears in the header bar alongside the copy button.
Use Code for short inline references like function names or CLI flags, and CodeBlock for standalone multi-line snippets.
Enable line numbers on short snippets (under 5 lines) where they add clutter without helping navigation.
Nest a code block inside a scrollable container. Use the maxHeight prop instead, which handles overflow natively.

props.name: code
props.description: The code string to display.

props.name: language
props.description: Language for syntax highlighting. A string selects a built-in: ts, js, tsx, jsx, json, html, xml, svg, css, scss, less, python, bash/sh/zsh/shell, php, hack, yaml, markdown, c, cpp (c++, cc, cxx, hpp, hh), sql, rust, kotlin, swift, go. Any other language is a value you import on its own and pass here: graphql, java, thrift, objectiveC, toml, powershell, ruby, lua, dockerfile from @astryxdesign/core/CodeBlock/languages/<path> (e.g. languages/graphql, languages/objective-c), or your own made with createCodeLanguage({name, identifiers, tokenize}). A value labels with its name and reflects its first identifier as data-language. Use "plaintext" to disable.

props.name: title
props.description: Filename or label shown in the header bar.

props.name: hasLanguageLabel
props.description: Show the language name in the header bar. Hidden when language is "plaintext".

props.name: hasLineNumbers
props.description: Show a line number gutter.

props.name: startLineNumber
props.description: First line number shown in the gutter. The gutter shows file coordinates (startLineNumber + index) so a code excerpt reads with its real line numbers. highlightLines uses the same file coordinates. Values below 1 clamp to 1.

props.name: highlightLines
props.description: 1-indexed line numbers to highlight, in the same file coordinates as the gutter (see startLineNumber). Out-of-range entries render no highlight.

props.name: isDiff
props.description: Render the code as a unified diff over `language`: lines starting with + are added, - removed, @@ is a hunk header (a `--- `/`+++ ` file-header pair directly before one is a header too), anything else is context. The language label reads `diff` or `<language> diff`. The glyph sits in its own column and the rest of each line keeps syntax highlighting; copy returns the exact source. Markdown ```diff and ```diff-<lang> fences set this.

props.name: hasCopyButton
props.description: Show a copy-to-clipboard button.

props.name: onCopy
props.description: Callback after the code is copied.

props.name: onCopyError
props.description: Called once with the rejection when the clipboard write fails. The copy button shows a cross and is named and announced as "Failed to copy value to clipboard."; the error is not shown.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Your own controls, shown just before Copy: in the header when the block has one, otherwise beside the code in the top inline-end corner, never over it. It never creates a header and never collapses the block. Ghost sm IconButtons match Copy’s size and variant.

props.name: isWrapped
props.description: Wrap long lines instead of enabling horizontal scroll.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Max height before the block scrolls vertically.

props.name: size
props.description: Text size variant.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the code block. Any CSS width value. 'fit-content' (default) shrinks to longest line. '100%' fills parent width.

props.name: container
props.description: Container presentation style. 'card' (default): border and radius with the muted syntax background for a standalone card look. 'section': no border or radius and a transparent background so the block blends into the card or panel it's embedded in.

props.name: tokenizer
props.type: (code: string, language: string) => Array<{type: string; start: number; end: number}>
props.description: Deprecated: pass language={createCodeLanguage({name, identifiers, tokenize})} with this same function instead. Still works exactly as released and wins over the language; astryx upgrade rewrites static uses.

props.name: syntaxTheme
props.description: Per-instance syntax theme override. Shorthand for wrapping the block in <SyntaxTheme theme={...}>. Accepts a preset from @astryxdesign/core/theme/syntax or a theme created with defineSyntaxTheme(). Defaults to the nearest SyntaxTheme ancestor or the theme-level syntax colors.

props.name: highlightMode
props.description: Syntax highlighting rendering mode.

props.name: isCollapsible
props.description: Allow collapsing the code body into just the header bar. Starts expanded; a visible header becomes clickable when the code exceeds collapsibleThreshold lines. Headerless blocks never collapse, and removing the header expands a previously collapsed block.

props.name: collapsibleThreshold
props.description: Minimum number of lines before the collapse toggle appears. Below this threshold the code block renders normally even when isCollapsible is true.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the root code-block element.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles. Prefer xstyle for StyleX-optimized styling.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

Collapsible.description: Collapsible hides and reveals content behind a trigger button. Use it in settings panels, FAQ pages, or detail views to keep the page scannable while letting users drill into sections they care about. Wrap multiple collapsibles in CollapsibleGroup for accordion behavior. For custom collapsible components, use the `useCollapsible` hook directly (`astryx hook useCollapsible`).

practices.text: Give every trigger a meaningful accessible name. Visible text usually supplies it; custom trigger content should include VisuallyHidden text when its visuals do not.
Use hasDividers on CollapsibleGroup for FAQ-style lists: built-in row hairlines with themed border tokens, no hand-rolled borders.
Wrap each Collapsible in an Card for visual separation in accordion layouts, or use CollapsibleGroup's hasDividers for flat lists; don't combine both.
Use CollapsibleGroup with type="single" for settings or FAQ pages where only one section should be open at a time.
Use type="multiple" when users need to compare content across sections, like feature lists or pricing tiers.
Start sections open (defaultIsOpen) when the content is likely needed on first view; don't make users click to see essential info.
Hide critical or required content behind a collapsible; users may not discover it.
Nest collapsibles more than two levels deep; it makes content hard to find and navigate.
Use a collapsible for a single short paragraph; just show the text directly instead.

props.name: trigger
props.description: Content shown in the trigger area (always visible).

props.name: children
props.description: Content that collapses and expands.

props.name: defaultIsOpen
props.description: Default open state for standalone uncontrolled usage. Ignored when value binds the item to a surrounding CollapsibleGroup.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Controlled open state for standalone usage. Ignored when value binds the item to a surrounding CollapsibleGroup.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disable the item so its trigger can't be toggled (dimmed, aria-disabled, and out of the tab order). Doesn't collapse an already-open item.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback invoked when standalone open state changes. A surrounding CollapsibleGroup owns grouped state and calls its onChange instead.

props.name: chevronPosition
props.description: Logical position of Collapsible's disclosure chevron. `end` (default) follows the label, pointing down when collapsed and up when expanded. `start` precedes the label, pointing inward toward content when collapsed (mirrored under RTL) and down when expanded. Inside a CollapsibleGroup this defaults to the group's chevronPosition.

props.name: value
props.description: Identifier used for group coordination. When set inside a CollapsibleGroup, the group owns open state and its onChange is the notification callback.

props.name: animatedLayout
props.description: The handle from useAnimatedLayout({containerRef}). With it, opening and closing glides the content after this Collapsible, up to that container, on one shared motion role instead of jumping, and the revealed content and the chevron move on the same motion. Without it, the content after it takes its place at once.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the root collapsible element.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles. Prefer xstyle for StyleX-optimized styling.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

props.name: type
props.description: Whether one or many items can be open simultaneously.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Default open item(s) for uncontrolled usage. Use a string for single mode and an array for multiple mode.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled open item(s).

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback invoked when the set of open items changes.

props.name: hasDividers
props.description: Whether to draw hairline dividers between the group's items. When set, the group renders a wrapper div and items default to 'balanced' density. Pair with bare Collapsible children; Card-wrapped items provide their own separation.

props.name: density
props.description: Row density controlling trigger and content block padding on the group's items. Defaults to 'balanced' when dividers are shown; otherwise items keep their default unpadded look.

props.name: chevronPosition
props.description: Logical position shared by the group's direct Collapsible items. `end` is the default trailing indicator; `start` is a leading disclosure arrow that points inward when collapsed (mirrored under RTL) and down when expanded. An individual Collapsible can still override it.

props.name: children
props.description: Collapsible instances to coordinate.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the group wrapper when hasDividers renders one.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the group wrapper when hasDividers renders one. Must be a stylex.create() value.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name for the group wrapper when hasDividers renders one. Prefer xstyle for styling.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the group wrapper when hasDividers renders one. Prefer xstyle for StyleX-optimized styling.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector forwarded to the group wrapper when hasDividers renders one.

CommandPalette.description: CommandPalette is a searchable dialog for quick access to commands, navigation, and actions. Use it as a keyboard-driven launcher powered by SearchSource for filtering and selection.

practices.text: Provide a searchSource with bootstrap results so users see useful options before typing.
Use auxiliaryData.group on items to automatically organize results into labeled sections.
Provide a specific label when more than one command palette can appear in the same product surface.
Keep renderItem content non-interactive; each rendered row is one option, so buttons and links cannot be nested inside it.
Intercept query-field keyboard events without preserving active IME composition and native Home/End caret movement.
Use CommandPalette for simple dropdowns or menus; use Menu or Selector for inline selections.
Add too many groups or items; curate results to keep the palette fast and scannable.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Whether the command palette dialog is visible.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the palette visibility changes.

props.name: searchSource
props.description: Search source providing items via search(query) and bootstrap(). Use createStaticSource for static lists.

props.name: input
props.description: Input slot. Defaults to CommandPaletteInput with standard behavior.

props.name: footer
props.description: Footer slot. Defaults to CommandPaletteFooter showing keyboard hints.

props.name: renderItem
props.description: Per-item render function for non-interactive presentation content such as labels, icons, descriptions, and shortcut hints. Do not return buttons or links inside the option. Auto-grouping by auxiliaryData.group is preserved. When omitted, renders label text.

props.name: emptySearchText
props.description: Content shown when a search query returns no results.

props.name: emptyBootstrapText
props.description: Content shown when there is no search query and bootstrap() returns nothing.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled selected value for picker mode.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called when the selected value changes in picker mode.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the command palette dialog.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the dialog.

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: Maximum height of the dialog.

props.name: isInline
props.description: Renders command palette content inline without modal behavior. Automatically disables input auto-focus and initial highlighted-item auto-scroll. For documentation previews and showcases only.

props.name: children
props.description: Message or content to display.

CommandPaletteFooter.description: CommandPalette renders CommandPaletteFooter automatically. Pass a CommandPaletteFooter to the footer slot only when replacing the default guidance.

props.name: children
props.description: Custom footer content. When omitted, renders default keyboard hints via Kbd.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

props.name: heading
props.description: Group heading text.

props.name: children
props.description: CommandPaletteItem children.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

CommandPaletteInput.description: Use CommandPaletteInput inside CommandPalette for a popup-backed command query, or as an independent search field when no result popup is present.

practices.text: Pass a concise label that identifies what can be searched when "Search commands" does not describe it; the placeholder is never the field's name.
Use endContent for short supporting controls or shortcut hints at the trailing edge.
Override combobox role or popup state. CommandPaletteInput owns those semantics when connected to CommandPalette.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text for the input.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the query field, announced by screen readers. Defaults to the translated "Search commands"; the placeholder is never used as the name.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Auto-focus the input when mounted. Automatically disabled when inside an inline command palette.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content rendered at the trailing end of the input, after the spinner. Use for clear buttons or keyboard shortcut hints.

props.name: value
props.description: Search value. When omitted inside CommandPalette, reads from context.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called when search value changes. When omitted inside CommandPalette, writes to context.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

CommandPaletteItem.description: Use CommandPaletteItem for one non-interactive result row inside CommandPaletteList or CommandPaletteGroup. CommandPalette owns the composite keyboard model; standalone items expose only their explicit visual state and pointer activation.

practices.text: Keep each value unique within the result list so highlight, active-descendant identity, and selection resolve to the same item.

Inside CommandPalette, each item is an option in the listbox popup of the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern: keyboard focus stays in the query field, arrow keys move the highlight through aria-activedescendant, and Enter selects the highlighted item.

Nest buttons, links, or other interactive controls inside an item. Option semantics make descendants presentational, so use non-interactive content such as icons, descriptions, and shortcut hints, and activate the option itself.
Treat isHighlighted as selection. Highlight is the active keyboard result; isSelected represents the chosen value.

props.name: value
props.description: Unique value used for item identity, highlight lookup, and selection.

props.name: children
props.description: Non-interactive item content such as a label, icon, description, or keyboard shortcut.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called after this item is activated by pointer. Keyboard selection in CommandPalette reports through CommandPalette onValueChange.

props.name: isHighlighted
props.description: Whether this item is the active keyboard result. Derived from context when omitted inside CommandPalette.

props.name: isSelected
props.description: Whether this item represents the selected value in picker mode. Derived from the CommandPalette value when omitted inside CommandPalette.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the item is unavailable and suppresses pointer activation.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

props.name: children
props.description: Items, groups, and empty states.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the listbox.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

ContextMenu.description: A right-click context menu that appears at the cursor position. Use to provide contextual actions for specific elements or regions without cluttering the UI with visible buttons.

practices.text: Keep menu items concise and action-oriented; users expect quick access to contextual actions.
Use sections and dividers to group related actions when the menu has many items.
Use `presentation="adaptive"` when right-click should remain cursor-positioned on desktop while long-press opens a reachable BottomSheet on compact touch devices.
Ensure all context menu actions are also accessible via other UI elements for keyboard-only users.
Keep a visible MoreMenu or equivalent trigger for important mobile actions; long-press must not be the only route.
Use a ContextMenu as the only way to access important actions; not all users know to right-click.
Place more than 10–12 items in a single menu without grouping them into sections.

props.name: children
props.description: The trigger area: right-click on this content to open the menu.

props.name: items
props.description: Data-driven menu entries. Pass exactly one of `items` or `menuContent`. Each entry is one of: an action item `{label, onClick?, icon?, isDisabled?, variant?, items?}` (nested `items` open a flyout in popover presentation and drill into a new view in bottom-sheet presentation; variant `"destructive"` renders it in the error color), a divider `{type: "divider"}`, or a section `{type: "section", title?, items: [...action items]}`.

props.name: menuContent

A DOM handler runs after DateInput's own handler for the same event and still receives events it handled (including ones it called preventDefault on), so it cannot cancel built-in behavior.
Provide clear labels and descriptions so users understand what date is expected.
Use min, max, and dateConstraints to restrict selectable dates to valid ranges.
Set min and max on a Buddhist or Minguo calendar field, so a Gregorian year typed by mistake shows an error instead of a date centuries away.
Use hasClear when the date is optional so the user can reset it.
Show a loading state with changeAction when the date triggers a server-side save.

On a fine pointer the field follows the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern with a dialog popup, as in the APG date picker combobox: ArrowDown or Alt+ArrowDown opens the calendar, and Escape closes it and returns focus to the field.

Use a DateInput for free-form text that does not represent a calendar date.
Hide the label without surrounding context that makes the field purpose obvious.

Wrap a disabled DateInput in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop instead, which ties the reason to the field.

DateTimeInput.description: DateTimeInput combines date and time selection in one field. With presentation="adaptive-native" (the default), mouse/trackpad devices use Astryx typed fields and popovers, while coarse-pointer devices use browser/OS date and time controls in the same two-segment field. presentation="native" uses both native controls on every pointer; presentation="adaptive-bottom-sheet" keeps Astryx's own surfaces — pointer fields on fine pointers and the coordinated Date/Time bottom sheet on coarse pointers; "popover" and "bottom-sheet" force one Astryx surface on every pointer. The closed segments stay side by side when at least 400px is available and wrap into full-width rows below 400px, independent of viewport width. Use it for scheduling, event creation, deadline setting, or any form field that needs a specific datetime.

A DOM handler runs after DateTimeInput's own handler for the same event and still receives events it handled (including ones it called preventDefault on), so it cannot cancel built-in behavior.

Use min and max to restrict selectable datetimes to valid ranges.
Set min and max on a Buddhist or Minguo calendar field, so a Gregorian year typed by mistake shows an error instead of a date centuries away.
Use hasClear when the datetime is optional so the user can reset it.

Leave hourFormat unset so the field follows the InternationalizationProvider locale's hour cycle (12-hour in en-US, 24-hour in en-GB or de-DE). Set it only when the field itself needs a fixed format, and carry a person's own 12/24-hour preference on the provider locale (e.g. 'en-US-u-hc-h23') rather than on each field.
Use DateTimeInput when only a date is needed; use DateInput instead.
Use DateTimeInput when only a time is needed; use TimeInput instead.
Hide the label without surrounding context that makes the field purpose obvious.
Wrap a disabled DateTimeInput in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop instead, which ties the reason to the field.

AlertDialog.description:
AlertDialog asks the user to confirm a destructive or irreversible action before it happens. Use it for things like deleting content, revoking access, or discarding unsaved changes.

It implements the WAI-ARIA APG [Alert Dialog pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alertdialog/): `role="alertdialog"`, a title linked by `aria-labelledby`, a consequence description linked by `aria-describedby`, focus moved into the dialog on open and returned to the trigger on close, and no dismissal by clicking outside. Escape cancels.

AlertDialog passes its requested width through to Dialog, which clamps the surface to the container and dynamic viewport with token gutters. Generic Dialog footers should wrap, but Dialog does not own action semantics or order; consumer composition controls that. AlertDialog owns its confirmation semantics: above 640px, actions render horizontally and may move onto another row; at 640px and below, the destructive action appears above Cancel and both buttons fill the footer width. Button labels retain their standard single-line behavior. The breakpoint follows available width, not pointer or hover capability. The body scrolls when block space is constrained.

The two actions are tracked as one group under every pointer, the way iOS tracks the actions of an alert: the action under the pointer highlights as soon as it is pressed, the highlight follows the pointer from one action to the other, and the release runs the action under it. Releasing off both actions runs nothing. The keyboard and assistive technology keep the click of each button.

For cases where you want to show an alert without managing open state, use the `useImperativeAlertDialog` hook: call `alert.show(options)` and render `alert.element` in your tree.

practices.text: Make the action button label specific: "Delete project" is better than "OK" or "Confirm".
Describe what will happen in the description so the user knows the consequences before confirming.
Keep the cancel button as the least-destructive focus target. On narrow screens the destructive action is visually and structurally above Cancel, but Cancel still receives initial focus.
Use concise, specific action labels. Above 640px, complete buttons may move onto another row; at 640px and below, the destructive action appears above Cancel and both buttons fill the footer width.
Use AlertDialog for non-destructive actions; use a standard Dialog instead.
Rely on color alone to signal danger; the action label itself should say what will happen.
Close the dialog from onAction before the work finishes; hold it open with isActionLoading and call onOpenChange(false) when the action settles.

props.description: Whether the dialog is open.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Visibility change callback.

props.name: title
props.description: Dialog title. Linked via aria-labelledby.

props.name: description
props.description: Consequence description. Linked via aria-describedby.

props.description: Action button label.

props.description: Action button variant.

props.name: isInline
props.description: Renders alert dialog content inline without modal behavior. For documentation previews and showcases only. Not being a modal, the inline path renders role="group" instead of role="alertdialog".

Dialog.description:
Dialog displays a modal overlay that blocks interaction with the page until the user responds. Use it for delete confirmations, edit forms, terms acceptance, or any decision that should not be skipped.

For cases where you want to show a dialog without managing open state, use the `useImperativeDialog` hook: call `dialog.show(content)` and render `dialog.element` in your tree.

practices.text: Choose the right purpose: info for dismissable content, form to prevent accidental backdrop dismissal, required when the user must respond.
Include a clear title in the header so users immediately understand what the dialog is asking.
Use purpose="form" for dialogs with inputs so the user can't accidentally lose data by clicking the backdrop.
Keep dialogs focused on a single task; if the content grows beyond what fits, consider a full page instead.
Use a dialog for simple messages that could be shown inline or as a toast notification.
Nest dialogs inside other dialogs; restructure the flow into steps within a single dialog instead.
Use the fullscreen variant for simple confirmations; it is meant for complex content like editors or long forms.

props.name: isOpen

props.description: Callback when dialog visibility changes.

props.description: Dialog content.

props.description: Preferred width of the dialog in pixels or any CSS value. Standard dialogs clamp to their container and the dynamic viewport with spacing-token gutters so narrow viewports keep content on screen.
