props.description: Maximum height of the dialog. Defaults to a dynamic viewport value so browser UI changes are reflected where supported.

props.name: position
props.description: Static position for the dialog; centered by default when omitted. Use logical `start`/`end` for inline offsets so positioned dialogs mirror correctly under RTL.

props.name: variant
props.description: Dialog variant: fullscreen expands to fill the entire viewport.

props.name: purpose
props.description: Controls dismissal behavior: required disables Escape and backdrop click; form disables backdrop click after interaction; info allows both.

props.name: padding
props.description: Internal padding of the dialog using the spacing scale step.

props.name: isInline
props.description: Renders dialog content inline without the <dialog> element, backdrop, or modal behavior. For documentation previews and showcases only.

DialogHeader.description: Use DialogHeader to give a dialog a labelled title area and optional close control.

props.name: title
props.description: Dialog title, rendered inside the focusable h2 (receives focus on open; its text content labels the dialog via aria-labelledby unless the Dialog has an explicit aria-label/aria-labelledby). Keep it inline, non-interactive, and non-empty.

props.name: subtitle
props.description: Subtitle below the title. Accepts inline content such as a Link; avoid block elements.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Close button callback (no button if omitted).

props.name: startContent
props.description: Content before the title (e.g., a back button).

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content after the title, before close button.

props.name: endContentEdgeCompensation
props.description: Selects compensation axes for the end-content slot. Omit to preserve automatic close-action compensation.

props.name: hasDivider
props.description: Adds border at the bottom edge.

Divider.description: A visual separator that divides content into distinct sections. Use to create clear boundaries between groups of related content, or to demarcate interactive regions within a layout.

practices.text: Use subtle dividers between related content sections and strong dividers for high-contrast boundaries.
Add a label to the divider when sections need a visible category heading.
Overuse dividers; rely on spacing and layout to separate content when possible.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Orientation of the divider.

props.name: label
props.description: Optional label centered on the divider. Numeric zero is preserved; null, booleans, and empty strings render no label.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual weight of the divider line.

props.name: isFullBleed
props.description: Extend the divider to container edges with negative margins.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

Drawer.description:
A side panel that floats above page content for inspectors and detail views: the "click a table row, see its details" pattern. Unlike a docked panel it overlays the layout instead of reflowing it. Works on desktop and touch: the width budget applies on desktop and the panel preserves a 56px page reveal below 640px without exceeding the width budget. Escape closes the drawer (unless purpose is required) and focus returns to the element that opened it. Entry/exit slide animation respects prefers-reduced-motion. On a phone or tablet (a coarse primary pointer), a tap or a drag that lands while the drawer is still sliding in reaches nothing (for a drawer without a scrim, only one on the panel: the page stays live), and the drawer finishes sliding in; keys and assistive technology stay live, and a mouse or a trackpad still clicks: at once when it was the last pointer used, otherwise once it moves. Stacking contract: sibling drawers stack last-opened on top, Escape closes only the topmost, and closing peels innermost-first; render them as siblings, never nested.

Like Dialog, the drawer is a container: its content area is inset by --spacing-4 (16px) by default, by the padding prop, or by a theme's padding on drawer. Compose the header, body, and footer the way Dialog does, with a Layout: DrawerHeader in the header slot (it shows a close button when you pass it onOpenChange, like DialogHeader), the body in LayoutContent, and actions in LayoutFooter. The Layout redistributes the inset to those regions so they line up on one content line, and the header is not inset twice. A lone Section child also escapes the inset. Drawer renders no close button of its own, so give every drawer a visible way to close, especially a non-modal one, which has no scrim to click. Put data-autofocus on the control that should receive focus on open.

Choosing a surface: use Dialog for a centered decision or short form, Drawer for full-height side detail that keeps the page in sight, BottomSheet for block-axis sheets on touch, and a docked panel (a layout column) when content should reflow the page instead of floating over it.

Theming: the panel is the single stable target (astryx-drawer, with data-side reflecting side), and the scrim is the panel's native ::backdrop. DrawerHeader exposes astryx-drawer-header targets for its row, slots, and close icon.

practices.text: Use for contextual detail views (row inspectors, entity details) where the user should keep the underlying list in sight.
Keep the caller as the source of truth: derive isOpen from selection state and clear the selection in onOpenChange.
Use hasScrim={false} for master-detail flows; non-modal drawers do not trap focus and the page behind stays interactive.
Keep the last-selected item rendered on close: children stay mounted during the exit animation, so nulling content mid-close blanks the panel while it slides out.
Give every drawer a visible close action, usually DrawerHeader with onOpenChange; a non-modal drawer has no scrim to click.
Use purpose="form" when a stray scrim click would discard unsaved input.
Use a Drawer for short confirmations or small forms; use Dialog or AlertDialog instead.
Reach for a Drawer when the content should push the page aside; a Drawer floats over content, so use a docked panel or layout column instead.
Use a Drawer as a bottom or top sheet; it is inline-axis only, so use BottomSheet for block-axis sheets.
Nest a Drawer inside another Drawer; render drawers as siblings; the last-opened stacks on top and Escape closes it first.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Whether the drawer is open. Fully controlled; pair with onOpenChange.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the drawer requests an open-state change. Escape and a scrim click call it with false as purpose allows; a DrawerHeader given the same callback calls it from its close button. The caller owns the open state. With sibling drawers open, Escape only closes the last-opened one.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the drawer. Required; the drawer has no built-in heading to derive a name from.

props.name: children
props.description: Drawer content, rendered inside a full-height scrollable area. Compose your own header/body/footer; an element with data-autofocus is focused on open. Children stay mounted during the exit animation; keep the last-selected item rendered instead of nulling content on close.

props.name: side
props.description: Edge the drawer slides from: 'end' is right in LTR (the inspector convention), 'start' is left. Inline axis only; for a bottom sheet use BottomSheet.

props.name: width
props.description: Desktop width budget. A number is pixels; a string is any CSS length ('50%', '32rem'). Below the 640px mobile breakpoint this remains the maximum while the drawer preserves a 56px reveal of the page behind.

props.name: experimental
props.description: Experimental options: anything in this object may change or be removed in a patch release, and omitting it keeps the stable behavior. isFullWidthOnMobile (default false) covers the full viewport width below the 640px mobile breakpoint instead of preserving the default 56px reveal of the page behind, which makes the drawer read as an overlay, not a navigation.

props.name: hasScrim
props.description: Modal scrim behind the drawer. true uses showModal() (top layer, focus trap, scroll lock; clicking the scrim closes unless purpose prevents it; modal only); false uses the manual Popover API for a non-modal top-layer overlay that does NOT trap focus and keeps the page behind interactive.

props.name: purpose
props.description: Configures implicit dismissal, matching Dialog. info: Escape and a scrim click close. form: Escape closes, a scrim click does not. required: neither closes (Escape is consumed) and a modal drawer is exposed as an alertdialog, so give its content a way out. A non-modal drawer has no scrim, so form and info behave the same.

props.name: padding
props.description: Internal padding of the drawer content using the spacing scale, matching Dialog. When omitted, uses the theme default for drawers: --spacing-4 (16px) unless the theme sets padding on drawer. Pass 0 for a full-bleed content area. A lone Section child escapes the padding, bleed children such as Table and Divider compensate against it, and a Layout picks it up for its regions. The content area's block-end edge adds the home-indicator safe area on top in every mode.

DrawerHeader.description: Compose DrawerHeader in the header slot of a Layout inside the Drawer, as DialogHeader is composed in Dialog, for a title row and, when you pass onOpenChange, a close button. The Layout keeps the header on the drawer inset instead of padding it twice. Drawer renders no close button of its own. Unlike DialogHeader it does not take focus on open (Drawer uses data-autofocus) and does not name the drawer (Drawer label does).

props.name: title
props.description: Drawer title, rendered as an h2. Keep it inline and non-interactive. It does not name the drawer; pass Drawer a label.

props.name: subtitle
props.description: Subtitle below the title. Accepts inline content such as a Link; avoid block elements.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Close button callback, called with false (no button if omitted). Pass the Drawer's own onOpenChange.

props.name: startContent
props.description: Content before the title (e.g., a back button).

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content after the title, before the close button.

props.name: endContentEdgeCompensation
props.description: Selects compensation axes for the end-content slot. Omit to preserve automatic close-action compensation.

props.name: hasDivider
props.description: Adds a border at the bottom edge. Defaults to the parent Layout's defaultHasDividers.

DropdownMenu.description: A dropdown menu that displays a list of actionable items in a popup triggered by a button. Use to present action options as a next step in a process, or to offer contextual actions without cluttering the interface. Like the menus of macOS and iOS, the row under the pointer when it is released is the row that acts, the highlight follows a held mouse or finger, a mouse opens it on press and can drag straight into it, and a finger held on the trigger opens it with the finger down.

practices.text: Keep menu items concise and action-oriented so users can scan options quickly.
Use sections and dividers to group related actions when the menu has many items.
For a short, flat action set, use presentation="bottom-sheet" when product policy calls for a modal touch surface.
Use presentation="adaptive" when the same short action set should remain anchored on pointer layouts and become a BottomSheet on compact coarse-pointer layouts.
For a hierarchy that cannot fit as adjacent flyouts on a compact touch surface, a product may explicitly use a drill-in interaction with a Back action.
Choose presentation explicitly in product code. A compact, coarse-pointer, hover-free media query is one useful policy, but DropdownMenu does not impose a universal device breakpoint.
When the content is no longer a short list of immediate actions, reevaluate the interaction and choose a component that matches the actual task; content traits alone do not determine the component.
Use a DropdownMenu for navigation; use a navigation component instead.
Place more than 10–12 items in a single menu without grouping them into sections.

props.name: button
props.description: Props for the trigger button (Button props except onClick). Mutually exclusive with `renderTrigger`.

props.name: renderTrigger
props.description: Render the control the menu hangs off — an IconButton, a chip, an avatar, a list row — instead of the built-in Button. Spread the given props onto it: they carry the press model (a mouse opens on press-down, a held finger opens with the finger down), the keyboard opens, the toggle click, and `aria-haspopup`/`aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`/`id`; the menu is then named by that control through `aria-labelledby`. Mutually exclusive with `button`.

props.name: items
props.description: Array of menu entries. Each entry is one of: an action item `{label, onClick?, href?, target?, rel?, icon?, description?, endContent?, isDisabled?, variant?, hasCloseOnSelect?, id?}` (`href` makes the row a real link, so a modified click keeps the browser's meaning; variant `"destructive"` renders it in the error color; `endContent` holds trailing content such as a keyboard-shortcut hint; `id` is the row's stable React key, needed only when the array reorders or filters), a divider `{type: "divider"}`, or a section `{type: "section", title?, id?, items: [...action items]}`.

props.name: presentation
props.description: Presentation surface for data-driven items. 'popover' stays anchored, 'bottom-sheet' always renders the actions in a modal BottomSheet, and 'adaptive' uses a BottomSheet on compact coarse-pointer layouts while remaining anchored elsewhere. Compound children currently support popover only. Omitted, the menu is anchored, and under a finger, on every device, the finger that opened it picks a row only after moving 10 px. Pass 'popover' to keep the pointer behavior on every device, the settle rule included.

props.name: isMenuOpen
props.description: Controlled open state for the menu. Mounting with true renders the menu open without moving focus into it; focus moves to the first item only when the menu opens after mount.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback fired when the open state changes.

props.name: menuWidth
props.description: Minimum width for the popover presentation. Length values may grow for content; intrinsic and CSS-wide keywords select the preferred inline size. Every form is capped to the available viewport space. Defaults to matching the trigger width up to that cap.

props.name: menuMaxHeight
props.description: Maximum height in pixels for the popover presentation, for a menu that must fit its rows. Lifts the default 300px cap; the viewport still bounds it.

props.name: header
props.description: Content above the rows and outside the menu itself — a filter field, a toggle. A menu holds only its rows, so a control that is not a row goes here or in `footer`, never among the rows. It keeps its own keys and presses. With a header or footer the popover is a modal dialog around the menu: Tab and Shift+Tab move through the header, the menu and the footer and wrap at either end, and Escape closes. The bottom sheet shows it above the actions.

props.name: footer
props.description: Content below the rows and outside the menu itself — a "Create" button. Tab from the menu moves into it, and Tab past its last control wraps to the start of the dialog (see `header`). The bottom sheet shows it below the actions.

props.name: placement
props.description: Popover placement relative to the trigger. Ignored by the bottom-sheet presentation. Logical: start/end resolve against the menu's own inherited direction (RTL mirrors).

props.name: alignment
props.description: Popover alignment along the placement axis. Ignored by the bottom-sheet presentation. Logical: start/end follow the menu's own inherited direction (RTL mirrors).

props.name: onClick
props.description: Callback fired for accepted trigger activation. The trailing click from the same press that light-dismissed the menu is ignored.

props.name: hasChevron
props.description: Whether to show a chevron icon on the trigger button. Set to false for icon-only triggers.

props.name: children
props.description: Compound-mode menu content: DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuDivider, DropdownMenuSubMenu (a flyout on a laptop, a drilled-in view with a Back row on a phone), and the selectable items. Mutually exclusive with `items`.

DropdownMenuCheckboxItem.description: An independently checkable option inside DropdownMenu. The row owns menuitemcheckbox semantics while the shared Indicator supplies decorative checkbox paint.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary label text identifying the item.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary description text displayed below the label.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon to display before the label. See `astryx docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: value
props.description: Whether the item is checked. Controlled; pair with onChange.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired with the next checked state when the item is toggled.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the item is disabled. A disabled item stays in the accessibility tree as disabled (aria-disabled), and the arrow keys and typeahead reach it so keyboard users find it. The pointer highlight skips it, and activation is blocked.

props.name: hasCloseOnSelect
props.description: Whether toggling the item closes the menu. Checkbox items default to staying open so several can be toggled in a single session.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the row root, the element carrying role="menuitemcheckbox". Register the row with an element-keyed observer or overlay.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content to render after the label and description, such as a keyboard shortcut hint or badge.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles applied after the menu spacing. Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

DropdownMenuGroup.description: Use DropdownMenuGroup to give related compound-menu rows one visible and programmatic name. Use an untitled group only when a separate name would not help people understand the rows.

practices.text: Use short, descriptive title content that explains what the grouped rows have in common.
Keep the title non-interactive so every available action remains in the menu arrow-key order.
Place buttons, links, fields, or other controls in title. Put them in DropdownMenu header or footer instead.
Wrap rows that do not form a meaningful set; a group adds structure only when its relationship helps users.

props.name: title
props.description: Non-interactive heading content shown above the rows and used as the group's accessible name. Omit for an unnamed group; place controls in DropdownMenu header or footer.

props.name: children
props.description: The grouped rows: DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuCheckboxItem, DropdownMenuRadioGroup, or DropdownMenuSubMenu.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles applied to the role="group" wrapper. Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name applied to the role="group" wrapper.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles applied to the role="group" wrapper.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the role="group" wrapper.

DropdownMenuItem.description: Use DropdownMenuItem inside DropdownMenu compound mode for one action or destination. Keep label, description, icon, and endContent non-interactive; controls belong in separate rows or the menu header/footer.

practices.text: Use href for a destination so LinkProvider, modified clicks, middle clicks, and browser link affordances remain available.
Use hasCloseOnSelect=false only when activation reports a result in place on the same row.
Put buttons, links, or other focusable controls inside label, description, or endContent. Each menu row is one interactive target.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon to display before the label. See `astryx docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary label text.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary description text displayed below the label.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Callback when the item is selected. A keyboard activation arrives as a synthesized click carrying the key's modifiers. On a row with `href` it runs before the browser navigates and is skipped for a modified click (⌘, Ctrl, Shift, Alt, middle button), which is left to the browser.

props.name: href
props.description: Address the row navigates to. The row then renders as a real anchor with role="menuitem" (through LinkProvider), so a modified click or a middle click keeps the browser's meaning — a new tab — instead of running onClick.

props.name: target
props.description: Link target. Only used with href.

props.name: rel
props.description: Link relationship. noopener noreferrer is added for target="_blank". Only used with href.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the row is unavailable. Disabled rows expose aria-disabled, remove link destinations, and suppress activation.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Non-interactive content rendered after the label and description.

props.name: hasCloseOnSelect
props.description: Whether activating the item closes the menu. Set false for an action that reports its result on the item itself.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual variant. 'destructive' renders the label, description, and icon in the error color for dangerous actions (e.g. Delete).

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the row root, the element carrying role="menuitem". Register the row with an element-keyed observer or overlay.

DropdownMenuRadioGroup.description: Use DropdownMenuRadioGroup inside compound-mode DropdownMenu when several commands represent one mutually exclusive choice. Keep value in caller state, provide a concise accessible label, and render each choice as DropdownMenuRadioItem.

practices.text: Keep value controlled and update it from onChange so checked state follows caller data.
Provide a concise label even when aria-labelledby points to visible text; label remains required and supplies the aria-label fallback.
Set hasCloseOnSelect=false only when the menu must stay open to show another selection or an in-place result.
Place buttons, links, checkboxes, or arbitrary menu rows inside the radio group.
Add a second key handler or roving-focus model; DropdownMenu owns keyboard navigation.

props.name: value
props.description: The currently selected value in the group. Pass undefined when nothing is selected yet.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the selected value changes.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the group, applied as aria-label so screen readers announce the radios as a named set, e.g. "Sort by". Required even when aria-labelledby (via base props) points to visible text; that visible reference becomes the computed name while label remains the fallback.

props.name: hasCloseOnSelect
props.description: Whether selecting a value closes the menu. Radio items default to closing on selection (a single-choice commit).

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the role="group" root.

props.name: children
props.description: The DropdownMenuRadioItems that make up the group.

props.name: value
props.description: The value this item represents within its group. The group's value matches against this to determine the checked state.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary label text identifying the option.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary description text displayed below the label.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon to display before the label. See `astryx docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether this individual radio item is disabled. A disabled item stays in the accessibility tree as disabled (aria-disabled), and the arrow keys and typeahead reach it so keyboard users find it. The pointer highlight skips it, and selection is blocked.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content to render after the label and description, such as a badge or metadata.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the row root, the element carrying role="menuitemradio". Register the row with an element-keyed observer or overlay.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary label text for the trigger row.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon to display before the label. See `astryx docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary description text displayed below the label.

props.name: children
props.description: The flyout menu items: the same components used at the top level (DropdownMenuItem, nested DropdownMenuSubMenu, selectable items).

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: A disabled submenu renders its trigger row but never opens the flyout.

props.name: hasSpinner
props.description: Show a spinner in place of the caret, e.g. while a lazy submenu's children are loading.

props.name: menuWidth
props.description: Minimum flyout width. The flyout may grow for its content, but it is capped to the available viewport space. Defaults to intrinsic sizing (min 160px).

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the flyout opens or closes.

props.name: presentation
props.description: How the sub-menu shows its rows. 'flyout' opens them beside the row; 'drill-in' replaces the menu's rows with them and a Back row, in the same box; 'adaptive' drills in when a finger opened the menu (a coarse pointer, decided when the menu opened) and flies out otherwise.

props.name: delay
props.description: How long a hovering pointer waits before the flyout opens, in milliseconds. Keyboard focus and touch never wait.

props.name: hideDelay
props.description: How long the flyout stays open after the pointer leaves, in milliseconds.

props.name: header
props.description: Content above the sub-menu's rows and outside its menu, a field that filters them, say. It keeps its own keys and presses. With a header or footer the sub-menu's surface (the flyout, or the drilled-in view on a phone) is a modal dialog named by the row, beside the menu rather than inside it: the row says aria-haspopup="dialog", Tab and Shift+Tab move through the header, the rows and the footer and wrap, Escape returns to the row, and a pointer leaving the flyout closes it only once focus leaves too. A ContextMenu does not show it.

props.name: footer
props.description: Content below the sub-menu's rows and outside its menu, a door to where the options are managed, say. Same rules as header.

props.name: menuDataTestId
props.description: Test id for the sub-menu's own role="menu" element: the flyout, or the drilled-in list on a phone. The trigger row takes data-testid.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the trigger row. Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the trigger row, the element carrying role="menuitem" and aria-haspopup="menu" ("dialog" with a header or footer).

EmptyState.description: EmptyState shows a placeholder when a content area has no data. Use it for empty lists, zero search results, first-time setups, or cleared inboxes. Always include a title and a next step so the user is not stuck.

practices.text: Include a clear title and a call-to-action button so users know how to proceed.
Use an illustration or icon that reinforces the context of the empty state.
Use the compact variant inside cards or sidebars where space is limited.
Leave an empty state without guidance; always explain what happened and what the user can do next.
Use a generic message like "No data"; be specific about what is empty and why.
Use an EmptyState for error messages that require immediate action; use a Banner instead.

props.name: title
props.description: Primary message rendered as the configured heading level inside the empty state.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional secondary text providing additional context below the title.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon or illustration displayed above the title; rendered as decorative (aria-hidden="true").

props.name: actions
props.description: Optional action buttons displayed below the description, laid out horizontally by default and stacked vertically when isCompact is true.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Controls only the rendered HTML heading tag (h1-h6) so the title fits the document outline. This is a semantic change for accessibility and does not change the visual size of the title, which stays fixed regardless of level.

props.name: isCompact
props.description: Enables the compact variant with reduced spacing for constrained content areas.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

Field.description: Field is a low-level wrapper for custom, native, or third-party controls that do not already provide field label, description, and status UI. Use it when you need the Field shell around a control you own; use styled Astryx inputs like TextInput, Typeahead, and Select directly when they already expose label, description, and validation props.

practices.text: Wrap custom controls, native inputs, or third-party widgets that need labeling, helper text, optional/required indicators, or validation status.
Always provide a label for accessibility, even if visually hidden with isLabelHidden.
Use inputID and descriptionID to connect the label and description to the inner control with htmlFor and aria-describedby.
Nest Field around styled inputs such as TextInput, Typeahead, Select, DateInput, or TextArea; those components already render their own Field shell.
Use attached status only when the wrapped control is opaque, bordered, and fixed-height; use detached for custom, tall, translucent, or non-bordered controls.
Set both isOptional and isRequired on the same field.
Hide the label without providing an alternative way for the user to understand the field purpose.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the field (always rendered for accessibility).

props.name: inputID
props.description: ID for the input element (used for the label htmlFor attribute).

props.name: labelID
props.description: ID applied to the label element itself for group accessibility.

props.name: isGroupLabel
props.description: Renders the label as a span for control groups (radiogroup, checkbox list).

props.name: children
props.description: The input or control to render.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hide the label (still accessible to screen readers).

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the associated input is disabled. Propagates disabled styling to the label.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed between the label and input.

props.name: descriptionID
props.description: ID for the description element (use for aria-describedby on the input).

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Whether the field is optional (mutually exclusive with isRequired).

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Whether the field is required (mutually exclusive with isOptional).

props.name: labelIcon
props.description: Icon to display before the label text. See `astryx docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Help text for an info button after the label, named "About {label}". Hover and keyboard focus preview it; a tap, click, Enter, or Space opens it and never focuses or toggles the control.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator with type and optional message. When message is set, displays a colored status box. messageID is for wiring aria-describedby on the input.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How status feedback is placed. Attached overlaps an eligible opaque, bordered, fixed-height control; detached renders a message below custom or non-bordered controls; tooltip leaves the visible affordance to the wrapped input and announces its message without a FieldStatus box.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned. Prefer this over setting width via xstyle/className/style, which only size the inner control box. Without a width, a row can shrink the whole field below the natural width of its control, so filter bars shrink instead of overflowing.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the root element.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name(s) appended to the root element. Prefer xstyle for StyleX deduplication.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles applied to the root element. Takes priority over StyleX inline styles.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text, always rendered for accessibility.

props.name: inputID
props.description: ID of the input this label is for.

props.name: labelID
props.description: ID applied to the label element itself. Use it with `aria-labelledby` when `isGroupLabel` is true.

props.name: isGroupLabel
props.description: Render a span that can name a group instead of a native label for one control.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hide the label and description while keeping both available to assistive technology.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Use disabled label presentation for the associated control.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Show the localized optional indicator unless it matches FormLayout's default optionality.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Show the localized required indicator unless it matches FormLayout's default optionality.

props.name: labelIcon
props.description: Icon or rendered icon content before the label text. See `astryx docs icons` for semantic names.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Help text for an info button after the label, named "About {label}". Hover and keyboard focus preview it; a tap, click, Enter, or Space opens it and never focuses or toggles the control.

props.name: description
props.description: Supporting content displayed below the label and kept separate from the control's accessible name.

props.name: descriptionID
props.description: ID applied to the supporting description for caller-owned `aria-describedby` wiring.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the label element. Group mode currently renders a span.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles applied to the label element after its base and state styles.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name appended to the label element.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles applied to the label element after StyleX inline styles.

FieldStatus.description: FieldStatus renders validation feedback for fields and field-like controls. Use it directly for custom controls that need the same error, warning, or success presentation as Field.

practices.text: Use attached status below bordered inputs when the message belongs to that input.
Use detached status for controls like checkboxes, switches, and custom controls where overlap would be visually awkward.
Use FieldStatus for general alerts or page-level notices; use Banner or Toast instead.

A field's status is announced when it first appears and when its message or type changes, not again when a repeated submit fails with the same errors. On such a repeated submit, with the errors unchanged, announce it once from the form with useAnnounce, for example announce(`${errors.length} errors. ${errors[0]}`, 'assertive'), and move focus to the first invalid field. On a first failed submit the fields announce their own errors, so the form adds no announcement.

props.name: type
props.description: Status type.

props.name: message
props.description: Status message text.

props.name: id
props.description: ID for aria-describedby association.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual variant: attached overlaps the input, detached floats below.

InputGroup.description: InputGroup connects an input with prefix/suffix addons in a single visual unit. Use it for URL fields, currency inputs, search fields with action buttons, or any input that needs contextual decorations.

practices.text: Use text addons to show units, prefixes, or suffixes that clarify the input format (e.g., "$", "kg", "https://").
Use InputGroupText for static prefixes/suffixes like "$", "kg", or "https://".
Use Button for an action attached to the input; InputGroup connects its corners automatically.
Use InputGroup with compatible single-line inputs: TextInput, NumberInput, TimeInput, DateInput, Typeahead, Selector, and MultiSelector.
Keep each inner input's label specific; grouped inputs automatically combine the group label with their own label and inherit the group description/status context.
Don't put multiple text inputs in one group; use separate fields instead.
Don't use InputGroup for unrelated inputs; it's for a single input with decorations.
Don't use InputGroup with TextArea, Slider, Switch, CheckboxInput, or RadioList.

props.name: children
props.description: InputGroupText, Button addons, and compatible input children: TextInput, NumberInput, TimeInput, DateInput, Typeahead, Selector, or MultiSelector.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the group.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hide the label.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text between label and input group.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disable the entire group.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Show the "Optional" indicator after the label.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Mark the field as required.

props.name: size
props.description: Default size for inputs in the group.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status. Its message shows below the group. The group border does not change; a theme can style the row from `data-status`.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text at the end of the label.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector.

InputGroupText.description: Use InputGroupText inside InputGroup for a short fixed prefix or suffix, such as a currency symbol, a protocol, or a unit, or for a decorative icon. It is plain text, not a control, and it is not part of the input's accessible name.

practices.text: Keep the text short, such as $, https://, or kg. It stays on one line and does not shrink.
Put what a screen reader user needs in the input's own label, such as "Amount in USD" beside a $ prefix. The addon is read as plain text in reading order.
Put buttons, links, or other controls inside InputGroupText. Use a Button addon for an action.
Use InputGroupText outside InputGroup. Its borders and corners join an InputGroup row.

props.name: children
props.description: Text or icon content.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name(s).

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the text cell element.

FileInput.description: FileInput provides file upload with optional drag-and-drop support. Use it for single or multiple file selection with built-in validation for file type, size, and count. Pair with validation status for upload feedback.

practices.text: Always specify an accept prop to guide users toward valid file types.
Use maxSize and maxFiles to prevent oversized uploads; the component handles validation and error display automatically.
Add a description to communicate constraints like file size limits or accepted formats.
Use changeAction for immediate upload workflows that benefit from optimistic UI.
Don't use FileInput for directory or folder uploads; that is not supported in v1.
Don't avoid dropzone mode unless space is constrained; drag-and-drop is the expected interaction for file uploads.
Don't wrap a disabled FileInput in Tooltip to explain why it's disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the file input.

props.name: value
props.description: Currently selected file(s). Controlled component.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when files are selected or removed.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async change action (React 19 transitions pattern). Use for immediate upload on file selection.

props.name: accept
props.description: Accepted file types. Uses the HTML accept attribute format (e.g. "image/*", ".pdf,.doc").

props.name: isMultiple
props.description: Whether multiple files can be selected. When true, value and onChange use File[] instead of File.

props.name: maxSize
props.description: Maximum file size in bytes. Files exceeding this are rejected with an error status.

props.name: maxFiles
props.description: Maximum number of files (only applies when isMultiple is true).

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible to screen readers.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed between the label and input.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Displays an "Optional" indicator next to the label. Mutually exclusive with isRequired.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Displays a "Required" indicator next to the label and adds a screen-reader-only "Required" description to the trigger (assistive tech does not reliably announce aria-required on the trigger). Mutually exclusive with isOptional.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the input, preventing interaction and dimming the element.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the input is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the trigger focusable via aria-disabled (opening the file picker stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled FileInput in Tooltip; disabled controls swallow the hover events an external Tooltip needs.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Puts the input in a loading state, showing a spinner and setting aria-busy.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when no file is selected.

props.name: mode
props.description: Visual mode. 'input' is a compact inline style; 'dropzone' is a larger area with drag-and-drop support.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status: applies a colored border. If message is provided, displays a floating message below the input. Error type also sets aria-invalid.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip hides the message box and surfaces it in a tooltip on the status icon. Dropzone mode does not support attached: use detached or tooltip. From the next minor release, a dropzone resolves attached to detached and defaults to it.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text displayed in an info icon at the end of the label.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the element that paints the border and background and holds icons and end controls. Never the native input.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Class name for the visual control box.

props.name: controlStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the visual control box.

props.name: level
props.description: Heading level. Determines the semantic HTML element (h1-h6) and the visual styling from the theme (unless `type` is set).

props.name: type
props.description: Display type variant. Overrides the visual styling from `level` with display-scale sizing (larger, lighter weight, tighter line-height). Themes may add custom visual types. The `level` still determines the HTML element for accessibility. Use for hero banners, marketing headlines, and data callouts.

props.name: weight
props.description: Explicit font-weight override. Wins over the selected visual type or heading-level default.

props.name: children
props.description: Heading content.

props.name: accessibilityLevel
props.description: Accessibility level override. When set and different from `level`, applies `aria-level` so the document outline differs from the visual style.

props.name: color
props.description: Text color. Themes may add custom colors.

props.name: display
props.description: Display type. Silently overridden to 'block' when maxLines > 0 or hasCapsize is true.

props.name: maxLines
props.description: Maximum lines before truncation. 0 means no truncation. When set, shows a tooltip on hover if content is truncated.

props.name: hasTruncateTooltip
props.description: Controls tooltip behavior for truncated text. true shows the tooltip at the default position, false disables it, or a placement string ('above' | 'below' | 'start' | 'end') sets a specific position.

props.name: wordBreak
props.description: Word break behavior when truncating. Defaults to 'break-all' for single-line truncation, 'break-word' otherwise. Without truncation, a token longer than its line (a URL, an ID) wraps (`overflow-wrap: break-word`), so in ordinary flow text does not make the page scroll sideways. Inside a flex row, give the flex child `min-width: 0` so it can shrink. A container you style with `overflow-wrap: anywhere` does not reach this text; Astryx's own containers pass their wrap through.

props.name: textWrap
props.description: Text wrapping behavior.

props.name: justify
props.description: Text alignment (justification). Uses logical values (start/end) for i18n/RTL compatibility.

props.name: hasCapsize
props.description: Enable optical alignment using text-box-trim. Forces block display.

props.name: hasStrikethrough
props.description: Apply strikethrough text decoration.

props.name: id
props.description: HTML id attribute.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles applied to the heading element. Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name applied to the heading element.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles applied to the heading element. When `maxLines` is above 1, its line clamp replaces any `WebkitLineClamp` in `style`.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the heading element.

HoverCard.description: HoverCard shows additional information when the user hovers or focuses a trigger element. Use it for profile cards, link summaries, or inline definitions where the user needs more context without navigating away.

practices.text: Keep content supplementary; hover cards should enhance understanding without blocking the primary workflow.
Provide a dashed underline on text triggers so users know the element is hoverable.
Use the hook API (useHoverCard) when you need more control over timing or placement.
Leave touchTrigger on auto so a tap opens the card on triggers that do nothing else, and stays out of the way on triggers that perform an action.
Place critical actions or required information inside a hover card; users may miss content that only appears on hover.
Use a hover card when a simple Tooltip or Popover would suffice.
Use a HoverCard for content the user must interact with; it disappears when the cursor leaves.

Put the trigger inside SVG <foreignObject>. In Chromium it cannot be a CSS anchor, so the card opens at the viewport corner. Render the trigger in an HTML layer positioned over the SVG node instead, and keep the SVG for shapes, edges and labels.

Prefer placing HoverCard in a block context rather than directly in a

, heading, or link. Those placements are supported when necessary through a corrective portal, but the DOM and tab order may differ.

props.name: children
props.description: The trigger. Text children, a string or number or text written around an expression such as `Edited {when}`, are wrapped in a focusable inline span; holes such as `false` and `null` are ignored. With element children, HoverCard wires the first element, so that element does not need to accept a ref.

props.name: content
props.description: Hover card content.

props.name: placement
props.description: Position relative to the anchor element. Logical: start/end resolve against the popover's own inherited direction (RTL mirrors in pure CSS).

props.name: alignment
props.description: Alignment along the placement axis. Logical: start/end resolve against the popover's own inherited direction (RTL mirrors in pure CSS).

props.name: delay
props.description: Show delay in milliseconds.

props.name: hideDelay
props.description: Hide delay in milliseconds.

props.name: focusTrigger
props.description: When focus should open the hover card. auto opens when the trigger itself takes focus, or focus lands inside a trigger that is focusable at that moment, so a roving-tabindex member opens when the arrow keys reach it.

props.name: touchTrigger
props.description: What a tap does where there is no hover. auto opens on tap unless the trigger performs an action of its own (a button, link, or form control), whose tap belongs to the control; an aria-disabled control performs none, so a tap on it opens its reason. tap always opens. none never opens on touch. A tap-opened card is dismissed by a tap outside it.

props.name: isEnabled
props.description: Enables or disables the hover and focus triggers.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the hover card popup. When provided, the popup is exposed as a named role="dialog"; when omitted, it falls back to role="group" (a group may validly be unnamed).

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback fired when hover card visibility changes. Called with true when shown and false when hidden.

props.name: hasHoverIndication
props.description: Shows a dashed underline on a text trigger. auto shows it when children is text: strings and numbers, such as `Edited {when}`, with holes such as `false` and `null` ignored. It has no effect on an element trigger, which keeps its own styling.

props.name: isDefaultOpen
props.description: Whether the hover card should be shown on mount. Still dismissible.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Controlled open state. true holds the card open. false holds it closed against hover and focus. A controlled card answers Escape by calling onOpenChange(false) without closing; it closes when you set isOpen to false, and focus inside the card then returns to the trigger.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the card surface, the element that carries the hover-card theme target.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name added to the card surface, beside the hover-card target class.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the card surface.

Icon.description: Icons are small visual symbols that represent actions, objects, or concepts. They improve scannability and reinforce meaning alongside text. Supports both direct SVG components and semantic icon names that adapt to the active theme.

practices.text: Use semantic icon names when available; they adapt to theme changes automatically.

Override icons through the theme, not globally: defineTheme({icons: {close: <XMarkIcon />}}) scopes the swap to the active <Theme>, and extends shallow-merges it into derived themes. registerIcons() mutates a process-wide registry and warns in dev, so keep it for app bootstrap rather than making it a library's theming seam.

To match artwork to the rendered size, make a theme or registered icon entry a pure, synchronous function of {size, variant}: defineTheme({icons: {info: ({size}) => <InfoIcon weight={size === 'sm' ? 'bold' : 'regular'} />}}). Icon passes the size it renders at; getIcon(), useIcon(), getIconRegistry() and theme.icons read the function at size md. A function that returns null draws nothing instead of falling back to the default icon. Do not use hooks, measure the DOM, or read browser or mutable state inside it.
Pair icons with text labels for accessibility; icon-only elements need an accessible label.
For a meaningful standalone icon (no adjacent text), give it an accessible name via the `label` prop: it sets role="img" + aria-label and unhides the icon.
Use color tokens for icon colors, not hardcoded hex values.
Be mindful of context; decorative icons in compact components can distract rather than help.
Use icons as the sole means of conveying meaning; always provide a text alternative.
Resize icons with arbitrary pixel values; use the provided size props.
Mix icon styles (e.g. outline and filled) within the same context.
Render raw SVG elements; always wrap in Icon for consistent sizing and color.
Pass a `name` prop; Icon uses `icon` (not `name`) to specify which icon to render.

props.name: icon
props.description: Semantic icon name or SVG component. Valid semantic names: close, chevronDown, chevronLeft, chevronRight, chevronsLeft, chevronsRight, check, success, error, warning, info, calendar, clock, externalLink, menu, moreHorizontal, search, upload, arrowUp, arrowDown, arrowsUpDown, funnel, eyeSlash, viewColumns, copy, checkDouble, wrench, stop, microphone. A namespaced key such as `richtext:bold` names a glyph that one component or library registers, and a theme can replace it by key; a namespaced key that nothing registers renders nothing. For any icon not in this list, pass an SVG component directly (e.g. import from lucide-react or @heroicons/react). Note: this prop is called `icon`, not `name`.

props.name: color
props.description: Color variant mapped to Astryx icon color tokens. Semantic values (primary through warning) follow the role, and inherit uses the surrounding text color. On the web, Icon also accepts the palette values blue, red, green, gray, cyan, teal, yellow, orange, pink, and purple, which pick a non-semantic hue.

props.name: size
props.description: Icon size. xsm, sm, md, and lg are 12, 16, 20, and 24px at a 16px root and scale with the root font size; a theme sets a size's glyph dimension with width and height, in px or rem, on components.icon['size:sm'] (and the other sizes). An explicit value wins. When omitted, Icon uses the nearest default supplied by an owning Astryx component for its icon slot, then falls back to md when no contextual default exists.

props.name: variant
props.description: Requests the active theme's alternate artwork for a semantic icon name, such as 'filled'. Names come from IconVariantMap, which an application augments from @astryxdesign/core/Icon; Astryx defines none. The theme's icon entry receives the variant only when the active theme lists it in iconVariants (and, for an entry the theme inherited, the theme that defined the entry lists it too); otherwise it draws its normal artwork. Ignored by an icon component passed directly. Selects artwork only: it is not written to the DOM and has no theming selector.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for a MEANINGFUL, standalone icon (a status glyph or icon-only indicator with no adjacent text). Setting it exposes the icon to screen readers as role="img" with this text as the accessible name (aria-label) and removes the default aria-hidden. Omit it (default) for decorative icons and the icon stays hidden from assistive tech (aria-hidden="true"). This is the accessible-name / alt-text prop for icons: one prop instead of manually setting aria-label + role + aria-hidden. An empty string is treated as decorative. Do not set it when an interactive parent (Button, IconButton, link) already names the control.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for customization (color, size, opacity). Folded into the icon's own stylex.props() call so it composes with the base color/size styles. Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name added to the rendered glyph, beside the astryx-icon target class.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles merged onto the rendered glyph after Icon's own size and color styles.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the rendered SVG element, for an icon component and for a semantic or namespaced name. For a name, it is the <svg> inside the wrapper, or null when the resolved glyph has no <svg>.

InfoTip.description: An info icon that reveals help: a small "i" button. Hover and keyboard focus preview the help, and a click, tap, Enter, or Space pins it open until Escape, a second press, a press outside, or focus leaving. Use it next to labels, values, and metrics for permission notes, metric definitions, and field help. Its value over hand-composing Icon inside Tooltip is the pre-wired accessible trigger: a real button with an aria-label, Tab-reachable, tooltip on hover AND focus AND tap, and Escape dismissal. It follows the toggletip pattern: the button reports `aria-expanded="true"` while the help is pinned, and a screen reader hears the help once when it pins.

practices.text: Keep tooltip content concise, plain, and non-interactive; use Popover or HoverCard for links and buttons.
Override label when "More information" is too generic, e.g. "About this metric".

Rely on InfoTip rather than a hand-rolled info button on touch: it pins its help on a press, so a tap, a click, Enter, or Space pins the tooltip even though the trigger is a button, and a tap outside dismisses it.
Hand-compose Icon inside Tooltip for info affordances; the bare Icon is aria-hidden and unfocusable, so keyboard and screen-reader users never see it.
Use InfoTip for essential information users must see to complete a task; put that text inline instead.

props.name: content
props.description: Content to display in the tooltip. Typically short, non-interactive text. Mirrors Tooltip's content prop.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the trigger button. Defaults to the translated "More information".

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the info icon (12px, 16px, 20px, 24px). Maps 1:1 to Icon sizes.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

Item.description: A single, flexible item primitive that unifies the "start content + label + description + end content" pattern across Astryx. Use it wherever you need a structured row: dropdown menus, selectors, contact lists, notifications, file browsers, and activity feeds.

practices.text: Use named slots (startContent, label, description, endContent) for the common layout. These cover the 80% case.
Use density="compact" for menus and dense lists, "balanced" for standard rows, and "spacious" for roomier layouts.
Set labelLines and descriptionLines to control truncation when content length varies.

Use align="first-line" when a wrapping label sits beside a small mark (a status dot, a radio, a timestamp) that belongs to its first line. Use align="start" to line up the tops of a tall slot and the text.
Give a swipe action a second home in the row (a menu or a button in endContent): the swipe is a touch accelerator, and a verb reachable only by swipe is unreachable by keyboard and by mouse.
Don't nest interactive elements (buttons, links) inside an interactive Item; it creates confusing focus and click targets.
Don't use Item for navigation between views; use proper navigation components instead.
Don't add read/unread or inbox-specific behavior directly; compose a thin wrapper like PreviewItem instead.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary text identifying this item. Accepts string (auto-truncated) or ReactNode (for rich content).

props.name: marker
props.description: Marker rendered before startContent as a direct flex child. Use for list bullets/counters that need custom baseline alignment.

props.name: startContent
props.description: Content rendered before the label/description area, such as an icon, avatar, or checkbox.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary text: subtitle, description, or supporting info.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content rendered after the label/description area, such as badges, metadata, timestamps, or action buttons.

props.name: as
props.description: What the root renders as: an HTML element, or a component for a caller that needs the root to be something else. A menu row that navigates passes the application's link component here, so the row's root IS the anchor. Give a component only when the row carries a role, and only when no interactive node sits in startContent or endContent.

props.name: align
props.description: Vertical alignment of start/end content slots. 'center' centers each slot on the whole text block; 'start' lines up slot tops with the text's top; 'first-line' centers each slot on the label's first line, so a small mark stays level with the first line of a wrapped label. A slot taller than that line moves the text down. The `item` theme target reflects the value as `align`.

props.name: density
props.description: Spacing density. "compact" uses 4px block padding, "balanced" uses 8px, and "spacious" uses 12px block and inline padding.

props.name: labelLines
props.description: Max lines before label truncates with ellipsis.

props.name: descriptionLines
props.description: Max lines before description truncates with ellipsis.

props.name: layout
props.description: How the label and description sit together. stacked puts the description on its own line below the label; inline keeps both on one line, description ellipsizing first, so the row fits a fixed-height host.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler. Makes the item clickable with button semantics.

props.name: interactiveRef
props.description: Ref to a nested control (e.g. a checkbox in startContent) that owns the item's keyboard access and action. The row becomes an enlarged click/tap target that delegates surface clicks to it (useClickableContainer) and renders no invisible button/anchor, so the row adds no second tab stop (WCAG 4.1.2). Mutually exclusive with onClick/href; those are ignored when set.

props.name: href
props.description: Link URL. Makes the item a link via an invisible anchor element. A row whose root is already a link component (see `as`) carries the address on that root instead, and no invisible anchor is rendered.

props.name: target
props.description: Link target. Only used with href. target="_blank" automatically adds noopener noreferrer.

props.name: rel
props.description: Link relationship tokens. noopener noreferrer are merged automatically for target="_blank".

props.name: isHighlighted
props.description: Highlighted state (hover/keyboard focus appearance).

props.name: isSelected
props.description: Selected state.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disabled state.

props.name: swipeActions
props.description: Swipe actions for touch: the verbs a sideways drag uncovers on each side, outermost last, each `{id?, label, icon?, onActivate, isDisabled?, variant?: 'neutral' | 'accent' | 'destructive', hasRemoval?}`. `leading` is uncovered by a drag toward the inline end, `trailing` toward the inline start. A mouse never starts the drag and a mostly vertical drag stays the scroller's. The gesture is a touch accelerator and never a row's only path to a verb: a verb reachable only by swipe is unreachable by keyboard and by mouse, so every entry must also be reachable through the row's own content. Served on a row whose role permits interactive descendants (a listitem, a row with no role) and not on an option, a menu item, or a row that is the enlarged target of a native radio. The element containing the rows clips in the inline axis with overflow-inline: clip — List does; any other host does it once. `hasRemoval` only says the row holds out after the action fires instead of springing back. The gesture and its panels are loaded on demand the first time a row has swipe actions, so a row without them ships none of it.

props.name: swipeBehavior
props.description: What a swipe does. `reveal` rests the row open with every entry a real button and fires the outermost on a long drag or a fling; `commit` slides the row out and fires the outermost on release, with nothing resting and a presentational panel. `commit` fits one entry per side.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the root element, whose type follows `as`.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name(s) for the root element.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the root element.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

Kbd.description: Renders a keyboard shortcut as styled key badges. Use Kbd in tooltips, menus, and help text to show key combinations.

practices.text: Place shortcuts near the action they trigger: in a tooltip, menu item, or inline instruction.
Use mod instead of ctrl or cmd; it automatically adapts to the user's platform.
Let Kbd name the shortcut: screen readers hear the keys as words, such as "Command + K". Kbd ignores an aria-label you pass; to name it from visible text, use aria-labelledby.
Use Kbd as the only way to discover an action; shortcuts should supplement visible controls, not replace them.
Expect Kbd to handle the key press. It only shows the keys; listen for the shortcut in your own code.

props.name: keys
props.description: Keyboard shortcut string. Use "+" to separate keys. Special keys: mod (⌘ on Apple platforms, Ctrl elsewhere), ctrl, alt and shift (Apple symbols on Apple platforms, Ctrl, Alt and Shift text elsewhere), meta (⌘ on Apple platforms, Win elsewhere and before hydration), enter, backspace, escape, tab, up, down, left, right, plus. Aliases: esc for escape and return for enter.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling; className is provided for integration with non-StyleX systems.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling; inline styles bypass StyleX optimization.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the shortcut group element.

Center.description: Center aligns content to the middle of its container. Use it for empty states, loading screens, login forms, or any content that should sit in the center of the available space.

practices.text: Use a single-axis value only in horizontal writing, or after verifying the active writing mode. In vertical writing, the current implementation follows flex main/cross axes rather than the physical prop names.
In horizontal writing, give Center height when using axis="vertical"; centering needs available space on the selected flex axis.
Use isInline to center small elements like icons or badges within a line of text without breaking the text flow.
Keep semantic structure and accessible names on the content. Center is a layout-only container and does not add a role or label.
Wrap large page sections in Center. Use Layout or AppShell for page-level structure.
Use Center for horizontal lists of items. Use Stack with hAlign="center" instead.

props.name: axis
props.description: Which Center mode to use. In horizontal writing, "horizontal" centers the flex main/inline axis and "vertical" centers the cross/block axis. In vertical writing, current single-axis behavior follows those logical flex axes rather than the physical names; "both" still centers both axes.

props.name: width
props.description: Container width (px or CSS value).

props.name: height
props.description: Container height (px or CSS value).

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: Maximum container width (px or CSS value).

props.name: minHeight

props.name: paddingInline
props.description: Logical inline-axis padding, using the spacing scale. Overrides padding on the inline axis when both are set.

props.name: paddingInlineStart
props.description: Logical inline-start padding, using the spacing scale. Its resolved physical edge depends on writing mode and direction. Overrides paddingInline and padding on that edge only.

props.name: paddingInlineEnd
props.description: Logical inline-end padding, using the spacing scale. Its resolved physical edge depends on writing mode and direction. Overrides paddingInline and padding on that edge only.

props.description: Logical block-start padding, using the spacing scale. Its resolved physical edge depends on writing mode. Overrides paddingBlock and padding on that edge only.

props.description: Use inline-flex (useful for text/icons).

FormLayout.description: A layout container that arranges form fields with consistent spacing and direction. FormLayout handles where fields go, not state or submission. Wrap it in a native <form> for that; <form> has no Astryx replacement, so it stays a plain element. Supports vertical (default), horizontal, and horizontal-labels directions, and can be nested to mix them.

practices.text: Stack fields vertically for most forms. It's the easiest to scan top to bottom.
Nest a horizontal FormLayout inside a vertical one when fields naturally pair up, like First Name + Last Name or City + State + ZIP.
Use horizontal-labels for settings pages where labels sit beside their inputs.
Use FormLayout for form state or submission. It's just layout. Wrap it in a native <form> for that.
Put unrelated fields side by side in a horizontal layout. Save it for fields that belong together.
Nest horizontal-labels inside another FormLayout. It uses CSS Grid and needs to be the outermost container.

props.name: direction
props.description: Controls field arrangement. Vertical stacks top-to-bottom, horizontal uses one fractional grid track per field in logical inline order, and horizontal-labels uses CSS Grid with labels beside inputs on the inline-start side (collapsing to vertical when the viewport is <=480px).

props.name: defaultOptionality
props.description: The state the form treats as its default, so only the exception shows an optional/required indicator. With "optional", only fields marked isRequired show an indicator; with "required", only fields marked isOptional do. A field that restates the default shows nothing. Under "required" the unmarked fields also expose aria-required so screen readers match the visual default; aria-required only, never the native required attribute. CheckboxInput, Switch and CheckboxList are the exception: an unchecked box, an off switch or an empty group is an answer, so they take no required state from the default. A CheckboxInput or Switch is required only through its own isRequired. Leave unset for today's per-field behavior.

props.name: children
props.description: Form fields to arrange. Accepts Astryx inputs (TextInput, Selector, etc.) and Field-wrapped custom controls.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

Grid.description: A CSS grid layout container for arranging children in rows and columns. Use Grid for card galleries, dashboards, and any multi-column layout. For columns that reflow on small screens, use `columns={{minWidth, max}}`; a numeric `columns` is exactly N columns at every width and never reflows.

practices.text: Default to responsive columns for anything that must survive a phone: `columns={{minWidth: 240, max: 4}}` renders at most 4 columns, each at least 240px, and drops to one full-width column when narrow.
Use `columns={4}` for a row that must work on small screens; a number never reflows and renders four narrow tracks on a phone. Reserve numbers for rows that must stay fixed, such as a 7-day week.
Always pair `minWidth` with `max`: `max` caps the count on wide screens and lets the last column shrink to a narrow container; `{minWidth}` alone overflows a phone narrower than `minWidth`.
Use `repeat: 'fill'` (the default) for consistent item widths. Use `'fit'` when items should stretch to fill leftover space.
Write manual CSS grid; Grid handles spacing and responsive behavior for you.
Use `HStack` with wrapping for grids; use Grid instead.
Track templates use CSS-variable indirection (not raw inline styles), so `xstyle` overrides of `gridTemplateColumns` (including inside `@media` queries) take effect.

props.name: columns
props.description: Column configuration. A number creates exactly N `1fr` tracks at every width and never reflows (e.g. `columns={3}`); a child's minimum content may widen its track. For columns that reflow on small screens, use `{minWidth, max}`. Use an object for responsive columns: `minWidth` sets the minimum column width in px, `repeat` controls track behavior (`"fill"` preserves empty tracks for consistent widths, `"fit"` collapses empty tracks so items stretch; defaults to `"fill"`), and `max` caps the maximum number of columns.

props.name: width
props.description: Container width. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is.

props.name: height
props.description: Container height. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is.

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: Maximum container width. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is.

props.name: minHeight
props.description: Minimum container height. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is.

props.name: gap
props.description: Spacing between all items.

props.name: rowGap
props.description: Row spacing; overrides `gap` for the row axis.

props.name: columnGap
props.description: Column spacing; overrides `gap` for the column axis.

props.name: rowHeight
props.description: Height of each implicit row track in pixels. Pair with `GridSpan rows={N}` for masonry-style layouts.

props.name: align
props.description: Vertical alignment of items (`align-items`). Unset leaves the browser default, `normal`, which stretches items that have no natural size or aspect ratio.

props.name: justify
props.description: Horizontal alignment of items (`justify-items`). Unset leaves the browser default, `normal`, which stretches items that have no natural size or aspect ratio.

props.name: children
props.description: Grid content.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: rows

props.description: CSS class name applied to the span wrapper.

props.description: Inline styles applied to the span wrapper. When `columns` or `rows` is set, its `grid-column` or `grid-row` replaces the same property in `style`.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the span wrapper.

HStack.description: Stack arranges items in a row or column with consistent spacing. Use the gap prop to control the space between items.

practices.text: Use the gap prop for spacing between items; don't add margins manually.
Use StackItem with size="fill" to make one item stretch and fill the leftover space.
Nest stacks inside stacks; try wrap="wrap" first to let items flow to the next line.

props.name: gap
props.description: Spacing step (number literal): 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10. Pass as a JSX number expression e.g. gap={4}, NOT a string like gap="4".

props.name: padding
props.description: Inner padding on all sides, using the spacing scale (0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10). Matches the padding prop on Card, LayoutContent, and LayoutPanel. Pass as a JSX number expression e.g. padding={3}.

props.name: paddingInline
props.description: Inline (horizontal) padding, using the spacing scale. Overrides padding on the inline axis when both are set.

props.name: paddingInlineStart
props.description: Inline-start padding, using the spacing scale (left in LTR, right in RTL). Overrides paddingInline and padding on that edge only.

props.name: paddingInlineEnd
props.description: Inline-end padding, using the spacing scale (right in LTR, left in RTL). Overrides paddingInline and padding on that edge only.
