props.name: paddingBlockEnd
props.description: Block-end (bottom) padding, using the spacing scale. Overrides paddingBlock and padding on that edge only.

props.name: isScrollable
props.description: Enables scrollable overflow (overflow: auto). Matches isScrollable on LayoutContent and LayoutPanel.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the stack container. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is (e.g., '100%').

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the stack container. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is (e.g., '100%').

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: Maximum width of the stack container. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is (e.g., '100%').

props.name: minHeight
props.description: Minimum height of the stack container. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is (e.g., '100%').

props.name: hAlign
props.description: Horizontal (main-axis) alignment of items.

props.name: vAlign
props.description: Vertical (cross-axis) alignment of items.

props.name: justify
props.description: Main-axis alignment alias for hAlign. Mirrors CSS justify-content. When hAlign is also set, hAlign wins.

props.name: align
props.description: Cross-axis alignment alias for vAlign. Mirrors CSS align-items. When vAlign is also set, vAlign wins.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Flex wrap behavior.

props.description: HTML element to render as the stack container.

props.description: Stack content.

props.description: Class name added to the stack element, after the component styles.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the stack element. width, height, maxWidth, and minHeight win over the same properties here.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the rendered stack element.

Layout.description: Layout is a general five-slot primitive for arranging header, start, content, end, and footer regions within a page or bounded container. AppShell owns the page shell and app-wide navigation behavior; use HStack or VStack for simple directional stacking.

practices.text: Use Layout when content needs named header, start, content, end, or footer regions.
Use HStack and VStack for simple directional stacking within a content area.
Hide a region by passing `false`, `null`, or `undefined` to its slot, for example `isOpen && <LayoutPanel />`. The slot counts as empty, so the neighbouring regions move out to the layout edge.
Give a region a landmark role and label on the region component when it is a page landmark, for example `<LayoutPanel role="navigation" label="Sections">`. Layout adds no role or name.
Use Layout for simple stacking layouts; use HStack or VStack instead.
Use Layout as the page shell or for app-wide navigation; use AppShell for that responsibility.

props.name: content
props.description: Content slot (center). Accepts any ReactNode; use LayoutContent when a content region is needed. Children passed to `<Layout>` render here too: `<Layout>{main}</Layout>` is shorthand for `<Layout content={main} />`.

props.name: header
props.description: Header slot. Accepts any ReactNode; use LayoutHeader when a header region is needed.

props.name: footer
props.description: Footer slot. Accepts any ReactNode; use LayoutFooter when a footer region is needed.

props.name: start
props.description: Logical-start slot (left in LTR). Accepts any ReactNode; use LayoutPanel when a panel region is needed.

props.name: end
props.description: Logical-end slot (right in LTR). Accepts any ReactNode; use LayoutPanel when a panel region is needed.

props.name: height
props.description: Height behavior: fill the container's height or grow with content. Fill needs a container with a set height, such as AppShell's content area; under an app root with no height, the layout grows with its content.

props.name: contentWidth
props.description: Maximum width of the aligned content within each slot (header, content, footer, panels), centered when narrower than the available space. Without panels, LayoutContent spans the available width so its scrollbar stays at the outer edge while its children align internally to contentWidth. With exactly one panel, the panel stays aligned to the contentWidth frame while LayoutContent extends to the opposite open edge. With both panels, contentWidth includes the complete middle composition. Percentage widths—including percentage-bearing calc(), min(), max(), and clamp() values—and intrinsic widths, plus bare var(...) values, retain the constrained composition; use calc(var(...)) for a variable guaranteed to resolve to a length. Dividers stay full-bleed. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is (e.g. `60ch`). Common page widths: 640 for forms, settings, and text-focused pages; 960 for content pages and wider layouts.

props.name: padding
props.description: Padding at the layout's outer edges using the spacing scale. Applies to this Layout's own header, footer, panels, and content. A nested Layout does not inherit it: without `padding`, its regions use the enclosing Card, Section, or Dialog padding, or the default inset (spacing 4). That keeps a page Layout inside AppShell inset even though AppShell's own regions are full bleed.

props.name: children
props.description: Shorthand for the content slot: `<Layout>{main}</Layout>` is the same as `<Layout content={main} />`. When both are given, `content` wins.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the root layout element.

props.name: defaultHasDividers
props.description: Default divider visibility for LayoutHeader and LayoutFooter children. Headers and footers that don't pass `hasDivider` use this value; when unset, nested layouts inherit from their parent context.

props.name: children
props.description: Content.

props.name: padding
props.description: Internal padding using the spacing scale. Overrides the default padding from the layout container.

props.name: isScrollable
props.description: Enable scrollable overflow. With arithmetic contentWidth values, the scrollport spans through every open side while context-aware insets keep children aligned.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the landmark element. While the region scrolls, it also names the scrolling region, which otherwise takes a translated "Content".

props.name: role
props.description: ARIA landmark role.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the content region element.

props.name: children
props.description: Footer content.

props.name: hasDivider
props.description: Border at top edge. When unset, the parent Layout's defaultHasDividers decides.

props.name: height
props.description: Footer height. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the landmark element.

props.name: padding
props.description: Internal padding on every edge, using the spacing scale. Replaces the inset from the layout; 0 is full bleed.

props.name: role
props.description: ARIA landmark role.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the footer element.

props.name: children
props.description: Header content.

props.name: hasDivider
props.description: Border at bottom edge. When unset, the parent Layout's defaultHasDividers decides.

props.name: height
props.description: Header height. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the landmark element.

props.name: padding
props.description: Internal padding on every edge, using the spacing scale. Replaces the inset from the layout; 0 is full bleed.

props.name: paddingBlockEnd
props.description: Block-end (bottom) padding, using the spacing scale. Overrides padding on that edge only; paddingBlockEnd={0} docks the last child on the header bottom edge.

props.name: role
props.description: ARIA landmark role.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the header element.

props.name: children
props.description: Panel content.

props.name: hasDivider
props.description: Line on the edge that faces the content: the inline end in the start slot, the inline start in the end slot. Without it and without padding, the panel and the content share one gap. The Layout's defaultHasDividers does not apply. Beside a ResizeHandle that draws its own line, leave it false.

props.name: padding
props.description: Internal padding on every edge, using the spacing scale. Replaces the automatic inset and the gap shared with the content. 0 is full bleed.

props.name: isScrollable
props.description: Enable scrollable overflow.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the landmark element. While the region scrolls, it also names the scrolling region, which otherwise takes a translated "Content".

props.name: role
props.description: ARIA landmark role.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the panel. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is. Ignored when resizable is provided; the hook controls width. Beside a ResizeHandle given a useResizable region's props, a panel at width={region.size} is inert while the region is collapsed, and focus inside it moves to the handle as it collapses.

props.name: resizable
props.description: The output of useResizable(), or its props. When provided, the hook drives the panel width and a ResizeHandle should be placed adjacent to the panel. Carries the region's axis ('horizontal' | 'vertical'), which must match the adjacent ResizeHandle's direction. With the hook's own value, the panel slides closed and open from the edge facing its ResizeHandle; a hand-built object does not slide. Either way, focus inside the panel moves to its ResizeHandle as it collapses, and the panel is inert while collapsed.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the panel element.

Section.description: Section is the correct way to create page regions and group related content on a page. Use it for settings groups, form sections, sidebar areas, or any time you need visual separation between parts of a page. If you are tempted to use a Card for a page section, use Section instead.

practices.text: Use Section for page-level grouping: settings panels, form groups, sidebar regions. These are sections of a page, not discrete items.
Start with the default variant. Use muted only to call attention to a specific region.
Add dividers between same-background sections that need separation.
Combine with a heading + Stack for a typical page section pattern.
Use Card when you mean Section. Cards are for discrete items (one notification, one profile). Sections are for page regions.

To center a Section, set marginInlineStart and marginInlineEnd to 'auto' in xstyle. If Astryx source is compiled in your app's own StyleX pass, the marginInline shorthand loses to Section's own inline margins.

props.name: paddingInlineEnd
props.description: Inline-end padding override (right in LTR, left in RTL). Overrides paddingInline and padding on that edge only.

Use StackItem with size="fill" to make one item stretch and fill the leftover space.

props.name: paddingInlineEnd

props.name: paddingBlock

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the stack element. width, height, maxWidth, and minHeight win over the same properties here.

Lightbox.description: A fullscreen overlay for viewing images and videos at full resolution. Supports single-item and gallery modes with prev/next navigation and swiping, optional zoom and pan for images, and native video controls.

practices.text: Always provide alt text for every image for screen reader accessibility.
Use gallery mode with onIndexChange for multi-image sets.
Enable hasZoom only when viewing high-resolution images that benefit from close inspection.
Use the lightbox for content other than images and videos; it shows one media item at a time.
Nest interactive content inside captions; keep them plain text.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Whether the lightbox is open.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback when the lightbox open state changes: the Close button, Escape, a tap beside the media, or, on a phone or tablet, dragging a photo down from its fitted size.

props.name: media
props.description: Media to display. Pass a single object for one item, or an array for gallery mode with prev/next navigation (on a phone or tablet, a swipe moves between items too). Each item is {src: string, alt: string, caption?: ReactNode, type?: 'image' | 'video'}; type defaults to 'image', and zoom/pan is disabled for 'video'.

props.name: index
props.description: Current index in gallery mode (when media is an array).

props.name: onIndexChange
props.description: Callback when the gallery index changes: prev/next, the arrow keys, or a swipe.

props.name: hasZoom
props.description: Enable zoom (images only): pinch (or ctrl-wheel), or double-tap or double-click to zoom in at that point and back; Enter/Space/+/- zoom 2× about the centre and back, and 0 returns to the fitted size. When zoomed, drag or scroll a trackpad to pan, or use arrow keys; on a phone or a tablet, the pan has momentum.

props.name: defaultIndex
props.description: Initial image index in gallery mode for uncontrolled usage.

props.name: hasAutoPlay
props.description: Automatically start video playback when a video media item is shown.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be stylex.create() value.

Link.description: A styled anchor for inline and standalone text navigation. Supports external links, underline variants, tooltips, and custom link components for router integration. Use it for navigating between pages or to external URLs.

practices.text: Write descriptive, concise link text that clearly communicates the destination.
Set `isStandalone` when the link appears outside of inline text, so it receives proper base font sizing.
Put a Link inside a <Text maxLines> to truncate it with the surrounding text; inside a clamped Text the link flows in the text's lines.

Only set `label` when the link content is not descriptive text (e.g. an icon-only link). For text links, the visible text is already the accessible name; adding `label` overrides it for screen readers, which is harmful.
Use Link for actions that do not navigate; use a Button instead.
Use generic text like "click here" or "read more"; describe the destination.
Set `label` on text links; `aria-label` prevents assistive technology from reading the actual link content.
Give a Link inside a clamped Text its own `display` or `maxLines`, or render it as a button (`onClick` with no `href`), and expect the outer clamp to cut it; that Link keeps its own box.
Put a Link with block-level content, such as an HStack with an icon, inside a clamped Text; block content breaks the clamp. Clamp a text-only Link, or place the composed Link outside the clamp.

props.name: as
props.description: Custom component to render instead of <a>

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label (aria-label). Only use when children are not self-descriptive (e.g. icon-only links). Omit for text links; the link text is the accessible name.

props.name: href
props.description: Link destination URL. Astryx-owned links and clickable surfaces block javascript:, vbscript:, and data:text/html after control-character removal, outer-whitespace trimming, and case-insensitive scheme inspection. The same rule covers native anchors, custom routers, Markdown links, and every activation method. Relative paths, fragments, protocol-relative URLs, HTTP(S), mailto, tel, safe custom schemes, and accepted downloads keep their existing behavior. A rejected destination renders inertly without invoking a custom router. There is no bypass prop; exceptional behavior requires caller-owned custom rendering outside this guarantee. Images and other resource URLs have separate policies.

props.name: hasUnderline
props.description: Always show underline

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the link

props.name: isExternalLink
props.description: Opens in new tab with external icon and safe rel tokens

props.name: newTabLabel
props.description: Screen-reader text announcing that an external link opens in a new tab. Override for localization.

props.name: target
props.description: Where to open linked document. target="_blank" automatically adds noopener noreferrer.

props.name: rel
props.description: Link relationship tokens. noopener noreferrer are merged automatically for target="_blank".

props.name: download
props.description: Causes the browser to download the linked URL. A string specifies the suggested filename.

props.name: referrerPolicy
props.description: Referrer policy for the link.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click event handler

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Tooltip text displayed on hover

props.name: isStandalone
props.description: Applies base font sizing

props.name: size
props.description: Explicit font size override forwarded to Text.

props.name: weight
props.description: Font weight override forwarded to Text.

props.name: color
props.description: Text color forwarded to Text.

props.name: display
props.description: Display type for Text.

props.name: maxLines
props.description: Maximum lines before truncation.

props.name: children
props.description: Link content

props.name: component
props.description: Component to use for all link elements. It receives accepted `href` and `to` values under the shared navigation rule described on the Link `href` prop. Supported structured destinations, including their `protocol`, are checked without changing object identity. If either supplied destination is rejected, Astryx renders inert content without invoking this component; it does not pass undefined or fall back to the other destination.

props.name: children
props.description: Subtree

List.description: A vertical collection of items with consistent spacing, dividers, and optional markers. Supports headers, icons, avatars, badges, and interactive items with click or link behavior. Use it to display ordered or unordered groups of related content.

practices.text: Provide a header to label the list and give context to screen readers.
Use start and end content slots to add icons, avatars, or badges to each item.
Set edge to line row text up with a heading above the list: flush for static rows, outset or bleed for rows in a Card, Section, or Dialog.

To line text up with a heading and keep room around the highlight where there is no Card, such as a sidebar, put the heading and the list in a Section with variant="transparent" and set edge="outset".
Place interactive elements inside an interactive list item; it creates nested click targets and confusing focus behavior.
Use a list for a single item or for laying out unrelated content; lists imply a meaningful collection.
Mix clickable and non-clickable items in the same list without clear visual distinction.

props.name: children
props.description: List items (ListItem components).

props.name: density
props.description: Spacing density for items. Under a finger, an interactive row's hit target reaches 44px where its neighbors leave room, with no change to how rows look or lay out.

props.name: hasDividers
props.description: Show dividers between items.

props.name: animatedLayout
props.description: The handle from useAnimatedLayout({containerRef}). With it, when rows are inserted, removed or reordered, an inserted row enters, a removed row collapses in place, a row that crosses rows moving the other way rides above them with the surface color behind it, and the rows after a change and the content after the list, up to that container, glide to their new places, all on one shared motion, under every pointer. Under Reduce Motion nothing travels. A row is identified by its itemKey: a row without one changes at once. Without a handle the list changes at once.

props.name: reorderable
props.description: Makes the rows reorderable, with the object createReorderable({onReorder, isReorderable}) makes: each ListItem with an itemKey gets a reorder handle at its end, and each committed move calls onReorder once with the row's key and its index after the move ({key, to}); render the rows in the new order to apply it. A row the object's isReorderable rejects has no handle and keeps its place; one at either end of the list also bounds the others. The object may be made on every render. On a touch screen, a finger held still on a handle for a moment picks up its row (a flick on it still scrolls): the row stays in its place, dimmed, while a copy of it follows the finger and an accent line marks where it would land; the other rows stay still, the page scrolls near the edges, and on release the rows rearrange, gliding to their new places. A mouse drags a handle at once with the same copy and line, and the rows take their places without motion; a drag reports once, at the drop, and a cancelled drag puts everything back at once. In reorder mode the line marks the row's new place after each move. Without a drag, the handle is a toggle: a click, Space or Enter turns on reorder mode for its row (aria-pressed), in which each Up or Down arrow moves the row a place at once and reports it, and Escape or another activation ends the mode, keeping the moves. Each move is announced once it renders, with the row's place and its neighbours ('Milk, position 3 of 5, after Eggs, before Bread'), and a move into a row that keeps its place is refused and announced. While the mode is on, a hint anchored to the handle shows the moves and Done as buttons that do what the keys do, so a row can also be reordered by taps alone. The object's start(key) enters the same mode from your own UI, such as a row's context menu. A disabled row's handle stays focusable but moves nothing.

props.name: edge
props.description: Where each row's text, dividers, and hover and selection backgrounds sit, relative to the list's edges and the container around it. 'padded' keeps text inside each row's padding, so it starts a little in from a heading above the list and backgrounds have room around it. 'flush' drops the rows' side padding: text starts on the heading's line, and dividers and backgrounds stop at the row's content, with no room beyond it on either side. It works anywhere and suits static rows. 'outset' puts text on the heading's line and reaches dividers and backgrounds a little past it into the container's padding; it suits interactive rows in a container. 'bleed' puts text on the heading's line and reaches dividers and backgrounds to the container's edges, like Table rows in a Card. Rows are square, except that when the list is the first or last child of a rounded Card or Dialog that holds no other Table or bleeding List deeper inside, its first row (when it has no header) or last row takes the container's corner, less the container padding above or below it. A row's first content is what lines up with the heading: its marker, icon, or avatar when it has one, otherwise its label. 'outset' and 'bleed' reach into the padding of the nearest container that shares its padding: a Card, Section, Dialog, or BottomSheet, or a transparent container such as a Layout region with explicit padding or a padded ScrollableArea. Place the List directly in that container's padding: padding that Stack, Center, or your own styles add in between is not counted. Drawers and the automatic padding of LayoutContent and LayoutPanel aren't supported yet. With no such container, including in a Popover, they look like 'padded'. In a container with less padding than the rows' own, text starts a little after the heading's line. A theme's inline padding on `item` replaces the row padding of every value, including the zero padding of flush.

props.name: edgeCompensation
props.description: Deprecated: use edge="outset", which this sets. Still works; edge wins when both are set. `astryx upgrade` rewrites existing usage.

props.name: header
props.description: Header content, associated with the list via aria-labelledby.

props.name: listStyle
props.description: List marker style. 'decimal' renders an <ol> element instead of <ul>.

props.name: start
props.description: Starting number for ordered lists (listStyle='decimal'). Sets the CSS counter to begin at this value.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary content. A plain string gets single-line truncation automatically; a ReactNode renders as given, so child components control their own text behavior.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary content below the label. A plain string gets single-line truncation automatically; a ReactNode lets child components control their own wrapping and line-clamp behavior.

props.name: startContent
props.description: Content rendered before the label area (e.g. icon, avatar).

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content rendered after the label area (e.g. badge, chevron).

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler; enables the invisible button pattern.

props.name: interactiveRef
props.description: Ref to a nested control (e.g. a checkbox in startContent) that owns the item's keyboard access and action. The row becomes an enlarged click/tap target that delegates surface clicks to it (useClickableContainer) and renders no invisible button/anchor, so the row adds no second tab stop (WCAG 4.1.2). Mutually exclusive with onClick/href; those are ignored when set.

props.name: href
props.description: Link URL; enables the invisible anchor pattern. The destination follows the shared navigation rule described on the Link `href` prop.

props.name: target
props.description: Link target attribute, only applicable when href is provided. target="_blank" automatically adds noopener noreferrer.

props.name: rel
props.description: Link relationship tokens. noopener noreferrer are merged automatically for target="_blank".

props.name: align
props.description: Vertical alignment of the start and end content against the label, passed through to Item unchanged. `first-line` keeps a small mark (a status dot, an icon) level with the first line of a wrapped label. See Item.align.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disabled state; sets aria-disabled on the item.

props.name: isSelected
props.description: Selected state; marks the item as the current one with aria-current="true" (a list item cannot carry aria-selected).

props.name: itemKey
props.description: The row's item key, a string or a number from the data (the shape Table's idKey returns). It is the row's identity for the list's animated layout (List animatedLayout): with a handle, the list matches rows by it to animate inserts, removals and moves, and a row without one changes at once. In a reorderable List (List reorderable), it is the key the reorderable object's onReorder reports and isReorderable is asked about, and a row without one has no reorder handle and keeps its place. Separate from React's key.

props.name: swipeActions
props.description: Swipe actions for touch, passed through to Item unchanged: the verbs a sideways drag uncovers on each side, each `{id?, label, icon?, onActivate, isDisabled?, variant?: 'neutral' | 'accent' | 'destructive', hasRemoval?}`. See Item.swipeActions; List clips its rows in the inline axis for them.

props.name: swipeBehavior
props.description: What a swipe does, passed through to Item unchanged. See Item.swipeBehavior.

Markdown.description: Renders a markdown string as Astryx-styled components. Use Markdown for user-generated content, AI responses, and documentation; it handles headings, lists, tables, code blocks, and citations with consistent styling.

practices.text: Set headingLevelStart to match the page hierarchy, e.g. start at 3 if the markdown sits inside an h2 section.
Use contentWidth to keep prose at a readable line length in wide layouts.

Emphasis and strong pair as CommonMark specifies, so *see **bold** more* puts the bold inside the emphasis. ***text*** renders as strong around emphasis, the order RichText draws, and is announced as both. Emphasis nested more than 100 levels deep stays as written text.
Use plugins created by createMarkdownPlugin for reusable syntax, immutable AST transforms, and typed extension rendering. Keep the ordered list stable while its syntax configuration is unchanged.

To render a plugin node outside Markdown, as another surface showing the same document does, read what the plugin declares with getMarkdownPluginCapabilities (syntax and transform, nothing else), and render each parsed extension node with MarkdownPluginNodeRenderer from the client-only @astryxdesign/core/Markdown/plugin-renderer subpath. It presents the node exactly as Markdown does, fallbacks and failure reports included, with no element of its own.

Add markdownSoftBreaksPlugin when single line endings are meaningful. It matches remark-breaks for supported Markdown, including multiline link labels, while code and other opaque content stay unchanged.

Add markdownSourceLinesPlugin when a feature maps the rendered document back to Markdown source lines (find, highlights, review comments). Every block Markdown renders, nested blocks included, then carries data-source-line and data-source-line-end (1-based, inclusive); components block renderers receive sourceLines to place on their own element, and plugin renderers read node.position lines. Inline elements, table rows, and cells carry none. Without the plugin no line work runs.

Use createMarkdownTextTransform for prose matching; it preserves code, links, images, citations, math, and accepted extension syntax as protected contexts. Provide requiredSubstrings only when they conservatively cover every possible match.

Use createMarkdownFenceTransform for declared code-fence languages with semantic data. createNode returns an owned block extension node; its standard plugin renderer and toText own presentation. A claimed fence renders through that plugin even when components.code is supplied; components.code renders every unclaimed fence and is the fallback when the plugin renderer declines, throws, or suspends, and without it the accessible, copyable CodeBlock is that fallback.

Use createMarkdownSourceDecoration to attach non-visual metadata — search hits, review annotations — to the blocks a source range touches, and getMarkdownSourceDecorations to read it back in a later plugin. Decorations appear on the settled document rather than on partial streaming chunks, and never change rendering, copyable text, accessible names, ids, focus order, or navigation.

Import parseMarkdownAst or parseInlineAst from @astryxdesign/core/Markdown/parser when server or React Server Component code needs to run plugins against the canonical readonly tree. The parser and plugin subpaths have no use-client boundary. The Markdown component remains client-owned, so function-bearing plugin entries must not be passed across an RSC serialization boundary.

Use decodeMarkdownCharacterReferences (from @astryxdesign/core/Markdown/parser or @astryxdesign/core/Markdown) to show text the way Markdown renders its character references: ©, ©, and © become ©, while unknown names and references without their semicolon stay as written. It decodes plain text and knows nothing of Markdown, so skip code and backslash-escaped references yourself. It uses the same table Markdown renders with.

Use createMarkdownFrontmatter for typed document metadata. Its parse() method gives the host metadata directly; its plugin removes a complete leading block before rendering and withholds an unfinished block during streaming.

Import createMarkdownRemarkTransform from '@astryxdesign/core/Markdown/remark' only to reuse an existing synchronous transform-only Remark plugin; it stays out of every other bundle. Prove each plugin with fixtures: anything outside the supported MDAST subset — async work, parser or compiler plugins, processor state, raw HTML, unsupported nodes, forged positions, or metadata Astryx cannot represent — keeps the last valid document and reports one diagnostic.
Use inlinePlugins for prefixed identifiers, mentions, and other prose-only shorthand instead of preprocessing the markdown string.
Provide components.math only for documents that use dollar-delimited math. The renderer owns typesetting and accessible output; Astryx passes the expression as text and never executes raw HTML.

For direct parsing, use MathParseOptions and handle InlineNodeWithMath or BlockNodeWithMath. Incremental math parsing also uses createIncrementalState<true>() and IncrementalParseState<true>; default calls and ParseOptions annotations keep the legacy unions.

Install createMarkdownHeadingLinks() through plugins when a document needs copyable h1–h6 permalinks. The returned entry carries its validated namespace and URL base across compatible Core package copies. Each built-in heading keeps its incoming fragment ID and gains an inline trailing # copy button: it is hidden at fine-pointer rest through useContainerReveal, reveals on heading-row hover or keyboard focus, and stays visible under the hook’s coarse/touch semantics. Unmodified tap, click, Enter, or Space copies the canonical URL without navigation, hash mutation, or scrolling; a check confirms success for 1.5 seconds. The no-plugin path stays unchanged, and nested headings use the same depth-first identity projection as Markdown-derived Outline.

For multiple documents, create one heading-links plugin per document with headingIdPrefix and pass that same plugin to Markdown and useOutlineFromMarkdown. Use the same stable value for Markdown id when the root also needs a DOM id; permalinkBaseUrl may supply a safe caller-owned URL before the fragment.
Use Markdown for hand-authored layouts; use Text and Heading directly when you control the content.

props.name: children
props.description: The markdown string to render.

props.name: display
props.description: Display type. Markdown defaults to block. Use 'inline' for markdown spans embedded inside text.

props.name: density
props.description: Controls spacing between block-level elements.

props.name: headingLevelStart
props.description: The HTML heading level that markdown # maps to. Shifts all heading levels down to fit the surrounding page hierarchy. Levels exceeding h6 are clamped to h6.

props.name: isStreaming
props.description: Enables streaming mode; it uses incremental parsing and a smooth fade-in animation for chunk-by-chunk text delivery.

props.name: onLinkClick
props.description: Handler for link clicks. Return false to prevent the default navigation behavior. Link destinations in the markdown follow the shared navigation rule described on the Link `href` prop: a blocked destination renders as plain text and never reaches this handler or a custom link renderer. Image URLs use a separate, stricter policy (every data: URL is rejected).

props.name: sources
props.description: Citation sources keyed by ID. When provided, [id] and 【id】 markers in the markdown that match a key are rendered as citation chips.

props.name: citationStyle
props.description: How citations are displayed inline. 'label' shows a chip with source title, icon, and border. 'number' shows a compact numbered badge.

props.name: contentWidth
props.description: Max width for prose content (paragraphs, headings, lists, blockquotes). Tables and code blocks are unconstrained and can expand to the full container width. Use for readable line lengths in wide layouts.

props.name: contentAlign
props.description: Alignment of prose content within the container when contentWidth is narrower than the available space.

props.name: plugins
props.description: Ordered extensions created by createMarkdownPlugin(). Plugins may add bounded syntax, immutable typed AST transforms, and typed extension renderers. Use isMarkdownExtensionNode() to narrow extension data observed from other plugins. Renderer callbacks are pure; return a child component when hooks are needed. Omitted and empty lists preserve the released Markdown behavior.

props.name: inlinePlugins
props.description: Transforms regex matches in parsed text nodes into custom inline React elements. Use for prefixed identifiers, mentions, and other shorthand patterns. Inline code, fenced code blocks, and math are unaffected.

props.name: autolink
props.description: Opt-in autolinking of bare URLs and emails. 'gfm' applies GitHub-Flavored Markdown autolink-literal rules: bare https?://..., www...., <scheme:url>, <email>, and user@host all become links. Trailing sentence punctuation and unbalanced trailing close-parens are excluded; matches inside code spans, code blocks, existing links, and image alt text are skipped. Default behavior (option unset) is unchanged.

props.name: codeLanguages
props.description: CodeBlock language values a fence may name, each imported on its own (e.g. graphql from @astryxdesign/core/CodeBlock/languages/graphql) or made with createCodeLanguage. A fence whose language word is one of a listed value's identifiers renders with it, ahead of a built-in; a diff-<identifier> fence takes the diff layer over it; a later entry wins. Pass the same list to RichTextEditor or RichTextView so read and edit match.

props.name: components
props.description: Custom React component overrides for rendered Markdown elements (code, inlineCode, math, link, heading, paragraph, image, blockquote, hr, citation). Providing math enables `$…$` inline and `$$…$$` display parsing and receives `{value, display}`; omit it when dollar text should stay literal.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling; className is provided for integration with non-StyleX systems.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling; inline styles bypass StyleX optimization.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

MetadataList.description: MetadataList displays key-value pairs for object attributes like quality, condition, and status, in a structured layout. Use it for detail panels, settings summaries, and record information.

practices.text: Choose label position based on content: "start" for short values, "top" for long or complex values.
Collapse long lists with `maxNumOfItems` to keep the page scannable.
Use for extensive form input; use a form layout instead.
Use for data that doesn't have a clear key-value structure.

props.name: children
props.description: Metadata items (MetadataListItem components).

props.name: columns
props.description: Column layout mode.

props.name: label
props.description: Label display configuration. position controls label placement, width sets a custom label column width. Defaults to { position: 'top' } for multi-column layouts. Position is ignored in horizontal mode, which always uses { position: 'top' }.

props.name: maxNumOfItems
props.description: Maximum items to show before collapsing with a show more/less toggle.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Layout orientation. Horizontal mode flows items in a row with flex-wrap.

props.name: title
props.description: Optional title or heading above the list.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

props.name: children
props.description: Content value for this metadata item.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for this metadata item.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon rendered before the label text.

MoreMenu.description: MoreMenu is a three-dot button that opens a list of actions. Use it for secondary actions that don't need to be always visible, like in table rows, card headers, or toolbars.

practices.text: Use for overflow or secondary actions; keep primary actions visible outside the menu.
Use dividers or sections to group related actions when the menu has many items.
Use `presentation="adaptive"` when the visible overflow trigger should open a thumb-reachable BottomSheet on compact touch devices.
Hide primary actions inside a MoreMenu; they should be directly visible.

props.name: items
props.description: Menu items: data array of actions, dividers, and sections. Same type as DropdownMenu items prop.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the trigger button (aria-label) and tooltip text.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual style variant of the trigger button.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the trigger button.

props.name: icon
props.description: Override the default three-dot icon. Accepts any ReactNode.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the menu trigger is disabled.

props.name: placement
props.description: Position of the menu relative to the trigger. Logical: start/end resolve against the menu's own inherited direction (RTL mirrors).

props.name: alignment
props.description: Alignment along the placement axis. Use 'end' to align the menu with the trigger's trailing edge, which is usually what an overflow menu wants.

props.name: presentation
props.description: Presentation policy forwarded to DropdownMenu. `adaptive` keeps the anchored popover on pointer-based layouts and uses a BottomSheet on a compact touch screen: a coarse primary pointer, and a viewport narrower than the theme `md` breakpoint (768px by default) or shorter than 500px. Omitted, the menu is the anchored popover, and under a finger, on every device, the finger that opened it picks a row only after moving 10 px. Pass 'popover' to keep the pointer behavior on every device, the settle rule included.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback fired when the menu opens or closes.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

MobileNav.description: A slide-out drawer for mobile navigation. MobileNav is the mobile counterpart to SideNav and accepts the same children. Use it on narrow viewports where a persistent sidebar is not practical. Inside AppShell, use MobileNavToggle as the trigger; it reads state from context automatically.

practices.text: Share the same nav items between MobileNav and SideNav by extracting them into a variable.
Provide a header when the drawer's purpose is not obvious from its content.
Inside AppShell, use MobileNavToggle to open the drawer; it reads state from context. Do not pass isOpen/onOpenChange to the toggle.
Use MobileNav on desktop: use a persistent SideNav instead.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Whether the drawer is open. Inside AppShell, this is managed automatically via context. Outside AppShell, provide this prop to control the drawer yourself.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the drawer visibility changes (backdrop click, Escape key, or close button). Inside AppShell, this is managed automatically via context. On a phone or tablet (a coarse primary pointer), the drawer takes no tap or drag while it slides in; keys and assistive technology still act. After a close, focus returns to the element that opened it once its dialog closes.

props.name: children
props.description: Drawer content: typically SideNavSection/SideNavItem, or any ReactNode.

props.name: header
props.description: Header content for the drawer. Rendered next to the close button. Pass a string for a simple text heading, or a ReactNode for custom content (logo, search bar, etc.).

props.name: width
props.description: Drawer width in pixels. Capped at 85vw to prevent overflow on small screens.

props.name: side
props.description: Which side the drawer slides from. Start is left in LTR, right in RTL. Auto picks a side based on the trigger position.

props.name: children
props.description: Custom content to render instead of the default hamburger icon.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the toggle button.

NavIcon.description: NavIcon is a circular icon container with an accent-colored background. Use it in navigation headers such as TopNavHeading and PageNavHeader to visually identify a section or application.

practices.text: Use in navigation headers to provide a recognizable visual anchor for the section.
Pass an Icon or similarly sized icon component to ensure proper proportions.
Use NavIcon for interactive purposes; it is a display-only container, not a button.

props.name: icon
props.description: The icon element to render inside the circular background. Should be an Icon or similar icon component.

SideNav.description: A sidebar navigation component for organizing application pages with sections, nested items, and icons. Use SideNav as the primary navigation when an app has 5 or more destinations or requires hierarchical grouping.

practices.text: Use sections to group related navigation items and help users scan for their destination.
Pair outline and filled icon variants so the selected state is visually distinct.
Mark the current page with isSelected: it sets aria-current="page", so the current destination is announced rather than carried by color alone.

SideNav renders a navigation landmark, and a collapsible item follows the WAI-ARIA APG Disclosure pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/): the toggle carries aria-expanded and aria-controls, and the group it owns is inert while collapsed. Keep item labels short; they name icon-only items unless a meaningful aria-label supplies more context.

While the nav is collapsed, an item with children shows them in a submenu flyout. On a device that can hover, pointing at the item opens it after a short delay and moving away closes it; a flyout opened by clicking stays open until it is dismissed. On touch, it opens on tap. Do not put an action in there that has no other route to it.
Include a SideNavHeading when a TopNav is already providing app identity; this duplicates branding.
Use for filtering content; use tabs or filter buttons instead.

props.name: header
props.description: Header area (typically SideNavHeading). Sticky.

props.name: topContent
props.description: Content below the header, e.g., a create button.

props.name: children
props.description: Navigation sections and items. Scrollable.

props.name: footer
props.description: Footer area above the icon bar.

props.name: footerIcons
props.description: Footer icon bar. The row cascades a 'sm' size to the interactive children it contains, so its icons and the built-in collapse button come out one height; pass an explicit size on a child to opt out.

props.name: collapsible
props.type: boolean | { defaultIsCollapsed?: boolean; isCollapsed?: boolean; onCollapsedChange?: (isCollapsed: boolean) => void; hasButton?: boolean; buttonLabel?: string }
props.description: Enables collapse behavior. true for uncontrolled with default toggle button, or an object for controlled mode and advanced config (defaultIsCollapsed, isCollapsed + onCollapsedChange, hasButton, buttonLabel). A controlled config can also be passed to a SideNavCollapseButton rendered outside this SideNav, so both share one state.

props.name: resizable
props.type: boolean | { defaultWidth?: number; minWidth?: number; maxWidth?: number; autoSaveId?: string; onWidthChange?: (width: number) => void; defaultIsCollapsed?: boolean; isCollapsed?: boolean; onCollapseChange?: (isCollapsed: boolean) => void } | ResizableRegion
props.description: Enables a resize handle at the inline-end edge. true for defaults (260px initial, 180-480px range), or a ResizableConfig object (defaultWidth, minWidth, maxWidth, autoSaveId for localStorage persistence of width and collapse state, onWidthChange). It can also own collapse state (defaultIsCollapsed, isCollapsed + onCollapseChange); when both props carry collapse state, resizable wins and a dev warning names the conflicting keys. It also takes the output of useResizable(), whose axis ('horizontal' | 'vertical') must be 'horizontal': that region then owns the width and the collapse state, so the rail follows its isCollapsed, the toggle calls its collapse and expand, and its autoSaveId saves the width. With the hook's output, the region's own collapsible option also decides whether the rail collapses; a collapsible prop that disagrees, or the collapse state it sets, is ignored, with a dev warning. The handle is hidden while collapsed.

props.name: handleRef
props.description: Deprecated. Imperative collapse handle for SideNavCollapseButton instances rendered outside this SideNav; hand both the same controlled collapsible config instead. Separate from `ref`, which continues to expose the root HTMLElement.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: collapsible
props.type: {isCollapsed: boolean, onCollapsedChange: (isCollapsed: boolean) => void, defaultIsCollapsed?: boolean, hasButton?: boolean, buttonLabel?: string}
props.description: The same controlled collapsible config passed to SideNav, with all its keys. Only needed when the button is rendered outside the sidenav, where collapse context cannot reach it.

props.name: handleRef
props.description: Deprecated. Imperative collapse handle from SideNav; pass collapsible instead.

props.name: label
props.description: Custom button label. When provided, renders as a text button with chevron. When omitted, renders icon-only.

props.name: size
props.description: Button size. Defaults to the size its container cascades ('sm' inside a SideNav footer) and to 'md' with no container. Set it when the button sits outside a sized container and has to match its neighbours.

props.name: children
props.description: Custom button content. Overrides the default chevron icon and label.

props.name: heading
props.description: Product/app name.

props.name: icon
props.description: Product/app icon.

props.name: headingHref
props.description: Link for the heading.

props.name: superheading
props.description: Text above the heading.

props.name: superheadingHref
props.description: Link for the superheading.

props.name: subheading
props.description: Text below the heading.

props.name: subheadingHref
props.description: Link for the subheading.

props.name: menu
props.description: Menu content rendered inside a popover.

props.name: headerEndContent
props.description: Content rendered at the trailing edge of the heading row, between text and chevron. Useful for badges, status indicators, or compact action buttons. Hidden when collapsed.

props.name: label
props.description: Item label.

props.name: as
props.description: Custom link component.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon displayed in the outline (unselected) variant. See `astryx docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: selectedIcon
props.description: Icon displayed when the item is selected (filled variant). See `astryx docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: isSelected
props.description: Marks this item as the current page.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disabled state.

props.name: href
props.description: Navigation URL.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Passive right-side content only (badges, counts). Interactive controls go in actions.

props.name: actions
props.description: Row-level secondary controls (icon buttons, menus) rendered as siblings of the primary element at the trailing edge of the row: after the expand/collapse toggle, before any nested children in DOM and focus order. Each control owns its accessible name and behavior. Controls inherit the row control size through SizeContext, so an unsized icon button matches the built-in expand/collapse toggle; an explicit size still wins. Hidden while the SideNav rail is collapsed. Use endContent for passive content (badges, counts); use actions for anything interactive.

props.name: children
props.description: Sub-items for nesting. Nested items span the full width of the nav list, like top-level items; their content is indented one step per nesting level.

props.name: collapsible
props.type: boolean | { defaultIsCollapsed?: boolean, isCollapsed?: boolean, onCollapsedChange?: (isCollapsed: boolean) => void }
props.description: Enables collapse behavior for items with children. Pass true for uncontrolled (starts expanded), or an object for controlled mode.

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant for the nav item row.

props.name: title
props.description: Section title.

props.name: subtitle
props.description: Section subtitle.

props.name: children
props.description: Section items.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Right-side content in the section header.

props.name: isHeaderHidden
props.description: Visually hides the section header while keeping it accessible to screen readers.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

TopNav.description: TopNav is a horizontal navigation bar for product-level navigation in application headers. Use TopNav for 5 or fewer always-visible navigation items, or minimal navigation paired with search and controls. For complex navigation hierarchies, use a sidebar; to filter content, use tabs or filter buttons instead.

practices.text: Include a product logo and name in the heading slot to clearly identify the application.
Limit primary navigation items to 5 or fewer for quick scanning and minimal cognitive load.
Avoid using TopNav to filter page content; use Tabs or filter controls instead.
Avoid deeply nested navigation hierarchies; keep menus to one level of depth.

props.name: heading
props.description: Heading slot content (logo, brand): positioned at the left edge of the nav bar.

props.name: startContent
props.description: Start content slot for navigation items or breadcrumbs: positioned after the heading, left-aligned.

props.name: children
props.description: Alias for startContent. Prefer startContent when composing with heading, centerContent, or endContent; children keeps the common React nav-item pattern from silently dropping items.

props.name: centerContent
props.description: Center content slot (tabs, search bar, primary navigation): when provided, switches the layout to three regions that keep it at the middle of the bar while they fit one row; the bar wraps when they do not.

props.name: endContent
props.description: End content slot for search, icons, or user profile: positioned at the right edge.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the navigation landmark, applied as aria-label on the <nav> element.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: logo
props.description: Logo element to display before the heading text. Can be an image, NavIcon, or any ReactNode.

props.name: heading
props.description: Product/app name displayed as the primary heading text.

props.name: headingHref
props.description: Link for the heading text (e.g. product home). When no menu is present and this is the only href, the whole heading becomes one clickable link.

props.name: superheading
props.description: Text above the heading (e.g. suite name). Rendered in a smaller secondary style.

props.name: superheadingHref
props.description: Link for the superheading text (e.g. suite home). When provided alongside a menu, renders as an independent inline link.

props.name: subheading
props.description: Text below the heading (e.g. account context). Rendered in a smaller secondary style.

props.name: subheadingHref
props.description: Link for the subheading text. When provided alongside a menu, renders as an independent inline link.

props.name: headerEndContent
props.description: Content rendered at the trailing edge of the heading row (e.g. a badge or status indicator).

props.name: menu
props.description: Menu content shown in a popover dropdown. When provided, a chevron indicator appears automatically. Interaction boundary is determined by the presence of hrefs: no hrefs means the whole header is the trigger; with hrefs, links are independent and the chevron area is the trigger.

props.name: as
props.description: Custom component to render instead of <a>. Overrides the provider-level default set by LinkProvider. Must accept href, className, style, and children props.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the nav item. Rendered as visible text by default. When isIconOnly is true, used as aria-label instead.

props.name: href
props.description: Navigation target URL.

props.name: isSelected
props.description: Whether this nav item is currently selected. Sets aria-current="page" and applies highlighted styles.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the nav item is disabled. Sets aria-disabled, drops href/target so the item cannot navigate, and prevents interaction.

props.name: isIconOnly
props.description: Renders the item as a square icon-only element. When true, label becomes the aria-label and visible text is hidden. Requires icon to be set.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon to display before the label.

props.name: children
props.description: Custom content to render instead of the label text.

props.name: as
props.description: Custom component to render instead of <a>. Overrides the provider-level default set by LinkProvider. Must accept href, className, style, and children props.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label for the trigger button.

props.name: items
props.description: Menu items slot: typically TopNavMegaMenuItem components, but accepts any ReactNode.

props.name: featured
props.description: Featured content slot: rendered in the right panel on desktop, below items in the mobile drawer.

props.name: delay
props.description: Delay in milliseconds before showing the menu on hover.

props.name: hideDelay
props.description: Delay in milliseconds before hiding the menu after the mouse leaves.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback fired when the mega menu opens or closes. Useful for coordinating wrapper styles.

props.name: title
props.description: Card title.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text below the title.

props.name: image
props.description: Optional image URL displayed above the body.

props.name: imageAlt
props.description: Alt text for the image. When omitted, the image is explicitly decorative (alt="", role="presentation", aria-hidden), usually correct since the card already has a visible title. Provide it only when the image conveys information beyond the title and description.

props.name: linkLabel
props.description: CTA link text.

props.name: linkHref
props.description: CTA link URL.

props.name: children
props.description: Custom content rendered below the standard body.

props.name: title
props.description: Display title for the menu item.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional description text displayed below the title.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon element displayed to the left.

props.name: href
props.description: URL to navigate to when clicked.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Callback when item is clicked.

props.name: as
props.description: Custom component to render instead of <a> for link items. Overrides the provider-level default set by LinkProvider.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label for the trigger button.

props.name: items
props.description: Menu items to display in the hover popover. Item href values follow the shared navigation rule described on Link; rejected destinations remain visible without navigation.

props.name: delay
props.description: Delay in milliseconds before showing the menu on hover.

props.name: hideDelay
props.description: Delay in milliseconds before hiding the menu after the mouse leaves.

NumberInput.description: A form input for numeric values with built-in validation, min/max constraints, and step controls. Use NumberInput for quantities, measurements, percentages, and similar inputs.

practices.text: Let people paste formatted numbers: a pasted 1,234,234,234 is read under the field's locale and commits as 1234234234 on blur. Typing is never intercepted.
Set min, max, and step to guide users toward valid values.
Show units (e.g. "%" or "GB") so users know what the number represents.
Set isWheelEnabled={false} when the input appears in a scrolling surface where wheel gestures should always scroll the page.
Use NumberInput for free-form text that happens to contain numbers; use TextInput instead.
Set both isOptional and isRequired on the same field.
Wrap a disabled NumberInput in Tooltip to explain why it's disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop, which attaches the reason to the field itself.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the input (always rendered for accessibility).

props.name: value
props.description: Current value of the input.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when a valid text edit commits on blur or Enter, or when a step or clear control changes the value.

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hide the label (still accessible to screen readers).

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed between the label and input.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Whether the field is optional (mutually exclusive with isRequired).

props.name: onKeyDown
props.description: Callback fired on keydown events on the input.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Whether the field is required (mutually exclusive with isOptional).

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the input is disabled.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: Makes the input read-only: the value is shown at full opacity and still submits with the form, but cannot be edited. Unlike isDisabled, a read-only input is not dimmed and keeps its form value. Stepping is off in every form while read-only: arrow keys, the wheel, and the number steppers. isDisabled takes precedence when both are set.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the input is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the input focusable via aria-disabled (the field becomes read-only). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled NumberInput in Tooltip.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text to display in an info icon at the end of the label.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon to display at the start of the input. See `astryx docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: labelIcon
props.description: Icon to display before the label text. See `astryx docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status with optional message.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip hides the message box and surfaces it in a tooltip on the status icon.

props.name: min
props.description: Minimum value allowed. A smaller entry commits at this value on blur or Enter.

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum value allowed. A larger entry commits at this value on blur or Enter.

props.name: step
props.description: Step increment for the input.

props.name: formatValue
props.description: Formats the committed value while the input is not focused. The raw numeric value is shown on focus for editing and the formatted value is exposed through aria-valuetext.

props.name: isWheelEnabled
props.description: Whether scrolling the wheel over the focused input steps the value. Disable this when page scrolling should always take priority.

props.name: hasNumberSteppers
props.description: Shows increment and decrement buttons at the end of the input on fine pointers. Hidden on coarse pointers (such as touch screens); text entry and keyboard stepping remain available. Holding a button with a mouse or a pen repeats the step and commits once, when the hold ends.

props.name: units
props.description: Units text to display at the end of the input (e.g., "%" or "GB").

props.name: isIntegerOnly
props.description: Only allow integer values (no floating point).

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Shows a clear (×) button when the input has a value. When true, the onChange callback also accepts null to signal the user cleared the input.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: HTML name attribute for form submissions.

props.name: autoComplete
props.description: HTML autocomplete attribute.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Whether to focus the input on mount.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Callback fired when the input receives focus.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Callback fired when the input loses focus.

props.name: onEnter
props.description: Callback fired when the user presses the Enter key.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the element that paints the border and background and holds icons and end controls. Never the native input.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Class name for the visual control box.

props.name: controlStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the visual control box.

Outline.description: A table-of-contents sidebar for documentation pages, help centers, wikis, and long settings pages. Use it for navigation within a single page, not for app routes. Features a sliding indicator track that animates to the active heading. Each link is in the normal Tab order, and Enter/Space activate.

practices.text: Pass a flat ordered list of headings and let level control indentation.
Use activeId when custom scroll logic owns the active section.
Use density="compact" in dense sidebars where vertical space is tight.

Use useOutlineFromMarkdown or useOutlineFromDOM when headings are generated from content. For linkable Markdown headings, pass the same createMarkdownHeadingLinks() entry to Markdown and Outline; configure headingIdPrefix on that plugin for multiple roots.
Pass scrollContainerRef when the content scrolls in a split pane, modal, or panel instead of the viewport.
Set offset to the height of a fixed header that overlays the content, so headings land below it instead of underneath it.
Use Outline for application navigation - use SideNav or TopNav for routes.
Use Outline for expandable hierarchy - use TreeList when nodes need expand and collapse.
Rely on onNavigateEnd to mean "arrived" - it also fires when the user interrupts the scroll.

props.name: items
props.description: Ordered heading items. Each item has id, label, and level (1-6). The id should match the target heading element id.

props.name: activeId
props.description: Currently active heading id. Providing this prop makes active state controlled and disables built-in scroll-spy.

props.name: onActiveIdChange
props.description: Called when the active item changes from built-in scroll-spy or from an outline link click.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the nav landmark.

props.name: density
props.description: Density variant controlling item padding. 'compact' for dense UIs, 'default' for standard spacing.

props.name: onNavigateStart
props.description: Called with the item id when navigation begins, before the scroll starts. Pair with onNavigateEnd to drive an arrival effect (flash, ring, pulse) on the target heading.

props.name: onNavigateEnd
props.description: Called with the item id once the navigation resolves - when the smooth scroll settles, or when reduced motion turns it into an instant jump. Fires exactly once per onNavigateStart, including when the user interrupts the scroll, so a "navigating" state can never leak.

props.name: offset
props.description: Height in px of a fixed header overlaying the top of the scroll root. Shifts both the activation line and the scroll landing by the same amount, so a heading activates exactly where navigating to it puts it - below the header, not underneath it. Composes with each heading's own scroll-margin-top (the header, then the breathing room below it); it does not replace it. Leave at 0 when nothing overlays the content and let scroll-margin-top do the work.

props.name: scrollContainerRef
props.description: Scroll container to track, instead of auto-detecting the nearest scrollable ancestor. Use it when content scrolls inside a split pane, modal, or dashboard panel rather than the viewport.

props.name: hasScrollOnClick
props.description: Whether activating an item smooth-scrolls to it. Set to false to own the scrolling yourself (virtualized content, a router): the Outline still updates the active item, the hash, and the navigate callbacks, but performs no scroll.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

OverflowList.description: A horizontal list that automatically hides items when they exceed the available width. Use OverflowList for breadcrumbs, toolbars, tag lists, or any row that needs to collapse gracefully at smaller sizes.

practices.text: Provide a meaningful overflowRenderer: a "+N more" badge, a dropdown, or a count indicator.
When the row already has its own menu, use onOverflowChange to feed the collapsed items into it instead of adding a second anchor with overflowRenderer.
Set minVisibleItems to keep key items visible, and maxVisibleItems to cap the row at a fixed count regardless of available width.
Use maxRows to let items wrap onto a bounded number of rows (e.g. a two-row tag cloud) before collapsing the rest into the indicator.
Use OverflowList for a vertical stack; horizontal multi-row wrap is supported via maxRows, but items still flow left-to-right, not top-to-bottom.

props.name: children
props.description: Items to render. Each child should be a single element.

props.name: overflowRenderer
props.description: Render function for the overflow indicator. Receives the list of hidden items (each with child and index). Only called when items are overflowing.

props.name: onOverflowChange
props.description: Called whenever the collapsed set changes: with the collapsed items once something collapses, and with an empty array once the row widens back out. Membership and order changes report even when the count stays the same; unrelated re-renders and callback identity changes do not. Silent while nothing overflows, including on mount. Use stable React keys for dynamic items.

props.name: gap
props.description: Gap between items as a spacing token step (0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10).

props.name: minVisibleItems
props.description: Minimum number of items to always show, even when overflowing.

props.name: maxVisibleItems
props.description: Maximum number of items to ever show, even when they all fit. The ceiling partner to minVisibleItems; extra items collapse into the overflow indicator. If less than minVisibleItems, the floor wins.

props.name: maxRows
props.description: Wrap items across up to this many rows before collapsing the rest into the overflow indicator. A number, not a boolean. Leave undefined (or set 1) for single-line behavior. Assumes uniform row height.

props.name: collapseFrom
props.description: Which end to collapse items from when overflow occurs.

props.name: behavior
props.description: Controls which element is measured for available width. 'observeSelf' uses the container's own width. 'observeParent' observes the parent element, useful when the list should stay content-sized while still detecting available space.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object.

Overlay.description: Overlay layers action or supporting content over media, cards, video, or other bounded surfaces with an optional scrim and reveal behavior. Host attributes and DOM handlers (id, data-*, aria-*) reach the root element.

practices.text: Use overlays for short, contextual actions or labels that belong directly to the underlying media or surface.
Keep overlay content compact so it remains legible over the scrim and does not obscure important visual information.
Do not use Overlay for floating content anchored outside the surface. Use Popover, Tooltip, or Dialog for those patterns.

props.name: content
props.description: Content rendered inside the overlay scrim.

props.name: children
props.description: Base content such as an image, video, card, or media surface that the overlay sits on top of.

props.name: showOn
props.description: Visibility trigger. Hover mode also reveals on focus for keyboard accessibility; hover-or-focus is an alias for hover.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Controlled visibility override. When set, this takes precedence over showOn and touch toggle behavior.

props.name: scrim
props.description: Scrim background mode. Set to false to render overlay content without a scrim background.

props.name: position
props.description: Where the scrim appears within the base surface.

props.name: align
props.description: Alignment of the overlay content within the scrim.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name(s) appended to the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling when possible.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles applied to the root element. Prefer xstyle for design-system styling.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the overlay root element.

Pagination.description: Pagination lets users step through pages of content. Place it below a table, list, or card grid so users can move forward and backward through results. Pick a variant to match the context: numbered pages for data tables, a count for large lists, compact for tight spaces, or dots for carousels.

practices.text: Place pagination below the content it controls so users see results before navigating.
Use the pages variant for data tables where users need to jump to a specific page.
Use the count variant with a page size selector when users need to control how many items they see at once.
Use the dots variant for carousels and walkthroughs where the total is small and position matters more than a number.
Pass totalItems when the total is known so users can see how much content remains.
Show pagination when all items fit on a single page; there is nothing to paginate.
Use the dots variant for more than about 10 pages; the dots become too small to be useful.
Place pagination above the content; users expect it at the bottom.

props.name: page
props.description: Current page number (1-based). Page 1 is the first page.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when the page changes.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action on page change. Fires after onChange and uses React transitions for built-in loading state.

props.name: totalItems
props.description: Total number of items. Used to calculate page count. Takes precedence over totalPages if both provided.

props.name: totalPages
props.description: Total number of pages. Use when you know page count but not item count.

props.name: hasMore
props.description: Whether more pages exist after the current one. Use for cursor-based pagination where total is unknown.

props.name: pageSize
props.description: Number of items per page. Coerced to a positive integer; non-finite values fall back to the default.

props.name: pageSizeOptions
props.description: Available page size options. Shows a page size selector dropdown when provided.

props.name: onPageSizeChange
props.description: Called when the page size changes. Automatically resets to page 1.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual variant controlling what appears between prev/next buttons. 'pages' shows page number buttons with ellipsis, 'count' shows 'X-Y of Z' text, 'compact' shows 'Page X of Y' (add first/last buttons with hasFirstLast), 'dots' shows dot indicators, 'input' shows an editable page-number box with a leading label ('Page [ n ] / N') flanked by first/last buttons by default (the box needs a known total to clamp against, so it is disabled in cursor/hasMore mode), 'none' shows just prev/next buttons.

props.name: pageLabel
props.description: The noun rendered before the editable box in the 'input' variant, e.g. 'Page' or 'Row'. Navigation is always page-based (via onChange); this only relabels the box. Defaults to the localized 'Page'.

props.name: hasFirstLast
props.description: Whether to show first/last («/») double-chevron buttons flanking prev/next. Applies to the 'input' variant (shown unless false) and the 'compact' variant (shown only when true); other variants ignore it. Omitted when the page count is unknown (cursor/hasMore pagination).

props.name: step
props.description: Number of pages the previous/next buttons advance per click. Clamped to the valid page range, so a step that would overshoot lands on the first/last page. When greater than 1, the buttons' accessible names reflect the stride. Non-integer or values < 1 fall back to 1.

props.name: siblingCount
props.description: Number of page buttons to show on each side of the current page. Only applies when variant='pages'.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the pagination controls.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the component is disabled.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the navigation landmark.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

Popover.description: A click-triggered overlay anchored to a button or trigger element. Use it for secondary actions, inline confirmations, or supplementary information that does not warrant a full dialog. For hover previews use HoverCard, for brief helper text use Tooltip.
