Under a finger (a coarse primary pointer), it is presented like a native popover: it grows out of its trigger and shrinks back into it on the theme’s motion tokens; with reduced motion it cross-fades, opacity only, in 200 ms or less.

practices.text: Keep popover content focused on a single task or piece of information.
Provide a clear way to close: either by clicking outside or with an explicit close button.
Theme the painted surface through the canonical popover target.
Nest popovers inside other popovers; it creates confusing focus and navigation.
Assume input complexity alone determines the presentation; evaluate the task's focus, space, and interaction requirements.
Assume scrolling alone means Popover is the wrong component; a bounded Popover may scroll while a focused anchored interaction remains appropriate.

props.name: children
props.description: Trigger element. Must contain a <button> or [role="button"] element.

props.name: anchorRef
props.description: External ref to use as the popover anchor in sibling mode.

props.name: content
props.description: Content to display inside the popover.

props.name: placement
props.description: Position placement relative to the trigger. Logical: start/end resolve against the popover's own inherited direction, so RTL contexts mirror automatically in pure CSS.

props.name: alignment
props.description: Alignment along the placement axis. Logical: start/end follow the popover's own inherited direction (RTL mirrors).

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Whether the popover is shown in controlled mode.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback fired when the popover visibility changes.

props.name: isEnabled
props.description: When false, trigger interactions are ignored.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the popover container. The layer still caps to the viewport with alignment-aware safe-area gutters before scrolling long content.

props.name: padding
props.description: Inner padding of the popover surface on the spacing scale (0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10), matching the padding prop on Card and Stack. Pass 0 for a flush surface when the content owns its own edges, such as a list of rows or a header with a rule, and pad the content itself. The padding sits on the painted popover target, so a theme padding on that target replaces it.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the popover dialog. A sheet without one is named by the trigger’s text.

props.name: role
props.description: ARIA role for the popover wrapper. Use dialog for dialog-style popovers; use none when content provides its own role, like menu or listbox.

props.name: isModal
props.description: Whether a dialog-style popover sets aria-modal. Only applies when role is dialog.

props.name: hasCloseButton
props.description: Whether to include a hidden close button for accessibility.

props.name: closeButtonLabel
props.description: Label for the hidden close button.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Whether to move focus into the popover when it opens. Focus enters the first genuine content control; dialogs with none fall back to the labeled surface. The generated fallback close control stays hidden until reached through keyboard navigation. Set to false for input-owned focus, inline showcases, or documentation previews.

props.name: hasLightDismiss
props.description: Whether clicking outside dismisses the popover. Set to false for surfaces that stay open until explicitly dismissed, like onboarding coachmarks.

props.name: hasEscapeDismiss
props.description: Whether pressing Escape dismisses the popover. Only takes full effect together with hasLightDismiss={false}, since native light dismiss also closes on Escape.

props.name: presentation
props.description: The surface that holds the content. 'popover' anchors it to the trigger, 'bottom-sheet' presents it in a modal BottomSheet labeled by label, and 'adaptive' uses the BottomSheet on a compact touch screen (a coarse pointer on a screen the theme counts as compact: narrower than its md width point or shorter than 500 px, so a phone in either orientation) and the anchored popover elsewhere. In a sheet, placement, alignment, width, role, isModal and hasAutoFocus do not apply, and xstyle, className and style style the sheet's panel; the sheet always light-dismisses (a tap outside it or a swipe down closes it, whatever hasLightDismiss says), Escape follows hasEscapeDismiss, and the fallback close stays hidden. The surface is chosen as it opens and kept until it closes.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

PowerSearch.description: PowerSearch is a structured filter bar where each token represents a field, operator, and value. Use it for complex multi-dimensional filtering when users need to combine multiple search criteria. For simple single-field search, use a text input instead.

practices.text: Define clear, descriptive field names and aliases so users can quickly find the filter they need.
Provide a result count to give users feedback on how their filters affect the data set.
Use PowerSearch for simple keyword searches; a standard text input is more appropriate for single-field lookups.
Wrap a disabled PowerSearch in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

props.name: config
props.description: Configuration defining available fields, operators, and their value types.

props.name: filters
props.description: Currently active filters.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when filters change. changeType is 'add', 'edit', or 'remove'. index is the affected filter's position.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the search input.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when no filters are selected.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Auto-focus the input on mount.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Show a clear-all button that removes every editable filter. Read-only filters stay.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: Prevent adding, editing, or removing filters.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the entire component.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the search is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the input focusable via aria-disabled (input stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled PowerSearch in Tooltip. Disabled controls swallow the hover events an external Tooltip needs.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status object with type and optional message.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon to display at the start of the input, before any filter tokens. Forwarded to the internal Tokenizer. Accepts a semantic icon name, an SVG icon component, or a ReactNode directly.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing.

props.name: maxTokenLength
props.description: Max character length for filter value display in tokens.

props.name: maxOperatorMenuItems
props.description: Maximum suggestions shown in string and entity value typeaheads. Does not affect the main field search menu or enum value menus.

props.name: maxSearchResults
props.description: Max ranked results for a non-empty query. Does not affect a field value editor. Browsing with an empty query shows up to 1,000 fields.

props.name: menuWidth
props.description: Width in pixels for the main field/search menu. Does not affect field value editors.

props.name: popoverSaveButtonLabel
props.description: Label for the save button in the edit popover.

props.name: timezoneID
props.description: IANA zone a date-only date_absolute value, and each absolute part of a date_range, is read and written in: the day shows, edits and stores (as that midnight) in it; unset, a day is its UTC day. A date_absolute with isDateOnly: false shows and edits its date and time in it; unset, in the viewer's zone. E.g. "America/New_York". Date values are written in the InternationalizationProvider calendar, such as calendar="persian"; filter values stay Unix seconds.

props.name: handleRef
props.description: Imperative handle with focusTypeahead() and blurTypeahead() methods.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content to display at the end of the input row. Useful for action buttons or other controls.

props.name: resultCount
props.description: Number of results matching the current filters. When a number, formatted as "N results". When a string, displayed as-is. Changes are announced to screen readers via a polite live region.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the search input and tokens.

props.name: menuWidth
props.description: Maximum width for the operator/value dropdown menu in pixels.

props.name: maxOperatorMenuItems
props.description: Maximum number of items displayed in the operator dropdown.

props.name: tokenOverflowBehavior
props.description: Controls how tokens overflow when the container is too narrow. Forwarded to Tokenizer.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Fires when focus enters the search input.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Fires when focus leaves the search input.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

props.name: presentation
props.description: How the field presents filter editing. adaptive (the default) uses the bottom sheet on compact touch screens and the popover otherwise, resolved the same way Selector resolves it; the server render and the hydrating render are the popover. popover is the tokenizer field with its typeahead and the editor popover on every device. bottom-sheet makes the whole field, on every device, one trigger showing display-only filter tokens: it opens a Filters sheet listing the filters as rows that edit or remove a filter, with Add filter, Done, and Clear all (which asks first and keeps read-only filters); an Add filter sheet with the fields (or the content search with inline suggestions) opens above it, and a value step that stages operator → value and confirms from its footer opens above that. Dismissing a step reveals the one beneath. The flow edits a draft: adding, editing and removing filters and Clear all change the draft, and onChange is called when Done applies it, once per edit in order; dismissing the flow with a changed draft asks before discarding it. List values edit through the Tokenizer's own sheet. In the sheet presentation menuWidth and tokenOverflowBehavior have no surface to act on and warn in development. Pass presentation="popover" to keep the tokenizer field and the editor popover on every device.

ProgressBar.description: A horizontal bar showing the completion progress of a task. Use it for operations where the duration is known, or as an animated indicator when progress can't be calculated. Supports semantic color variants, value labels, and custom formatting. Under a finger a new value animates as on iOS: linearly, in proportion to how far it moves (a full track takes one second at the theme's default tempo), and the fill keeps a minimum visible length above zero.

practices.text: Use a determinate bar when the total amount of work is known, and indeterminate when it's not.
Choose a color variant that matches the context: accent for general progress, success for completion, warning or error for alerts.
Always provide a label, even if hidden; screen readers need it to announce what's loading.
Place icons or labels inside the bar; compose them alongside it using layout components.
Use a progress bar for instant actions; it's meant for operations that take noticeable time.
Use multiple progress bars stacked together for the same operation; use one bar with a value label instead.

props.name: label
props.description: accessible label

props.name: value
props.description: Current value (ignored when indeterminate).

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum value.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hide the label (remains accessible).

props.name: hasValueLabel
props.description: Show formatted value text (ignored when indeterminate).

props.name: formatValueLabel
props.description: Custom value label formatter; defaults to a percentage string.

props.name: variant
props.description: Semantic color variant.

props.name: isIndeterminate
props.description: Animated loading indicator for unknown progress. Under reduced motion it pulses in place instead of sliding.

props.name: marks
props.description: Fixed target marks drawn on the track at values in the same 0..max scale as value (e.g. a goal line). They stay visible whether progress is below or past them, and take their color from what they sit on: a mark inside the filled area uses the fill variant's on-color (on-accent, on-warning, on-error, and so on), a mark still out on the bare track uses the primary text color (the secondary one on a disabled bar, which dims everything it draws). Each mark requires a label: it is the mark's accessible name and the text revealed via a tooltip on hover/focus. Ignored when indeterminate.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Visually disabled state: grays out the fill and text. Use for canceled or inactive operations.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

RadioList.description: A group of options where only one can be selected at a time. All options are visible at once, making it easy to compare choices. Use it when users need to pick one option from a small set.

practices.text: Keep the number of options small: typically 2 to 7 choices.
Use clear, concise labels that differentiate each option at a glance.
Pre-select a default option when there's a sensible default; don't leave the group empty unless the choice is optional.
Use when multiple selections are needed; use CheckboxList instead.
Use for long lists; use Selector for better discoverability.
Use horizontal layout with more than 4 options; it wraps awkwardly.
Wrap a disabled RadioList in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the radio group (always rendered for accessibility).

props.name: value
props.description: The currently selected value.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the selected value changes.

props.name: children
props.description: RadioListItem elements.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Whether to visually hide the label.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed below the label.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Layout direction of the radio items.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether all radio items are disabled.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: The HTML name attribute shared by the radio inputs, useful for form submissions. When omitted, a unique internal name still groups the radios.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the group is disabled. Applies to the whole-group disabled state (isDisabled), not per item. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the radios focusable via aria-disabled (selection stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled RadioList in Tooltip. Disabled controls swallow the hover events an external Tooltip needs.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Whether the radio group is required.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Whether the field is optional (mutually exclusive with isRequired).

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator ({ type, message }).

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the radio controls.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text for an info icon next to the label.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the element that paints the border and background and holds icons and end controls. Never the native input.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Class name for the visual control box.

props.name: controlStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the visual control box.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary label for the radio item. Rich labels may contain links or buttons, which keep their own behavior without selecting the item. The label text names the radio; use aria-label only when that text is absent, or retain every visible label word in the override.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Plain-text accessible name for the radio, applied to the control rather than the row. It overrides the name derived from the label. Use it when a rich label has no visible text; otherwise retain every visible label word.

props.name: value
props.description: Value of this radio item.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary content displayed below the label. Links and buttons keep their own click behaviour — the row only delegates clicks from its non-interactive surface to the radio.

props.name: align
props.description: Vertical alignment of the start and end content against the label, passed through to Item unchanged. `first-line` keeps a small mark (a radio) level with the first line of a wrapped label. See Item.align.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether this individual radio item is disabled.

props.name: startContent
props.description: Content to render before the radio circle.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content to render after the label.

ScrollableArea.description: Provides a native scroll viewport and a real observed content box. The viewport enters the tab order only while a requested logical axis is effectively scrollable, and containment applies only to effective axes.

practices.text: Give every area a concise label that identifies the content keyboard users will scroll.

Leave `role` unset (it renders `group`) for ordinary scroll containers. Choose `role="region"` only when the area is significant enough to appear in screen-reader landmark navigation; every `region` adds an entry to that list.
Choose `inline`, `block`, or `both` from content intent; the component maps the logical axes through writing mode and direction.
Keep the default `overscroll="allow"` for nested areas unless the interaction deliberately needs containment.

Use `useScrollableArea` instead when a component already owns both a viewport and a suitable content box, or when children must remain direct flex/grid items or retain a definite percentage block-size basis.

ScrollableArea owns one normal block content box with a 100% minimum size. Inline and both-axis modes use max-content inline sizing, so intrinsic inline layout is intentionally wider than the viewport.
Use logical padding props on the content box so nested full-bleed components receive the same inset geometry.
Set `isFullBleed` only when the viewport itself should reach an ancestor container edge; it is off by default.
Set `stickyContainment="always"` only when a fitting viewport should intentionally remain a Sticky boundary.
Hide the native scrollbar without another visible and operable overflow affordance.
Add another overflow wrapper around ScrollableArea; one native viewport should own scrolling.

props.name: axis
props.description: Logical axis or axes where native scrolling is allowed.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the viewport when it becomes keyboard scrollable.

props.name: role
props.description: Semantics for the named viewport; use `region` only for areas that belong in landmark navigation.

props.name: overscroll
props.description: Whether effective axes continue scrolling an ancestor at their edge.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the viewport; a number is interpreted as pixels, a string is used as-is.

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the viewport; a number is interpreted as pixels, a string is used as-is.

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: Maximum width of the viewport.

props.name: minHeight
props.description: Minimum height of the viewport.

props.name: stickyContainment
props.description: Whether fitting content passes Sticky ownership to an outer container or deliberately keeps this viewport as the CSS Sticky boundary.

props.name: padding
props.description: Content padding on every logical edge; publishes matching inset geometry.

props.name: paddingInline
props.description: Logical inline-axis content padding; overrides `padding` on that axis.

props.name: paddingInlineStart
props.description: Logical inline-start content padding; overrides broader padding values.

props.name: paddingInlineEnd
props.description: Logical inline-end content padding; overrides broader padding values.

props.name: paddingBlock
props.description: Logical block-axis content padding; overrides `padding` on that axis.

props.name: paddingBlockStart
props.description: Logical block-start content padding; overrides broader padding values.

props.name: paddingBlockEnd
props.description: Logical block-end content padding; overrides broader padding values.

props.name: isFullBleed
props.description: Lets the viewport escape inherited container padding without changing content padding.

props.name: children
props.description: Content rendered inside the observed content box.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX sizing and native scrollbar presentation overrides for the viewport. Must be a `stylex.create()` value, not an inline style object.

SegmentedControl.description: A segmented button group that allows users to make a single selection from a small set of mutually exclusive options. Use SegmentedControl when all options should be visible at once and the selection controls a value or mode, not page navigation. Under a finger, on a touch device (a coarse primary pointer), the selection slides to the new segment, whether a tap, an arrow key or a new value moved it; with Reduce Motion nothing travels: the old selection fades out as the new one fades in. There, dragging the selected segment carries the selection along with the selected label’s colour following it, and the segment under the finger is chosen when it lets go (letting go outside the control selects nothing); a tap selects through the browser’s click; a pressed segment shows the shared pressed overlay, and nothing lifts or dims. With a mouse or a pen every change, a click included, slides on the theme’s duration and easing, and dragging the selected segment carries it as a finger does.

practices.text: Use for switching between 2–5 mutually exclusive views or modes where all options should be visible.
Provide a descriptive label for the control to ensure the group is accessible to screen readers.
Use for page-level navigation; use TabList instead. TabList is a navigation component, while SegmentedControl is an input that always has exactly one selected option.
Use for simple on/off states; use ToggleButton instead. ToggleButton can be toggled on or off independently, while SegmentedControl enforces a single selection from a group.
Wrap a disabled SegmentedControl in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; the reason is then not attached to the control or its segments. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

props.name: value
props.description: The currently selected value (controlled).

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when a segment is selected.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the radio group (used as aria-label, never rendered visually).

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant for the control.

props.name: layout
props.description: Layout mode. hug (default) sizes segments to content, capped at the container width (segment labels truncate when it is too narrow); fill stretches them equally to fill the container.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the entire control is disabled. The selected segment keeps the Tab stop, announced as disabled (aria-disabled), and nothing can be selected.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the control is disabled. Applies to the whole-group disabled state (isDisabled), not per segment. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus, and the reason describes each segment (selection stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled SegmentedControl in Tooltip, so the reason is attached to the control itself.

props.name: children
props.description: SegmentedControlItem children.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: value
props.description: Unique value for this segment, matched against the parent value.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for this segment. Rendered as visible text unless isLabelHidden is true.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Whether the label is visually hidden. When true, only the icon is displayed and label is used as aria-label.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon element displayed before the label.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether this individual item is disabled. A disabled selected item keeps the control's Tab stop.

ComplexSelector.description: Use ComplexSelector when a selection needs richer custom content than a Selector option row. It is intentionally one component: ComplexSelector owns the field, trigger, popover, focus restore, and changeAction flow, while the content render prop owns the selector-specific accessible structure.

practices.text: Use variant="secondary" beside secondary buttons, or variant="ghost" beside ghost buttons; add a startIcon when it helps identify the trigger. Use alignment="end" when a wide surface should align its end edge to the trigger.
For staged editors, keep draft state in the composed content and call the provided onChange helper only from Apply. Cancel or dismiss without committing.

Compose the dialog content from the appropriate accessible structure for the job: RadioList for a simple choice, Calendar/date inputs for date picking, TreeList or a searchable list for hierarchy, or a custom grid when two-dimensional arrow navigation is useful.
Use the provided onChange helper from children; it already calls both onChange and changeAction and updates optimistic busy state.
Call close() from custom content when a selection should dismiss the popup. Keep it open for multi-step content or freeform entry flows.
Use Astryx focus hooks for custom content: useGridFocus for two-dimensional grids, useTreeFocus through TreeList for hierarchies, and useListFocus for custom linear collections.

Evaluate custom content against WCAG 2.2: keyboard operation, focus visible/not obscured, names and roles, labels/instructions, target size, and contrast/non-text contrast are especially relevant for selector popovers.
Do not rebuild trigger ARIA, popover focus management, or changeAction handling in product code.
Do not use ComplexSelector for a plain single-column text list; use Selector instead.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for accessibility and the field label.

props.name: value
props.description: Current controlled value.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when custom content commits a new value.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action after onChange. ComplexSelector exposes optimistic value and busy state while pending.

props.name: children
props.type: (value: Value, onChange: (value: Value) => void, close: () => void, state: ComplexSelectorRenderState) => ReactNode
props.description: Custom dialog content. Receives positional value, onChange, close, and state helpers.

props.name: triggerLabel
props.description: Label/content shown in the closed trigger.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder shown when triggerLabel is omitted.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the selector.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Shows loading state on the trigger.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status.

props.name: statusVariant
props.default: 'attached' for input selectors; 'detached' for secondary and ghost selectors
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment; detached when variant is secondary or ghost); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip reveals the message in an info-tip button.

props.name: size
props.description: Exact trigger height: sm 28px, md 32px, or lg 36px.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual trigger style. Input is the bordered form treatment; secondary matches the secondary buttons of the active theme (borderless and neutral-filled by default); ghost is borderless and transparent to match ghost buttons.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon displayed at the start of the trigger.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field.

props.name: placement
props.description: Popup placement.

props.name: alignment
props.description: Popup alignment along the placement axis.

props.name: renderTrigger
props.description: Render the control the popup hangs off — a glyph in a list row, a chip, an icon button — instead of the selector's own field and button. Spread the given props ({ref, id, onClick, onKeyDown, role, aria-haspopup, aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-busy, aria-required, aria-disabled}) onto it: the control becomes the selector's combobox field, the popup is anchored to it and still labelled by `label`, and a disabled control keeps its tab stop but does not open. The field chrome is not rendered. Pair with handleRef to open from a keystroke elsewhere.

props.name: handleRef
props.description: Imperative handle for programmatic control. Exposes open(), close(), toggle(), and isOpen().

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called whenever the surface opens or closes, however it happened — trigger, keyboard, light dismiss, Escape, close(), or the imperative handle.

props.name: contentXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the popup content container.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler on the trigger. Runs before the popup opens; call preventDefault() to keep it closed. A press elsewhere in the control box goes through the trigger too. With renderTrigger it runs after the built-in toggle and cannot cancel it.

props.name: onKeyDown
props.description: Key handler on the trigger. Runs after the built-in handling and receives every key, including the ArrowDown that opens the popup. With renderTrigger it is skipped for keys the built-in handling cancels.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the element that paints the border and background and holds the value, icons, and end controls. Never the trigger button itself.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Class name for the visual control box.

props.name: controlStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the visual control box.

MultiSelector.description: A checkbox dropdown for selecting multiple values from a list. Selected items can display as a count, labels, or badges. Use it for filtering or when presenting a finite set of options where multiple choices are needed.

practices.text: Use for a moderate, finite set of options where multiple choices are needed.
Enable search filtering when the list exceeds ~15 options.
Use renderOption for custom option rows; the checkbox affordance remains owned by MultiSelector.
Enable select-all when most users will want all or nearly all options selected.
Use inside InputGroup only when the control needs a short prefix or suffix addon as part of one decorated input surface; prefer count or labels trigger display so the group stays single-line.

Use variant="secondary" when a multi-selector sits beside secondary buttons or segmented controls, and variant="ghost" when it sits beside ghost buttons. If validation status is needed there, prefer statusVariant="tooltip" so the toolbar height stays compact.
Use presentation="adaptive" when the multi-selector should become a bottom sheet on compact touch screens.
Use for single-value selection; use Selector instead.
Show more than ~20 options without enabling search.
Wrap a disabled MultiSelector in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop, which attaches the reason to the trigger itself.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for accessibility.

props.name: options
props.description: Array of items: strings, objects with value/label/icon/disabled, dividers, or sections. An option may carry `action`: one node — an IconButton, a Button, a menu trigger — the caller renders and names. Once any option does, the popup is a grid whose rows pair the option with its action: Up/Down move rows, the inline-end arrow reaches the action, Enter fires it, pointer and touch press it directly, and pressing it never changes the selection.

props.name: value
props.description: Currently selected values.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when the selection changes. A creation (hasCreate) arrives with `{type: "create", query}` as the second argument and the query appended to value; the caller adds the matching option in that same update. Every other change passes no descriptor, so a one-argument handler keeps working.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action on change. Fires after onChange.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when no value is selected.

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant for the selector.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual trigger style. input is the bordered input treatment for forms; secondary matches the secondary buttons of the active theme (borderless and neutral-filled by default) for navs and toolbars; ghost is borderless and transparent, matching ghost buttons for toolbar usage.

props.name: triggerDisplay
props.description: How to display selected items in the trigger.

props.name: formatValue
props.description: Formats the trigger text when triggerDisplay="count" or "labels". Receives the selected items (value plus resolved label); the count is items.length. Not used by triggerDisplay="badges".

props.name: maxBadges
props.description: Maximum badges to show before "+N". Only for triggerDisplay="badges".

props.name: hasSelectAll
props.description: Whether to show a select-all checkbox.

props.name: selectAllLabel
props.description: Label for the select-all checkbox.

props.name: hasSearch
props.description: Whether to show a search input for filtering options. As the user types, the match count (or "No results found") is announced to screen readers via a polite live region. The search field has built-in affordances: a leading magnifier icon and, once a query is typed, a trailing clear (✕) button that resets the query and returns focus to the input.

props.name: searchPlaceholder
props.description: Placeholder text for the search input.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Content shown in the dropdown panel when there are no options to show, and announced in a polite live region when the panel opens. The announcement is the text this content renders, read from the DOM, so an element is announced as written and aria-hidden parts are left out of both. Not shown while isLoading.

props.name: emptySearchText
props.description: Content shown in the dropdown panel when a search query matches no options, and announced in a polite live region at the same time. The announcement is the text this content renders, read from the DOM, so an element is announced as written and aria-hidden parts are left out of both.

props.name: hasCreate
props.description: With hasSearch, offers a `Create "<query>"` row first in the list when the typed text equals no option label under the search’s case-insensitive matching. Picking it, or Enter with nothing highlighted, calls onChange with the query appended to value and a `{type: "create", query}` descriptor, then clears the search; the caller must add an option for the new value in that update. Nothing is offered while isLoading. Without hasSearch it warns in development and offers nothing.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the selector.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: Makes the selector read-only: the selected values stay visible, focusable, and included in form submission, and retain their combobox identity with aria-readonly. The selection surface, clear action, and disclosure indicator are removed. Unlike isDisabled, the control is not dimmed. isDisabled takes precedence when both are set.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: The HTML name attribute for form submissions. Renders one hidden input per selected value, like a native multi-select.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the selector is disabled. With isDisabled, shows the reason as a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus of the trigger, which stays focusable (aria-disabled) like every disabled selector; activation stays blocked. Use this instead of wrapping a disabled MultiSelector in Tooltip.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text displayed below the label.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Marks the field as optional.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Marks the field as required.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Shows a loading spinner in the trigger.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status with an optional message.

props.name: statusVariant
props.default: 'attached' for input selectors; 'detached' for secondary and ghost selectors
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the bordered input and is only valid for the input variant; secondary and ghost selectors detach attached status messages by default. Use tooltip for compact toolbar controls.

props.name: renderOption
props.description: Custom render function for each selectable option in the dropdown. Not called for dividers, sections, or the select-all row.

props.name: indicatorPosition
props.description: Which edge of the option row carries the checkbox. end pushes it to the far edge of the row, including on the select-all row.

props.name: presentation
props.description: How the option list is presented. adaptive uses a bottom sheet on compact touch screens and an anchored popover otherwise.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon displayed at the start of the selector trigger.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Shows a clear button when values are selected.

props.name: isDefaultOpen
props.description: Whether the dropdown starts open on mount.

props.name: renderTrigger
props.description: Render the control the panel hangs off — a glyph in a list row, a chip, an icon button — instead of the selector's own field and button. Spread the given props ({ref, id, onClick, onKeyDown, onFocus, aria-haspopup, aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-busy}) onto it; the listbox is anchored to that control and named by `label`. The field chrome (Field, status, clear, spinner) is not rendered. Pair with handleRef to open from a keystroke elsewhere.

props.name: handleRef
props.description: Imperative handle with open(), close(), toggle() and isOpen(). Prefer it over mirroring open state in the parent; the selector owns its visibility.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called whenever the panel opens or closes, however it happened: the trigger, the keyboard, a light dismiss, Escape, or the handle.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler on the trigger (or the renderTrigger control). Runs after the built-in toggle and cannot cancel it.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Focus handler on the trigger. Runs before the selector's own focus handling.

props.name: onKeyDown
props.description: Key handler on the trigger button. Runs after the built-in keyboard model and is skipped for keys it handles and cancels.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the element that paints the border and background and holds the value, icons, and end controls. Never the trigger button itself.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Class name for the visual control box.

props.name: controlStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the visual control box.

Selector.description: A dropdown selector for choosing a single value from a list of options. Supports labels, validation, descriptions, and required/optional states. Use it in forms and settings when presenting a moderate number of options. Keyboard typeahead matches a native select: typing on the focused closed trigger selects the matching option directly, repeated presses cycle through options sharing a first letter, and spaces count as match characters ("new y" reaches "New York"). With the menu open, typing moves the highlight and Enter commits. With hasSearch, typing on the closed trigger opens the popup and seeds the search input.

practices.text: Provide a visible label so users understand what they are selecting.
Use sections and dividers to organize options when the list exceeds ~8 items.
Use renderOption for custom option rows. Do not pass SelectorOption directly as JSX children.
Set a meaningful placeholder that hints at the expected selection (e.g. "Choose a country" not "Select...").
Use inside InputGroup only when the selector needs a short prefix or suffix addon as part of one decorated input surface.

Use variant="secondary" when a selector sits in a nav or toolbar beside secondary buttons or a segmented control, so it shares their treatment instead of reading as a form field. Use variant="ghost" when a selector sits in a toolbar with ghost buttons. If validation status is needed there, prefer statusVariant="tooltip" so the toolbar height stays compact.
Use presentation="adaptive" when the selector should become a bottom sheet on compact touch screens.
Use for action menus; use Dropdown Menu for triggering commands or navigation.
Use when there are only two options; use a SegmentedControl or radio buttons instead.
Use Selector for navigation; links should be links, not dropdown options.
Use for yes/no or on/off choices; use Switch or CheckboxInput instead.
Put more than ~20 options without sections; consider Typeahead for large lists.
Wrap a disabled Selector in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop, which attaches the reason to the trigger itself.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for accessibility.

props.name: options
props.description: Array of items: strings, objects with value/label/description/icon/disabled, dividers ({type: "divider"}), or sections ({type: "section", title, options}).

props.name: value
props.description: Currently selected value.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the selection changes.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Shows a clear (×) button when a value is selected. When true, onChange also accepts null to signal the user cleared the selection.

props.name: hasSearch
props.description: Whether to show a search input for filtering options. As the user types, the match count (or "No results found") is announced to screen readers via a polite live region. The search field has built-in affordances: a leading magnifier icon and, once a query is typed, a trailing clear (✕) button that resets the query and returns focus to the input.

props.name: searchPlaceholder
props.description: Placeholder text for the search input.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Content shown in the dropdown panel when there are no options to show, and announced in a polite live region when the panel opens. The announcement is the text this content renders, read from the DOM, so an element is announced as written and aria-hidden parts are left out of both. Not shown while isLoading.

props.name: emptySearchText
props.description: Content shown in the dropdown panel when a search query matches no options, and announced in a polite live region at the same time. The announcement is the text this content renders, read from the DOM, so an element is announced as written and aria-hidden parts are left out of both.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when no value is selected.

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant for the selector.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual trigger style. input is the bordered input treatment for forms; secondary matches the secondary buttons of the active theme (borderless and neutral-filled by default) for navs and toolbars; ghost is borderless and transparent, matching ghost buttons for toolbar usage.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the selector.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: Makes the selector read-only: the selected value stays visible, focusable, and included in form submission, and retains its combobox identity with aria-readonly. The selection surface, clear action, and disclosure indicator are removed. Unlike isDisabled, the control is not dimmed. isDisabled takes precedence when both are set.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: The HTML name attribute for form submissions. Renders a hidden input carrying the selected value, like a native select.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the selector is disabled. With isDisabled, shows the reason as a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus of the trigger, which stays focusable (aria-disabled) like every disabled selector; activation stays blocked. Use this instead of wrapping a disabled Selector in Tooltip.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text displayed below the label.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Marks the field as optional.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Marks the field as required.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status with an optional message.

props.name: statusVariant
props.default: 'attached' for input selectors; 'detached' for secondary and ghost selectors
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the bordered input and is only valid for the input variant; secondary and ghost selectors detach attached status messages by default. Use tooltip for compact toolbar controls.

props.name: renderOption
props.description: Custom render function for each selectable option in the dropdown. Use this instead of JSX children; dividers and sections are rendered by the selector.

props.name: renderValue
props.description: Custom render function for the selected option inside the closed trigger. A one-line value follows the active size token, including compact or wide spacing scales with icons or a clear control. Padding accommodates the trigger line box, and each extra line grows the control by one line (28/32/36 for one line and 48/52/56 for two with the default tokens). Content inherits the trigger line height; content that sets a larger font should set its own line height so the trigger grows to fit it. Inside an InputGroup the group owns the row height: a SelectorOption folds onto one line and ellipsizes, and any taller node is cut off at the row.

props.name: indicatorPosition
props.description: Which logical edge of the option row carries a rendered selection mark. An empty mark consumes no space, so selected and unselected labels may shift or have different available width. end is the house convention shared with Typeahead and CommandPalette.

props.name: presentation
props.description: How the option list is presented. adaptive uses a bottom sheet on compact touch screens and an anchored popover otherwise.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned. Without a width the field follows its displayed value and can shrink with its row (the value truncates) instead of overflowing it; use `<HStack wrap="wrap">` for filter bars so selectors move to a second line on phones.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon displayed at the start of the selector trigger.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Shows a loading spinner in the trigger.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler on the trigger button. Runs before the selector toggles its surface; preventDefault() does not keep it closed.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Focus handler on the trigger button. Runs before the selector's own focus handling.

props.name: onKeyDown
props.description: Key handler on the trigger button. Runs after the built-in keyboard model and is skipped for keys it handles and cancels.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the element that paints the border and background and holds the value, icons, and end controls. Never the trigger button itself.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Class name for the visual control box.

props.name: controlStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the visual control box.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary label text for the item.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon displayed before the label. See `astryx docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary description text displayed below the label.

props.name: layout
props.description: How the label and description sit together. 'stacked' puts the description on its own line; 'inline' keeps both on one line so the row fits a fixed-height host. Inside a Selector trigger the trigger's padding sizes itself to whichever layout you pick, so both land on the 4px rhythm; an InputGroup pins the row height and forces 'inline'.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Additional content rendered after the label and description.

Skeleton.description: An animated shimmer placeholder that previews the shape of content while it loads. Use it to build loading screens that match the layout of the real content. For content with unknown dimensions, use Spinner instead.

practices.text: Match the size and shape of the content being loaded to create a realistic placeholder.
Stagger multiple skeletons with the `index` prop for a natural wave animation.
Use when the content dimensions are unknown; use Spinner instead.
Combine with a Spinner on the same content area; pick one loading pattern.
Show skeletons indefinitely; if loading takes too long, show an error or empty state instead.

props.name: width
props.description: Width in pixels (number) or CSS value (string).

props.name: height
props.description: Height in pixels (number) or CSS value (string).

props.name: radius
props.description: Border radius using design token scale. Use none for sharp corners, rounded for fully rounded (avatars, pills, circles).

props.name: index
props.description: Index for staggered animation timing. For element at index n, animation starts at DELAY_TIME + (STAGGER_TIME × n).

Slider.description: A draggable control for selecting a numeric value or range within defined bounds. Supports single value and range selection, tick marks, custom value formatting, and vertical orientation. Use it when users need to explore a continuous range, such as volume, price, or percentage. Under a finger, on any touch device, it tracks as UISlider does: only the thumb takes a drag, through a target larger than it, the value follows the finger’s travel rather than jumping to it, a release coasts on before `onChangeEnd`, a swipe from the track scrolls the page, and a tap on the track or a mark sets the value when the finger lifts (the thumb springs there). A mouse drag on a thumb tracks the same way, past the same 10 px in any direction, with no lift or coast; a mouse press on the track moves the thumb there, and only a primary click presses. A pen drags as a finger does, claiming only along the track, and its drag ends at the release with no coast. A wheel or a trackpad scroll over the slider goes to whatever scrolls under it.

practices.text: Always provide a label, even if visually hidden, so the slider is accessible to screen readers.
Format values with meaningful units like "$50" or "75%" instead of raw numbers.
Use for precise numeric entry; pair with a text input or use NumberInput instead.
Set a step size so large that only a few positions are possible; use SegmentedControl or radio buttons instead.
Wrap a disabled slider in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text (always rendered for accessibility).

props.name: value
props.description: Current value: a `number` for single thumb mode or `[number, number]` for range mode.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired on value change during drag.

props.name: onChangeEnd
props.description: Callback fired when drag ends.

props.name: min
props.description: Minimum value.

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum value.

props.name: step
props.description: Step increment.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Orientation of the slider.

props.name: formatValue
props.description: Custom value formatting function used for display and `aria-valuetext`.

props.name: valueDisplay
props.description: How the current value is displayed.

props.name: marks
props.description: Tick marks at specified positions with optional labels. Unfilled marks use the track color; marks inside the filled region (at or behind the thumb, or between the thumbs in range mode) use the fill color.

props.name: minStepsBetweenThumbs
props.description: Minimum number of steps between thumbs in range mode; prevents thumbs from overlapping.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the slider is disabled.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: The HTML name attribute for form submissions. Renders hidden inputs carrying the current value (two entries in range mode).

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the slider is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the thumb focusable via aria-disabled (value changes stay blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled Slider in Tooltip. Disabled controls swallow the hover events an external Tooltip needs.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Whether the field is optional.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Whether the field is required.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Whether to visually hide the label.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text rendered below the label.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator object (`{ type, message }`) for validation feedback.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text for an info icon displayed next to the label.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the element that paints the border and background and holds icons and end controls. Never the native input.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Class name for the visual control box.

props.name: controlStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the visual control box.

Spinner.description: An animated loading indicator for processes with unknown duration, such as data fetching or form submission. Supports visible labels, multiple sizes, and a dark background variant. For content with known dimensions, use Skeleton instead.

practices.text: Provide a meaningful label to describe what is loading for screen reader users.
Use the "onMedia" shade when placed on dark or accent-colored backgrounds.
Use for content areas with known dimensions; use Skeleton to preserve layout instead.
Stack multiple spinners in the same view; use one to represent the overall loading state.

props.name: size
props.description: Spinner size: ring diameter (10px, 14px, 18px, 28px).

props.name: shade
props.description: Color shade for light or dark backgrounds.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible content below the spinner. A string label names the indicator through aria-labelledby.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name for screen readers. Defaults to label (if string) or a translated "Loading" from the i18n catalog.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

StatusDot.description: A small colored dot that communicates status like online/offline presence or severity levels. Supports five semantic variants and an optional pulse animation. Always pair with a visible text label, as color alone should not carry meaning.

practices.text: Use StatusDot as a binary present/absent signal; avoid encoding many distinct states in a single dot, since color and size alone cannot reliably distinguish them.
Always pair with a visible text label so status is not conveyed by color alone.
Provide a descriptive `label` prop for screen reader accessibility.
Pair the dot with an icon that carries the status as a distinct shape when it must stand on its own without adjacent text, so meaning survives without color.
If you can't add a label or an icon, make sure the status is conveyed elsewhere accessibly (e.g. adjacent text, a table column, or a live region).

Rely on color alone to communicate status; StatusDot is not fully accessible in isolation, so the builder must make the status distinguishable in context via a label, an icon, or an accessible alternative.
Use the pulse animation for purely decorative purposes; reserve it for states that require immediate attention.

props.name: variant
props.description: Semantic color variant.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label surfaced via aria-label.

props.name: isPulsing
props.description: Enables a pulse animation; respects prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Tooltip text shown on hover to explain the status meaning.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon rendered centered inside the dot, painted in currentColor (the variant's ink). Gives the status a non-color mark, so use a different icon per status. Booleans and empty strings are ignored, so `cond && <Icon />` is safe. Same contract as AvatarStatusDot.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: step
props.description: Zero-based index of this step. Used to derive progress (completed/active/not-started) relative to the parent activeStep.

props.name: label
props.description: Step label text. Kept to a single line and ellipsized when the step is narrower than the label, so a row of horizontal steps stays the same height and the track under them stays straight. The full string is still read out as part of the step, so a truncated label costs nothing in the accessible name — but short labels survive narrow layouts better.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional description shown below the label for additional context.

props.name: children
props.description: Content rendered below the label and description. Useful in vertical steppers for form fields or detailed step content. In a compact horizontal Stepper, the content remains mounted to preserve local state while it is hidden with the expanded step details.

props.name: status
props.description: Semantic color for the step. Controls color only and maps to the global Astryx semantic tokens. Leave unset for the progress-derived default coloring.

props.name: indicator
props.description: What to show as the step indicator. 'auto' shows a number until completed then a check, 'number' always shows a numbered badge, 'none' hides it, or pass any ReactNode (e.g. an Icon) for a fully custom indicator.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables interaction and dims the step indicator and label.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Marks the step as optional, appending an "Optional" affordance after the label.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Trailing content rendered at the end of the label row.

props.name: density
props.description: Controls vertical padding of the step. Falls back to the stepper-level density when unset.

Stepper.description: Steppers display progress through a sequence of logical and numbered steps. Use them for multi-step workflows like forms, onboarding flows, or checkout processes where users need to see their position and the steps ahead. Rendered as an ordered list (not a navigation landmark).

practices.text: Keep step labels short and descriptive: "Payment" not "Enter your payment information".

Use the vertical orientation when steps carry longer descriptions. A horizontal stepper handles narrow containers itself: once the frame gives each step less than horizontalOptions.minimumStepWidth (112px by default) it drops the labels for a segmented track and uses the configured collapsedVariant beneath it.

Set horizontalOptions.collapsedVariant to 'withLabel' when the page already supplies Back/Continue, or to 'hiddenLabel' when surrounding UI owns both the current-step heading and navigation and only a bare progress track is needed.
Provide onStepClick for non-linear workflows where users may need to revisit earlier steps.
Use status only to apply a semantic color (accent/success/warning/error); pass a custom icon for richer indicators.
Use a stepper for fewer than 3 steps; a simple heading or progress bar works better.
Use more than 7 steps; consider grouping related steps or using a different pattern.

props.name: activeStep
props.description: Zero-based index of the currently active step. Steps before this index are marked as completed.

props.name: children
props.description: Step elements to render in the stepper.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Layout direction of the stepper.

props.name: onStepClick
props.description: Called when a step is clicked or a compact summary control is used. Enables non-linear navigation. Every step becomes a button until a horizontal Stepper collapses: enabled steps activate, and disabled steps stay focusable and are announced as unavailable but do not activate. When collapsed, navigation moves to summary controls that skip disabled steps.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label describing the set of steps (applied to the ordered list). Defaults to a localized "Progress".

props.name: density
props.description: Controls the padding of all steps.

props.name: indicatorPosition
props.description: Position of step indicators relative to the connector track.

props.name: horizontalOptions
props.description: Options for horizontal collapse. minimumStepWidth is the per-step threshold in pixels. collapsedVariant selects a label with controls, the label alone, or a bare progress track with no compact row. Controls appear only for withLabelAndControls when onStepClick is set, and every step keeps its accessible name.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

Switch.description: A toggle control for on/off states that take effect immediately. Supports labels, descriptions, loading states, and validation. Use it for settings or preferences that apply instantly. For changes requiring a form submission, use a checkbox instead. Under a finger it moves like the iOS switch on every touch screen: a press lifts the thumb, a drag across flips it, lifting the finger commits, and a tap toggles through the browser’s click. The thumb keeps its circle and size on every device, and under a coarse pointer the invisible hit area grows toward 44 × 44 px, stopping halfway to any neighbouring control so a tap goes to the nearer one. With reduced motion on, a change cross-fades on a touch screen and is immediate with a mouse.

practices.text: Use for settings that apply immediately; the toggle should take effect without a separate save action.
Pair with a clear, concise label that describes the setting being controlled.
Use for options that require a form submission to take effect; use a checkbox instead.
Use a switch for multi-state values; it's strictly on/off.
Wrap a disabled switch in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the underlying <input> element.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the switch (always rendered for accessibility).

props.name: value
props.description: Whether the switch is on or off.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the switch state changes.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action fired after onChange. Triggers optimistic UI and shows a loading spinner until the promise resolves.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Whether the switch is in a loading state, showing a spinner inside the thumb.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible to screen readers.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed below the label.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the switch is disabled.

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant controlling track and thumb dimensions. sm (32x20px) matches sm checkbox/radio vertical rhythm; md (40x24px, default) matches md checkbox/radio vertical rhythm.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: The HTML name attribute for the underlying checkbox input, useful for form submissions (submits "on" when the switch is on).

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the switch is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the switch focusable via aria-disabled (toggling stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled Switch in Tooltip. Disabled controls swallow the hover events an external Tooltip needs.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Whether the field is optional. Mutually exclusive with isRequired.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Whether the switch is required. Mutually exclusive with isOptional.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator with type and message. Displays a colored message box below the switch and sets aria-invalid when type is "error".

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Callback fired when the switch receives focus.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Callback fired when the switch loses focus.

props.name: labelIcon
props.description: Icon displayed before the label text. See `astryx docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text shown in an info icon at the end of the label.

props.name: labelPosition
props.description: Which side of the switch the label appears on. "start" places the label before the switch.

props.name: labelSpacing
props.description: Spacing behavior between label and switch. "hug" places them next to each other; "spread" pushes them to opposite ends of the container (full width).

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

Table.description: Table displays structured data in rows and columns with consistent dimensionality. It supports rich cell content, sorting, selection, pagination, and column management through a composable plugin system. Use Table for data sets with uniform structure; for simpler or inconsistent data, consider a list or card layout instead.

practices.text: Use density and divider variants to match the information density and scanning needs of your data.
Compose rich cell content with Astryx components like Badge, StatusDot, and Avatar via renderCell.

In children mode, put every row inside TableHeader, TableBody, or TableFooter. <table> cannot contain a <tr> directly: the HTML parser inserts an implied <tbody> for server-rendered markup and React does not on the client, so unwrapped rows mismatch on hydration.

Omit width for equal flexible columns with a compact 60px readability floor. Give one column its own floor with proportional(1, {minWidth}), weight columns with proportional(n), and fix widths with pixel(); the Table scroll region activates when the combined floors no longer fit.

Use the data-driven API from React Server Components: proportional(), pixel(), and column definitions without function props are server-safe. Columns using renderCell (or any function prop) need the table wrapped in a "use client" component, since functions cannot cross the server-client boundary.
Use a table for data without consistent columns. Use a list or card layout for heterogeneous content.
Enable every plugin at once. Add only the features your use case requires to keep the interface focused.
Rely on the 60px omitted-width floor when a text-heavy column needs more room; set proportional(1, {minWidth}) on that column instead.

props.name: data
props.description: Array of data items to render as rows. T must extend Record<string, unknown> (use `interface MyRow extends Record<string, unknown>` for custom types).

props.name: columns
props.description: Column definitions: each column has {key, header, width?, align?, renderCell?}. The `header` field sets the column heading text. If omitted, columns are auto-generated from data object keys. The `width` field is typed as `ColumnWidth` (not a number); use `proportional(n)` or `pixel(n)` helpers imported from `@astryxdesign/core/Table`. Omitting `width` keeps an equal flexible share with a compact 60px readability floor. To give one column a different floor, set `width: proportional(1, {minWidth: 80})`; its `minWidth` replaces the 60px floor for that column. Example: `width: pixel(120)` for 120px fixed, `width: proportional(1)` for a flexible column with a 120px default minimum.

props.name: idKey
props.description: Canonical row identity: a property name projects valid strings and finite numbers to strings; a function retains string/number type. Optional legacy tables fall back to index. Virtualization requires explicit unique valid keys.

props.name: density
props.description: Row density controlling cell padding and font size.

props.name: dividers
props.description: Divider style rendered between cells.

props.name: isStriped
props.description: Applies a background wash to even-numbered rows.

props.name: hasHover
props.description: Applies a hover highlight background to rows on pointer devices.

props.name: verticalAlign
props.description: Vertical alignment for body row cells. Controls `vertical-align` on the `<td>` elements.

props.name: textOverflow
props.description: How body cell text behaves when it exceeds the column width. 'wrap' lets text wrap and the row grow taller; 'truncate' clips with an ellipsis (default-rendered cells show a tooltip on hover when truncated). Header cells always truncate.

props.name: virtualization
props.description: Geometry-only capability from useTableRowsVirtualization({rowHeight, initialViewportHeight}), both positive finite CSS pixels; the Table scrolls inside the height its parent gives it, and initialViewportHeight only sizes the first window. Give the Table's parent a height, fixed or relative, or a flex child, so windowing can bound the rows; with no height every row renders. Pass complete flat data and an explicit idKey. Default text truncates; custom renderers, wrapping, structural plugins, incompatible offsets, invalid identity or unrepresentable geometry use full rendering. Logical row positions include the header.

props.name: plugins
props.description: Named plugins that extend table behavior via the transform pipeline. Converted to an ordered array internally.

props.name: rowIndexStart
props.description: ARIA row index (1-based) for the first rendered body row. The row ordinal is an accessibility concern independent of any visible index column, so setting this (or rowCount) makes the table emit aria-rowindex on body rows and aria-rowcount on the table. For a paginated/windowed view, pass the offset of the first visible row (e.g. (page - 1) * pageSize + 1) so aria-rowindex reflects position in the full dataset. Data-driven mode only.

props.name: rowCount
props.description: Total number of body rows across all pages/windows, used for aria-rowcount so assistive tech can announce "row X of Y" against the full dataset. When omitted but rowIndexStart is set (windowed view with an unknown total), aria-rowcount is set to -1 per the ARIA unknown-count convention. Data-driven mode only.

props.name: children
props.description: Children mode: compose the table yourself from TableHeader / TableBody / TableFooter, each holding TableRow and TableCell, instead of using data-driven rendering. The children are passed straight to the <table>, so the section is yours to supply. A TableRow placed directly in Table emits <table><tr>, which is invalid HTML and mismatches on hydration (the parser inserts an implied <tbody> for server-rendered markup; React does not on the client). Data-driven mode renders the sections for you.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: children
props.description: The <tbody> rows.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: children
props.description: Cell content.

props.name: children
props.description: The <tfoot> rows.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: children
props.description: The <thead> rows.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: children
props.description: Header cell content.

props.name: children
props.description: Row cell elements.

TableSelectionToolbar.description: Pass both outputs of useTableSelectionState to their matching consumers: selectionConfig to useTableSelection and selectionState to TableSelectionToolbar. An app that keeps its own selection, such as every row matching a query across server pages, passes its own config and state instead. Render product actions through startContent. Keep fixed or floating placement in the surrounding layout.

practices.text: Pass selectionState directly from useTableSelectionState so the count and clear action stay synchronized with row selection, unless the app keeps its own selection across server pages.
Provide product actions as startContent instead of encoding them as configuration objects.
Inject the toolbar through the Table plugin or its horizontal scroll wrapper.

props.name: selection
props.description: Shared selection state: selectedKeys, selectedCount, hasSelection, and clearSelection. Usually useTableSelectionState returns it; an app that keeps its own selection builds it.

props.name: startContent
props.description: Product-owned action controls aligned to the logical start. Child controls inherit the toolbar size.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the action surface.

props.name: renderSelectionLabel
