props.description: Overrides the visible count text for localisation or domain-specific copy.

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: Visible label for the command that clears the complete controlled selection.

props.name: size
props.description: Toolbar size. Cascades to product action controls and the clear action.

props.name: variant
props.description: Toolbar surface variant.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: Caller-owned layout styles, including sticky positioning for floating compositions.

props.name: value
props.description: Unique value for this tab, matched against TabListContext.value.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for this tab. Used as visible text by default, or as aria-label when isLabelHidden is true.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Whether the label is visually hidden. When true, only the icon and endContent are displayed, and label is used as aria-label for accessibility.

props.name: href
props.description: URL to navigate to; when provided, the tab renders as an anchor element. Ignored in a TabList given an explicit role="tablist".

props.name: panelId
props.description: Id of the panel this tab controls, wired up as aria-controls where the TabList speaks the tabs pattern. Put the same id on the panel element. No effect under the navigation pattern, and a development warning says so.

props.name: as
props.description: Custom component to render instead of <a> for link tabs. Overrides the LinkProvider default. Only applies when href is provided.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon element shown when the tab is not selected.

props.name: selectedIcon
props.description: Icon element shown when the tab is selected; falls back to icon if not provided.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content rendered after the label, such as a badge count or status dot. The tab is one button, so endContent holds only non-interactive content: no button, link, InfoTip, or other focusable control. To explain a tab, anchor a Tooltip on the Tab through its ref, render it after the TabList, and put a decorative info Icon here.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

TabList.description: TabList provides tab-style navigation for organizing content into categorized sections. Use it to let users switch between related views without leaving the page. A strip narrower than its tabs scrolls horizontally and keeps the selected tab in view.

practices.text: Keep tab labels short and descriptive so users can quickly scan available sections.
Leave overflow handling on: a strip narrower than its tabs scrolls, and the selected tab is kept in view. Use TabMenu when you want a curated group of extra options rather than a scrolling strip.

When using hasDivider with action buttons alongside tabs, match the Button size to the TabList size (both md, both sm); the divided tab strip reserves space so tabs and same-size buttons align to a shared baseline above the rail.

Reach for role="tablist" when the strip switches panels in place, and give each tab a panelId pointing at the panel it opens: that link is how a screen reader gets from a tab to its content. Leave it off for navigation between views.
Set isFullBleed to stretch a tab bar inside a padded LayoutHeader, Card, or Section to the container's inline content edges, instead of reaching for negative-margin CSS.
Use tabs for sequential steps or workflows; use a stepper or wizard pattern instead.
Place more than 6–8 visible tabs before the overflow menu; prioritize the most important categories.

Confuse TabList with SegmentedControl or ToggleButton. TabList is for navigation between views. SegmentedControl and ToggleButton are input controls: SegmentedControl always has exactly one selected option, while ToggleButton can be toggled on or off.

props.name: value
props.description: The currently selected tab value.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when a tab is selected.

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant applied to all child tabs.

props.name: layout
props.description: Layout mode for tab sizing. 'hug': each tab hugs its content width. 'fill': tabs stretch equally to fill the container width.

props.name: hasDivider
props.description: Whether to show a bottom border divider under the tab list.

props.name: isFullBleed
props.description: Makes the tab strip escape its parent's container padding, extending to the container's content edges (cancels the nearest padded Layout container's --container-padding-* custom properties with negative margins). The inner strip pads back by the portion of the container inset that is not already supplied by the first or last tab stop, keeping edge labels aligned while a hasDivider underline spans the full content width. Matches Divider's isFullBleed: inline (start/end) edges only; block-edge docking stays with the surrounding layout.

props.name: role
props.description: ARIA role for the strip. 'tablist' asks for the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern: role="tablist" / role="tab" and aria-selected, with each tab pointing at the panel it controls via its panelId; only tabs may live in a tablist strip, and an href on a tab is ignored there. Left unset, the strip is a nav landmark marking the current tab with aria-current. Any other value is passed through to the element unchanged.

props.name: overflow
props.description: What happens when the tabs are wider than the strip. 'auto' lets the component choose, which today always scrolls. 'scroll' scrolls the tabs horizontally, with edge fades and arrow affordances for pointers that can hover. 'visible' turns overflow handling off and lets the tabs spill out of the strip. The selected tab is always scrolled back into view.

props.name: children
props.description: Tab and TabMenu items to render inside the strip.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: label
props.description: Label for the trigger button (shown when no option is selected) and the dropdown heading divider.

props.name: options
props.description: Array of menu options rendered in the dropdown.

Text.description: Text renders styled body text and headings from the theme. Use Text with a semantic type for body copy, labels, and captions, and Heading for section titles that output the correct h1–h6 element.

practices.text: Pick a semantic type (body, label, supporting, large, code) instead of manually setting size and weight; the theme handles the details.
Set accessibilityLevel on Heading when the visual level differs from the document outline so screen readers announce the correct hierarchy.
Use maxLines with a number to truncate long content; a tooltip appears automatically on hover so no text is lost.
Enable hasTabularNumbers for columns of numeric data so digits align vertically across rows.
Override size and weight when a semantic type already matches; extra overrides fight the theme and break when themes change.
Skip heading levels in the document outline; go h1 then h2 then h3, never h1 then h3.

Use raw HTML tags like

,

–

, or for text; Text and Heading apply the correct theme tokens automatically.
Pass a `variant` prop; Text does not have a `variant` prop. Use `type` for semantic styling (body, label, large, supporting, code) or use Heading for headings.
Use Text for headings; use Heading with a `level` prop (1–6) for section titles and headings.

props.name: type
props.description: Semantic text type. Determines size, weight, and line-height from the theme. 'inherit' takes all three from the surrounding text instead. Themes may add custom types. Note: this prop is called `type`, not `variant`.

props.name: children
props.description: Text content.

props.name: size
props.description: Explicit font size override. Overrides the size from `type` but preserves other type properties. Prefer using `type` alone.

props.name: color
props.description: Text color. Defaults to 'secondary' for the 'supporting' type, 'primary' for all others. Themes may add custom colors.

props.name: weight
props.description: Font weight override.

props.name: display
props.description: Display type. Silently overridden to 'block' when maxLines > 0 or hasCapsize is true.

props.name: as
props.description: HTML element to render.

props.name: maxLines
props.description: Maximum lines before truncation. 0 means no truncation. When set, shows a tooltip on hover if content is truncated.

props.name: hasTruncateTooltip
props.description: Controls tooltip behavior for truncated text. true shows the tooltip at the default position, false disables it, or a placement string ('above' | 'below' | 'start' | 'end') sets a specific position.

props.name: wordBreak
props.description: Word break behavior when truncating. Defaults to 'break-all' for single-line truncation, 'break-word' otherwise. Without truncation, a token longer than its line (a URL, an ID) wraps (`overflow-wrap: break-word`), so in ordinary flow text does not make the page scroll sideways. Inside a flex row, give the flex child `min-width: 0` so it can shrink. A container you style with `overflow-wrap: anywhere` does not reach this text; Astryx's own containers pass their wrap through.

props.name: textWrap
props.description: Text wrapping behavior.

props.name: justify
props.description: Text alignment (justification). Uses logical values (start/end) for i18n/RTL compatibility.

props.name: hasCapsize
props.description: Enable optical alignment using text-box-trim. Forces block display.

props.name: hasStrikethrough
props.description: Apply strikethrough text decoration.

props.name: hasTabularNumbers
props.description: Use tabular (monospace) numbers for aligned numeric data.

props.name: id
props.description: HTML id attribute.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

TextArea.description: TextArea is a multi-line text input for collecting longer-form content like comments, descriptions, or messages. Use it when the expected input spans multiple lines. For shorter, single-line values, use TextInput.

practices.text: Provide a visible label so users know what to enter. If the label must be hidden, set isLabelHidden with a descriptive label for screen readers.
Set maxLength with a character counter when there is a defined limit; it helps users stay within bounds before they submit.
Keep Return a line break in a multi-line field. Relabel it with enterKeyHint (send, done) only when your own Enter handling does what the label says.
Use the status prop to surface validation feedback inline: show success when input is valid, warning for soft limits, and error for hard failures.
Add a description or placeholder to clarify expected content, like "Describe the issue in detail," but never rely on placeholder alone as the only label.
Avoid using TextArea for short, single-line values like names or emails; use TextInput instead.
Don't rely solely on placeholder text to communicate the purpose of the field; placeholders disappear on focus and are not accessible labels.
Don't show a status message without also setting the status type; the colored border and icon are what draw the user's attention to the message.
Don't wrap a disabled TextArea in Tooltip to explain why it's disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop, which attaches the reason to the field itself.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the underlying <textarea> element.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the textarea. Always rendered for accessibility.

props.name: value
props.description: Current value of the textarea.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the textarea value changes.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action fired after onChange inside a React transition. Enables optimistic updates via useOptimistic.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible to screen readers.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text displayed between the label and textarea.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Displays an "Optional" indicator next to the label. Mutually exclusive with isRequired.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Displays a "Required" indicator next to the label and sets aria-required. Mutually exclusive with isOptional.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the textarea, preventing interaction.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: Makes the textarea read-only: the value is shown at full opacity and still submits with the form, but cannot be edited. Unlike isDisabled, a read-only textarea is not dimmed and keeps its form value. isDisabled takes precedence when both are set.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the textarea is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the textarea focusable via aria-disabled (the field becomes read-only). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled TextArea in Tooltip, so the reason is attached to the field itself.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Puts the textarea in a loading state, showing a spinner inside the input.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when the textarea is empty.

props.name: rows
props.description: Number of visible text rows.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Maximum number of characters allowed, counted as user-perceived characters: an emoji or flag sequence counts as one. When set, a character counter (current/max) is displayed inside the input container, anchored to the bottom-right beneath the text. Does not enforce the limit natively; when exceeded the counter turns red and shows a warning icon (a non-color cue), and screen-reader users hear the remaining/over-limit count announced. Consumers validating the limit should count with characterCount (exported from the package) so enforcement matches the displayed count.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator that applies a colored border and icon. An optional message is displayed in a floating box below the textarea.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip hides the message box and surfaces it in a tooltip on the status icon.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text displayed in an info icon at the end of the label.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon component rendered inside the leading edge of the textarea wrapper. See `astryx docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: hasSpellCheck
props.description: Enables or disables browser spell checking.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Automatically focuses the textarea on mount.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the textarea, affecting internal padding. Height is controlled by rows, not size.

props.name: onPaste
props.description: Callback fired when content is pasted into the textarea.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: HTML name attribute for the textarea element, useful for form submissions.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Callback fired when the textarea receives focus.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Callback fired when the textarea loses focus.

props.name: autoComplete
props.description: The native autocomplete attribute, forwarded to the textarea unchanged. Does not affect the controlled value.

props.name: enterKeyHint
props.description: What the Return key of a touch keyboard says (the native `enterkeyhint`). iOS gives `done`, `go`, `next`, `search` and `send` their own key (a glyph on iOS 26: a checkmark, an arrow, a chevron, a magnifier, an up arrow); `enter` and `previous` keep the plain Return key. Chrome on Android (Gboard) gives every value its own key; with no hint a TextArea keeps Return. It only labels the key: what Enter does stays with your handlers.

props.name: inputMode
props.description: Which touch keyboard the field asks for (the native `inputmode`) without changing what it accepts: `numeric` brings up the number pad, `decimal` the decimal pad, `tel` the phone pad, `search` the web-search keyboard (whose Return key reads Go on iOS even with `enterKeyHint="search"`).

props.name: autoCapitalize
props.description: When a touch keyboard capitalizes as you type (the native `autocapitalize`). Unset, iOS capitalizes sentences. `off` and `none` never capitalize; `on` and `sentences` capitalize each sentence.

props.name: hasAutoCorrect
props.description: Whether a touch keyboard corrects words as you type (the native `autocorrect`). Unset, the browser decides; turn it off for usernames, codes and other values that are not words.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the element that paints the border and background and holds icons and end controls. Never the native input.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Class name for the visual control box.

props.name: controlStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the visual control box.

TextInput.description: TextInput collects short-form text like names, emails, or search queries. Use it for single-line values where the expected input is brief. Pair it with validation status to guide users through required or formatted fields.

practices.text: Always provide a visible label so users know what the field is for. Only hide the label when surrounding context makes it obvious, like a search bar with a magnifying-glass icon.
Use validation status with a message to explain what went wrong: "Email must include @" is better than just turning the border red.
Size the input to match the expected content length so users can gauge how much to type: small for zip codes, medium for names, large for URLs.
Add a clear button for search and filter inputs so users can quickly reset without selecting all text.

Tell a touch keyboard what the field holds: `type="email"`, `"tel"` or `"url"` for those values, `inputMode="numeric"` for digits that are not a number (a one-time code), `enterKeyHint` for what Return does (Search, Send, Next), and `autoComplete` so AutoFill can fill it.
Don't use placeholder text as a replacement for a label; placeholders disappear on focus and are not reliably read by screen readers.
Don't use TextInput for multi-line content like comments or descriptions; use TextArea instead.
Don't mark every field as required; only flag mandatory fields so users are not overwhelmed by validation errors.
Don't wrap a disabled TextInput in Tooltip to explain why it's disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop, which attaches the reason to the field itself.

props.name: type
props.description: The HTML input type. `email`, `tel` and `url` also bring up the matching touch keyboard (email, phone pad, URL); `search` makes the field a search box (pair it with `enterKeyHint="search"` for a Search key on iOS; Chrome on Android shows one for `type="search"` alone).

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the input: always rendered for accessibility.

props.name: value
props.description: Current value of the input.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the input value changes.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action fired after onChange (if not prevented). Triggers optimistic update and shows a loading spinner while pending.

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant of the input.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible to screen readers.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed between the label and input.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Displays an "Optional" indicator next to the label. Mutually exclusive with isRequired.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Displays a "Required" indicator next to the label and sets aria-required. Mutually exclusive with isOptional.

props.name: onEnter
props.description: Callback fired when the user presses the Enter key. IME-safe: Enter used to commit a Japanese/Chinese/Korean conversion does not fire it.

props.name: onKeyDown
props.description: Callback fired on keydown events on the input.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the input, preventing interaction and dimming the element.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: Makes the input read-only: the value is shown at full opacity and still submits with the form, but cannot be edited. Unlike isDisabled, a read-only input is not dimmed and keeps its form value. isDisabled takes precedence when both are set.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the input is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the input focusable via aria-disabled (the field becomes read-only). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled TextInput in Tooltip, so the reason is attached to the field itself.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Puts the input in a loading state, showing a spinner and setting aria-busy.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when the input is empty.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text displayed in an info icon at the end of the label.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: SVG icon component displayed at the start of the input. See `astryx docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status: applies a colored border and status icon. If message is provided, displays a floating message below the input. Error type also sets aria-invalid.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip hides the message box and surfaces it in a tooltip on the status icon.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Shows a clear (×) button when the input has a value. Clicking it clears the value and returns focus to the input.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Automatically focuses the input on mount.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: The HTML name attribute for the input, useful for form submissions.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned. Without a width the field can shrink with its row, so a filter bar never overflows; use `<HStack wrap="wrap">` when the controls should move to a second line instead.

props.name: autoComplete
props.description: The native autocomplete attribute, forwarded to the input unchanged. Does not affect the controlled value. It is also how AutoFill knows what a field holds: tag sign-in, address and payment fields (`username`, `new-password`, `one-time-code`, `email`, `tel`, `street-address`, …).

props.name: enterKeyHint
props.description: What the Return key of a touch keyboard says (the native `enterkeyhint`). iOS gives `done`, `go`, `next`, `search` and `send` their own key (a glyph on iOS 26: a checkmark, an arrow, a chevron, a magnifier, an up arrow); `enter` and `previous` keep the plain Return key. Chrome on Android (Gboard) gives every value its own key, `enter` and `previous` included; with no hint the key reads Next while another field follows, and a `type="url"` field shows Next instead of `go` while another field follows. It only labels the key: what Enter does stays with your handlers.

props.name: inputMode
props.description: Which touch keyboard the field asks for (the native `inputmode`) without changing what it accepts: `numeric` brings up the number pad, `decimal` the decimal pad, `tel` the phone pad, `search` the web-search keyboard (whose Return key reads Go on iOS even with `enterKeyHint="search"`; Chrome on Android shows the Enter key for `inputMode="search"` alone).

props.name: autoCapitalize
props.description: When a touch keyboard capitalizes as you type (the native `autocapitalize`). Unset, iOS capitalizes sentences, except in a URL field. `off` and `none` never capitalize; `on` and `sentences` capitalize each sentence.

props.name: hasAutoCorrect
props.description: Whether a touch keyboard corrects words as you type (the native `autocorrect`). Unset, the browser decides; turn it off for usernames, codes and other values that are not words.

props.name: hasSpellCheck
props.description: Whether misspelled words are underlined (the native `spellcheck`). Unset, the browser decides.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the element that paints the border and background and holds icons and end controls. Never the native input.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Class name for the visual control box.

props.name: controlStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the visual control box.

Thumbnail.description: Thumbnail displays a compact, square preview of an image attachment. It shows a shimmer effect while uploading, the image on success, and a placeholder icon when no source is set. Use it in chat composers, file upload lists, or anywhere you need a small image preview with optional remove and click actions.

practices.text: Always provide a label prop with the file name so the thumbnail and its remove button are accessible to screen readers and show a tooltip on hover.
Use isLoading without a src to show a skeleton during initial upload, and isLoading with a src to show a spinner overlay once a preview URL is available.
Pair onClick with a lightbox or detail view so users can inspect the full image; the thumbnail adds button semantics and a hover overlay automatically.
Don't use Thumbnail for non-image file types like PDFs or spreadsheets; use a file attachment component with an appropriate icon instead.
Don't omit alt text when a src is provided; screen readers need a description of the image content, not just the file name from label.

props.name: src
props.description: Image source URL.

props.name: alt
props.description: Alt text for the image. When omitted, the image is explicitly decorative (alt="", role="presentation", aria-hidden) and hidden from screen readers; a dev warning fires if neither alt nor label is set.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label (e.g. file name). Shown as tooltip on hover.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: Callback for the overlaid remove button.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler. Adds button semantics and a hover overlay.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Shows skeleton (no src) or upload overlay (with src).

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the thumbnail is disabled.

props.name: showRemoveOn
props.description: When the remove button is visible. `hover` (the default) reveals it on hover and on keyboard focus, and keeps it visible on any touch-capable device; `always` shows it at rest. Only applies when `onRemove` is set.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling; className is provided for integration with non-StyleX systems.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling; inline styles bypass StyleX optimization.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

TimeInput.description: TimeInput uses a browser/OS time picker on coarse pointers by default and Astryx's typed field on fine pointers. It converts values to a standard format and supports arrow-key adjustment on the typed surface. Use it in forms, scheduling flows, or any interface where users need to select a specific time.

practices.text: Base props such as ref, id, data-*, aria-*, and DOM event handlers go to the time input, the element that is focused and announced. A DOM handler runs after TimeInput's own handler for the same event and still receives events it handled (including ones it called preventDefault on), so it cannot cancel built-in behavior.

Leave hourFormat unset so the field follows the InternationalizationProvider locale's hour cycle (12-hour in en-US, 24-hour in en-GB or de-DE). Set it only when the field itself needs a fixed format, and carry a person's own 12/24-hour preference on the provider locale (e.g. 'en-US-u-hc-h23') rather than on each field.
Set min and max constraints when the context has a valid range, like business hours or event windows, so users cannot submit an out-of-bounds time.
Provide a description or placeholder that hints at the expected format or purpose, like "Business hours: 9 AM – 5 PM".
Use the status prop to surface validation errors inline: show a message like "Time must be during business hours" so users know exactly what to fix.
Enable hasClear when the field is optional, so users can remove a previously selected time.
Place TimeInput inside InputGroup when the time needs a single-line prefix or suffix addon, like a start/end label or timezone marker.
Don't use TimeInput for combined date-and-time selection; pair it with a separate DateInput instead.
Don't hide the label; even when space is tight, keep the label visible or provide a description so the purpose is clear.
Wrap a disabled TimeInput in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled. Use the disabledMessage prop instead, which ties the reason to the field.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the input (required for accessibility).

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible to screen readers.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed between the label and input.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Shows an "(optional)" indicator next to the label. Mutually exclusive with isRequired.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Marks the field as required and sets aria-required. Mutually exclusive with isOptional.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the input and suppresses interactions. The input stays focusable and exposes `aria-disabled`.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the input is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and describes the input (activation stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled TimeInput in Tooltip.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled time value in ISO format (HH:MM or HH:MM:SS).

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the time changes. Receives undefined when the input is cleared.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action fired after onChange. Wrapped in a React transition to provide optimistic UI; triggers the loading spinner while pending.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Puts the input into a loading state, displaying a spinner.

props.name: min
props.description: Minimum selectable time in ISO format. Values outside the range are rejected.

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum selectable time in ISO format. Values outside the range are rejected.

props.name: hasSeconds
props.description: Includes seconds in the time display and parsing.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Shows a clear button when a value is set and the input is not disabled.

props.name: hourFormat
props.description: Controls the display format. '12h' shows the locale's day period (e.g. '2:30 PM', '오후 2:30'); '24h' uses 24-hour notation (e.g. '14:30'). When unset, follows the InternationalizationProvider locale's hour cycle: en-US reads 12-hour, en-GB and de-DE read 24-hour. To honor a person's own preference, pass it on the locale tag (e.g. 'en-US-u-hc-h23') rather than per field.

props.name: increment
props.description: Number of minutes to add or subtract when the user presses the up or down arrow key. Steps are whole minutes; a fractional value leaves the time unchanged.

props.name: presentation
props.description: Which surface selects the time. 'adaptive-native' (the default) uses Astryx's typed field on a fine pointer and the browser/OS input type=time on a coarse pointer — except hasSeconds or increment other than 1, which retain the typed field because iOS has no seconds wheel and treats step as validation rather than picker cadence; 'native' always uses the browser/OS control with no Astryx fallback; 'adaptive-bottom-sheet' uses the typed field on a fine pointer and Astryx's bottom-sheet time wheels on a coarse pointer; 'bottom-sheet' forces the wheels on every pointer; 'text-input' (like 'popover', which has no distinct TimeInput surface) keeps only the typed field. Native mode forwards min/max and enforces them on commit. hourFormat formats the closed value; the open OS picker follows the device locale.

props.name: nativePicker
props.description: Deprecated: use presentation ('touch' = 'adaptive-native', 'always' = 'native', 'never' = 'text-input'). Still works exactly as released; presentation wins when both are set.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when no time is selected. When the input is focused and empty, a format hint overrides this text.

props.name: size
props.description: Controls the height of the input element.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator that colors the border and displays an icon. When a message is provided it is rendered below the input.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip hides the message box and surfaces it in a tooltip on the status icon.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text rendered as an info icon at the end of the label row.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the Field box around the label, control, and status. containerClassName and containerStyle take a class name and inline styles for the same box. No effect (development warning) where no Field box renders: inside InputGroup (style the group) and in a horizontal-labels FormLayout.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the bordered element that holds the text, icons, and end controls, never the native input. controlClassName and controlStyle take a class name and inline styles for the same box. Replaces root xstyle, className, and style, which this component does not accept.

Timer.description: Displays a standardized elapsed duration for active work without scheduling a React render on every tick. Elapsed format updates by second below one hour and by minute after one hour; clock format remains second-precise.

practices.text: Use elapsed for compact duration text that may span seconds, minutes, or hours.
Use clock for stopwatch-like surfaces where seconds remain meaningful after an hour.
Pass startTime when the operation began before Timer mounted so the display reflects the complete wait.
Do not use Timer for dates, time zones, or relative calendar language; use Timestamp instead.
Do not add aria-live unless hearing an announcement every tick is appropriate for the specific task.

props.name: startTime
props.description: Unix time in milliseconds when the measured operation began. Omit it to start from this Timer's mount.

props.name: format
props.description: Standard duration representation. Elapsed uses compact units and drops seconds after one hour; clock uses m:ss or h:mm:ss.

props.name: type
props.description: Semantic text type. Uses the same typography behavior as Timestamp.

props.name: size
props.description: Explicit font size override. Overrides the size from type.

props.name: color
props.description: Text color.

props.name: weight
props.description: Font weight override.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the Text wrapper. Must be a stylex.create() value.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name for the Text wrapper. Prefer xstyle for styling.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the Text wrapper. Prefer xstyle for styling.

Timestamp.description: Timestamp formats a date or time value into human-readable text. Use it to show when something was created, updated, or is scheduled; picking relative for recency, absolute for precision, or auto to let the component decide.

practices.text: Use the auto format in feeds and lists so recent items show "2 hours ago" and older items show the full date automatically.
Keep formatting consistent within the same list or table; mixing relative and absolute timestamps in the same column confuses scanning.
Enable isTimezoneShown when the audience spans multiple time zones, like a global team calendar or audit log.
Use tooltipEntries when readers must compare zones, such as an incident log where the reader's time and the event's origin zone both matter.

Pass timezoneID when an absolute time must read the same for every viewer and on the server, like an incident log timestamp or anything server-rendered; without it the server markup depends on the server zone.
Label every entry once a tooltip shows more than one zone; a bare abbreviation is not always recognizable (Tokyo renders as "GMT+9", not "JST").
Use isLive for active dashboards or real-time feeds so the relative time stays accurate without a page refresh.

Reach for tooltipEntries when readers need to grab an exact value: an incident log or deploy record where someone pastes the UTC time or Unix seconds elsewhere; configuring entries turns the hover into copy-to-clipboard rows.
Don't display raw Unix timestamps or ISO strings to users; always pass them through Timestamp to get a human-readable format.
Avoid system_date or system_time formats in user-facing UI; they are meant for developer tools, logs, and machine-readable contexts.
Don't disable the hover card on relative timestamps; users expect to hover for the full date when they see "3 hours ago".
Don't stack many zones into one card; it is capped at 300px wide and long labelled lines wrap. Two or three entries read well.

Don't pass a fixed-offset abbreviation like "EST" as timezoneID; it is a valid identifier but never observes daylight saving, so it reads an hour wrong for half the year. Use the region id, "America/New_York".

props.name: value
props.description: The date/time to display. Accepts Unix timestamps (seconds) or ISO 8601 strings.

props.name: format
props.description: Display format. 'relative' uses the locale's native long relative-time wording ('2 hours ago' in English), 'relative_short' uses its narrow pattern ('2h ago' in English) for compact surfaces, 'date' shows 'Mar 21, 2025', 'date_long' shows 'March 21, 2025', 'date_weekday' shows 'Wed, Mar 21, 2025', 'date_time' shows 'Mar 21, 2025, 2:51 PM', 'time' shows '2:51 PM', 'system_*' variants use ISO-style formatting, 'unix_seconds' shows the Unix time in whole seconds since the epoch (an absolute, zone-independent value), 'auto' switches from relative to date_time based on recency. Absolute formats never read the current time. 'relative', 'relative_short' and 'auto' read it on the client only: a server render or static prerender shows the full date and time in UTC, labelled, and the client switches to the format's normal output after hydration. Date-bearing formats ('date', 'date_long', 'date_weekday', 'date_time', and the full date in the hover card and the accessible name) use the InternationalizationProvider calendar, such as calendar="persian"; 'time', the relative formats, 'system_*', and 'unix_seconds' do not change.

props.name: timezoneID
props.description: IANA time zone the absolute formats render in, such as 'UTC' or 'America/Los_Angeles'. Omit (or pass 'local') for the viewer's own zone. An explicit zone renders identically on the server and the client, so it is the way to show an absolute time without a hydration mismatch; relative formats' visible text ignores it, while configured tooltipEntries rows still follow it. An unknown identifier warns once in development and falls back to the viewer's zone.

props.name: autoThreshold
props.description: Threshold in seconds for 'auto' format to switch from relative to date_time.

props.name: hasTooltip
props.description: Whether to show a copyable hover card with the full date/time on hover or keyboard focus. Applies to relative timestamps and to any format once tooltipEntries is configured.

props.name: tooltipEntries
props.type: ReadonlyArray<{timezoneID?: string; format?: TimestampTooltipFormat; label?: string; isCopyable?: boolean}>
props.description: Lines to show on hover, so one instant can be read (and optionally copied) in several time zones and/or formats at once. Each entry is one line, in the order given. An entry without timezoneID follows the Timestamp timezoneID when set, else the viewer's zone; 'local' always means the viewer's zone; format defaults to the full absolute style and also accepts 'full' alongside every non-relative TimestampFormat. Rows are read-only unless they set isCopyable (default false); copyable rows show a copy button in a dedicated trailing action column so buttons align, and the column is only present when some row is copyable. With no entries the card shows a single default row with the full absolute time, which is copyable. Configuring entries also attaches the surface to absolute formats, which otherwise have none.

props.name: isTimezoneShown
props.description: Whether to append the timezone abbreviation to the visible text. Applies to the date_time and time formats; system_* formats stay machine-readable and never carry one. Use tooltipEntries to control the tooltip's time zones.

props.name: isLive
props.description: Whether the relative time should update live (e.g. "2 min ago" → "3 min ago").

props.name: type
props.description: Semantic text type from Text. Determines size, weight, and line-height.

props.name: size
props.description: Explicit font size override. Overrides the size from type.

props.name: color
props.description: Text color.

props.name: weight
props.description: Font weight override.

Toast.description:
Toast shows a brief, non-blocking notification to confirm an action or present temporary information. Use it for scenarios where the user needs feedback but not a decision, such as saving, deleting, or changing a status.

For production use, prefer the `useToast()` hook; it handles positioning, stacking, auto-dismiss, and deduplication via `ToastViewport`. Toasts stay within viewport and safe-area gutters, wrap long message content, and enter, exit, or swipe-dismiss toward their configured top or bottom edge. The vertical swipe uses the same spatial model as placement motion: top Toasts leave upward and bottom Toasts leave downward. Swipe waits for dominant edge-directed intent before cancelling native touch movement and reports the existing manual dismissal reason. Pen is supported as direct-contact input; mouse drag is excluded to avoid conflicting with desktop text selection, where the visible close control remains available. Set `isAutoHide: false` explicitly when an action or message must remain available. The `Toast` component renders the visual toast element inline and is useful for previews, documentation, and static showcases where the viewport lifecycle is not needed.

practices.text: Keep messages short: only a few words that tell the user what happened, like "Changes saved" or "Message sent".
Add a short undo action in the endContent slot for reversible operations. Set isAutoHide to false when the action must remain available.
Use uniqueID to deduplicate toasts that fire from repeated actions, like clicking a save button multiple times.
Use error type for failures that need attention but not immediate action; it persists until dismissed so the user won't miss it.
Don't use a toast for critical errors that block the user. Use Banner for persistent, in-context messaging that requires acknowledgment.
Don't put long or multi-line content in a toast; it disappears after 5 seconds and the user may not finish reading.
Don't show form validation errors as toasts. Use inline field validation so the user can see exactly which field needs fixing.

props.name: body
props.description: Primary message content.

props.name: type
props.description: Toast type controlling background color. Error toasts persist until dismissed.

props.name: isAutoHide
props.description: Whether the toast auto-dismisses. Defaults to true for info, false for error.

props.name: autoHideDuration
props.description: Duration in ms before auto-dismiss. Timed content must satisfy WCAG 2.2.1.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content rendered at the trailing end (e.g. Undo button, link). Keep action labels short.

props.name: uniqueID
props.description: Unique identifier for deduplication.

props.name: collisionBehavior
props.description: Behavior when a toast with matching uniqueID already exists.

props.name: onHide
props.description: Callback fired when the toast is removed.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Callback fired when the toast is dismissed.

props.name: renderContent
props.description: Replaces the content of this toast's card with your own layout. Astryx keeps the card, its astryx-toast theme target and auto-hide behavior (inside a ToastViewport the viewport announces the toast, over a modal too, and the card itself is not a live region), then hands the renderer the message, endContent, resolved toast settings and a dismiss callback. The custom renderer owns every control in its layout: compose the control you want and call dismiss from it. Astryx does not inject a fallback close into custom content. Per-toast: an app shares one layout by wrapping useToast and passing it on every call, while a toast raised by library code that never passes it renders as an ordinary Astryx toast. The argument is {body, endContent, type, isAutoHide, autoHideDuration, dismiss}, where type is 'info' | 'error'.

Token.description: Token is a small, inline element for representing discrete pieces of associated data, like tags, categories, or selections. Use it to label content, show active filters, or represent removable items like selected recipients in a compose field.

practices.text: Use color to distinguish categories (for example, green for "Active", red for "Blocked", blue for "In Review") so users can scan status at a glance.
Provide an onRemove callback when tokens represent user selections that can be undone, like filters or multi-select values.
Add a leading icon when it helps identify the token type faster, like a person icon for user tokens or a tag icon for labels.
Keep labels short: one to three words. Tokens truncate with ellipsis when the text overflows.
Don't use tokens for primary actions or navigation; use Button or Link instead. Tokens are for displaying metadata, not triggering workflows.
Don't hide the label unless the icon alone is universally understood. A color dot without text is ambiguous.
Don't mix too many colors in one token group. Stick to two or three meaningful colors so the palette stays scannable.

props.name: label
props.description: Text label displayed inside the token.

props.name: size
props.description: The size of the token.

props.name: color
props.description: Color variant of the token.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon rendered before the label.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the token is disabled; reduces opacity and blocks interactions.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: Callback fired when the remove button is clicked. When provided, an X button is rendered inside the token.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler. When provided, the token renders as a <span> container with an invisible <button> inside for accessibility.

props.name: href
props.description: Link URL. When provided, the token renders as an <a> element. The destination follows the shared navigation rule described on the Link `href` prop.

props.name: description
props.description: Accessible description applied via aria-description on the root element.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content rendered after the label and before the remove button.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label using a screen-reader-only clip technique; the label remains accessible.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

Tokenizer.description: Tokenizer is a multi-select input that lets users search, select, and manage multiple items displayed as removable chips. Use it when users need to build a set of selections from a searchable data source, like adding team members, applying tags, or choosing filters.

practices.text: Write a placeholder that tells users what they can search for, such as "Search people..." or "Add tags...", so the input is not a blank mystery.
Set maxEntries when the number of selections should be bounded, like limiting a review to 5 approvers.
Use hasCreate for free-form tagging where users need to enter values that do not exist in the search source.
Show validation status with the status prop so users know immediately when a selection is missing or invalid.
Don't use Tokenizer for single-item selection; use Typeahead instead. Tokenizer is for building sets of two or more items.
Avoid applying custom colors to individual tokens inside a Tokenizer; use the default token style for visual consistency across the set.
Don't hide the label; every Tokenizer needs a visible label so users understand what they are selecting. Use isLabelHidden only when surrounding context makes the purpose obvious.
Wrap a disabled Tokenizer in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the input.

props.name: searchSource
props.description: Data source providing search and bootstrap methods. `search(query, context)` may call `context.update(items)` to show matches it already has before it returns; the value it returns is the final list, and every list after the first for a query keeps the shown rows first and adds new rows after them.

props.name: value
props.description: Array of currently selected items.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when selection changes. The change argument includes the affected item and type ('add' | 'create' | 'remove' | 'reorder'). Additions and removals (including Backspace on an empty input) are announced to screen readers via a polite live region.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Input placeholder text. Only shown when no tokens are selected.

props.name: maxEntries
props.description: Maximum number of selections allowed. Input is hidden when the limit is reached.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Show a clear-all button for bulk removal of all tokens.

props.name: renderToken
props.description: Custom render function for selected tokens. Default renders Token with label and onRemove.

props.name: renderItem
props.description: Custom render function for dropdown items. Default renders TypeaheadItem.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the input and all token interactions. The input keeps its tab stop: it is announced as disabled (aria-disabled), is read-only, and opens and picks nothing. With tokenOverflowBehavior="unfocusedLayer" and no disabledMessage, the input is natively disabled and out of the tab order.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: The HTML name attribute for form submissions. Renders one hidden input per selected item id.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the tokenizer is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the input focusable via aria-disabled (input stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled Tokenizer in Tooltip, so the reason is attached to the field itself.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status object with type and message for error/warning/success states.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip reveals the message in an info-tip button.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text displayed below the label.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Marks the field as required.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Shows an optional indicator on the label.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text shown on the label.

props.name: hasEntriesOnFocus
props.description: Show bootstrap results on focus before typing.

props.name: maxMenuItems
props.description: Maximum number of search results to display. The hasCreate entry is offered on top of them, so a menu can show one more than this.

props.name: menuWidth
props.description: Fixed dropdown width in pixels. The menu never shrinks below its anchor width.

props.name: minQueryLength
props.description: Minimum query length before the search source is queried. Below it no search runs, and the menu stays closed — unless hasCreate is set, in which case the "Create ..." entry is still offered, being derived from the typed text rather than fetched for it.

props.name: emptySearchText
props.description: Content shown when the query matched nothing. Takes a ReactNode, so the dead end can carry a link or a create row. Announced in a polite live region as the text it renders, read from the DOM; aria-hidden parts stay out of both, and content that renders no text announces nothing. null counts as not given, like undefined, and falls through to the default; pass an empty string to render nothing.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Auto-focus the input on mount.

props.name: size
props.description: Input and token size.

props.name: debounceMs
props.description: Debounce delay in ms before triggering search. Set to 0 for synchronous sources, and for a source that shows local matches through `context.update` and delays its own server request.

props.name: hasCreate
props.description: Allow users to create new tokens from free-text input. When true, a "Create" option appears in the dropdown for typed text that doesn't match existing results. The onChange change type is 'create' for these items.

props.name: onChangeQuery
props.description: Callback fired when the search query text changes.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon to display at the start of the input, before any tokens. Accepts a semantic icon name, an SVG icon component, or a ReactNode directly.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content to display at the end of the input row. Useful for buttons, result counts, or other controls.

props.name: handleRef
props.description: Imperative handle exposing focusInput(), focusFirstToken(), focusLastToken(), clearInput(), and selectAll().

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: tokenOverflowBehavior
props.description: Controls how tokens overflow when the container is too narrow.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Fires when focus enters the tokenizer input.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Fires when focus leaves the tokenizer input.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the element that paints the border and background and holds icons and end controls. Never the native input.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Class name for the visual control box.

props.name: controlStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the visual control box.

props.name: presentation
props.description: How the field presents its choices. adaptive (the default) uses the bottom sheet on compact touch screens and the popover otherwise, resolved the same way Selector resolves it; the server render and the hydrating render are the popover. popover is the inline combobox with its anchored suggestion menu on every device. bottom-sheet replaces it on every device with a field showing the selected tokens, whose trigger opens one tall modal sheet: a search row on top, full-width checkbox rows that keep their place while the sheet is open, a Create row with hasCreate, and a footer pinned in every state with a confirmed Clear all and Save; the sheet edits a draft, so onChange fires once, when Save commits it, and a swipe, scrim or Escape close of a changed draft asks before discarding. In the sheet presentation the field box holds the trigger, the tokens and endContent, and keeps the box, theming target and focus ring of the inline field; the trigger is the control: ref, id, aria-* and data-* reach it, and ref receives the trigger button there, so type it Ref<HTMLInputElement | HTMLButtonElement>, which the component accepts (TokenizerProps keeps its released input ref type). endContent sits at the inline end of the field and renderToken renders its tokens, as in the inline field; their own controls act without opening the sheet. renderItem, hasClear (the sheet has its own Clear all), hasEntriesOnFocus, menuWidth, tokenOverflowBehavior (the field wraps its tokens) and hasAutoFocus have no surface in the sheet, and the field warns once in development when they are passed. Pass presentation="popover" to keep the inline field and those props on every device.

Toolbar.description: Toolbar is a horizontal bar with left, center, and right areas. Use it for contextual actions within a content area (above a table, inside a card, or in a panel), not as a page-level header. Set the size once on the toolbar and all buttons, inputs, and tabs inside it match automatically.

practices.text: Put secondary actions like "Back" on the left, and primary actions like "Save" on the right.
Make temporary toolbars like bulk selection visually distinct so users can tell they're contextual, for example with a background color or border.
Visually separate the toolbar from the content below it, with a divider, a background variant, or both.

Use Toolbar as a card header when the header has interactive actions like filter or add; it gives you slot layout, keyboard navigation, and size cascading. If the header is just a title with no actions, a LayoutHeader or Section is enough.
Put too many actions in one toolbar; move less common items into a MoreMenu.
Set size on individual child buttons; set it once on the toolbar and it cascades automatically.
Use Toolbar for app-wide navigation like main menu links or sign out; use TopNav or LayoutHeader for that.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the toolbar, applied as aria-label.

props.name: startContent
props.description: Content aligned to the start (left in LTR).

props.name: centerContent
props.description: Centered content. Switches to the three-lane layout: centered while each side lane fits in half of the width it leaves, and the row wraps when the lanes do not fit.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content aligned to the end (right in LTR).

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the toolbar. Controls minimum height and coordinates with Button, TextInput, TabList, and Selector; children inherit this size as their default via SizeContext.

props.name: gap
props.description: Gap between items within each slot.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Orientation for keyboard navigation. Controls arrow key direction.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual variant passed to Section.

props.name: dividers
props.description: Borders/dividers rendered around the toolbar.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

Tooltip.description: A short text hint that appears on hover or focus, anchored to a trigger element. Use it to describe icon-only buttons, show the full text of truncated labels, or provide supplementary context without cluttering the UI.

practices.text: Keep tooltip content concise: aim for under 140 characters of plain text.
Add a tooltip to icon-only buttons and controls that lack a visible label.

Set touchTrigger to tap when the trigger is a button whose only job is revealing the tooltip: touch has no hover, and auto keeps the tap for triggers that perform an action. For an info icon, use InfoTip, which also pins its help on a press.
Place interactive elements like links or buttons inside a tooltip; use HoverCard or Popover instead.
Use tooltips for essential information that users must see to complete a task.

props.name: children
props.description: Trigger element(s) that activate the tooltip.

props.name: anchorRef
props.description: External anchor ref for sibling mode.

props.name: content
props.description: Tooltip content, typically short text.

props.name: placement
props.description: Position relative to the anchor element. Logical: start/end resolve against the popover's own inherited direction (RTL mirrors in pure CSS).

props.name: alignment
props.description: Alignment along the placement axis. Logical: start/end resolve against the popover's own inherited direction (RTL mirrors in pure CSS).

props.name: delay
props.description: Show delay in milliseconds.

props.name: hideDelay
props.description: Hide delay in milliseconds.

props.name: focusTrigger
props.description: Controls when focus events trigger the tooltip.

props.name: touchTrigger
props.description: What a tap does where there is no hover. auto opens on tap unless the trigger performs an action of its own (a button, link, or form control), whose tap belongs to the control; an aria-disabled control performs none, so a tap on it opens its reason. tap always opens, for a button whose only job is to reveal the tooltip; for an info icon, use InfoTip. none never opens on touch.

props.name: isEnabled
props.description: Enables or disables the tooltip triggers.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback fired when tooltip visibility changes. Called with true when shown and false when hidden.

props.name: hasHoverIndication
props.description: Shows a dashed underline on the trigger element.

props.name: isDefaultOpen
props.description: Whether the tooltip should be shown on mount. Still dismissible.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Controlled open state for the tooltip. Held closed, focus that would open it calls onOpenChange(true) and shows nothing; held open, Escape calls onOpenChange(false) and it stays.

TreeList.description: An expandable tree structure for displaying hierarchical data with branch connector lines. Use it for file explorers, nested category browsers, or any interface that visualizes parent-child relationships. Under a finger, expanding a row glides the rows below it while its children fade in on the same timing, and a collapse plays it back; pass an `animatedLayout` handle for content after the tree to glide too.

practices.text: Provide meaningful labels and icons for each node to make the hierarchy easy to scan.
Pre-expand important branches so users see key content immediately.

Leaf rows reserve space for a chevron column whenever the tree has any expandable item to line up under; only a fully flat tree (no expandable items at all) renders its rows flush. Rely on this rather than nudging indentation with custom CSS.
Nest more than 4–5 levels deep; flatten the structure or use a different pattern.
Use a tree for flat, non-hierarchical data; use a List instead.

props.name: items
props.description: Recursive tree item data with id, label, optional children and isExpanded, plus optional xstyle, className, and style applied to that item row.

props.name: density
props.description: Spacing density for items.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual treatment of the hierarchy guide lines. lineGuides shows connector lines; noGuides hides them, keeping indentation. Orthogonal to density.

props.name: animatedLayout
props.description: The handle from useAnimatedLayout({containerRef}). With it, expanding or collapsing a row glides the rows and content after it, up to that container, on one shared motion role instead of jumping, and the shown rows and the chevron move on the same motion. Without it, the content after the row takes its place at once.

props.name: header
props.description: Header content, associated with the tree via aria-labelledby.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

BaseTypeahead.description: Composable combobox engine providing a bare input, search, keyboard navigation, and a styled result dropdown. It renders no input wrapper, border, or selected-value token. Typeahead and Tokenizer compose it for standard fields.

practices.text: Use Typeahead or Tokenizer for standard fields; they wrap BaseTypeahead with input chrome and selected-value rendering it intentionally omits.
Provide your own visible label or aria-label and custom input wrapper so the bare combobox has an accessible name, focus treatment, border, and layout.
Pass anchorRef pointing to your wrapper so the dropdown positions against your custom input chrome, not just the bare input element.
Expect input chrome or selected-value rendering. BaseTypeahead is an engine; the caller owns those visible parts.
Use BaseTypeahead when Typeahead or Tokenizer would suffice; the extra wrapper and styling work is only justified for truly custom compositions.
Treat Escape as cancellation of pending source work. It hides the current popup, but a late response can reopen it.

props.name: searchSource
props.description: Data source providing search and bootstrap methods. `search(query, context)` may call `context.update(items)` to show matches it already has before it returns; the value it returns is the final list, and every list after the first for a query keeps the shown rows first and adds new rows after them.

props.name: value
props.description: Currently selected item.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when the selection changes.

props.name: renderItem
props.description: Custom render function for dropdown items.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Input placeholder text.

props.name: hasEntriesOnFocus
props.description: Show bootstrap results on focus before typing.

props.name: maxMenuItems
props.description: Maximum dropdown items to display.

props.name: menuWidth
props.description: Requested dropdown width in pixels before viewport clamping.

props.name: minQueryLength
props.description: Minimum query length before the search source is queried. Below it no search runs and the menu stays closed.

props.name: emptySearchText
props.description: Content shown when the query matched nothing. Takes a ReactNode, so the dead end can carry a link or a create row. Announced in a polite live region as the text it renders, read from the DOM; aria-hidden parts stay out of both, and content that renders no text announces nothing. null counts as not given, like undefined, and falls through to the default; pass an empty string to render nothing.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the input is disabled.

props.name: isFocusableDisabled
props.description: Keep a disabled input focusable with aria-disabled and readOnly so a caller-owned disabled reason remains discoverable. It blocks text entry, opening the results and picking a result, also from results that were open before it applied; Escape or Tab still closes them.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Auto-focus the input on mount.

props.name: debounceMs
props.description: Debounce delay in ms before triggering search. Set to 0 for synchronous sources, and for a source that shows local matches through `context.update` and delays its own server request.

props.name: size
props.description: Size used to scale dropdown option padding.

props.name: anchorRef
props.description: Ref to the anchor element for dropdown positioning. If not provided, the input itself is used.

props.name: inputXStyle
props.description: Additional StyleX styles for the input element.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: Standard BaseProps StyleX styles applied to the input. Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object.

props.name: inputTabIndex
props.description: Legacy input-specific alias for native tabIndex. When provided, it takes precedence; otherwise native tabIndex is preserved.

props.name: onKeyDown
props.description: Additional keydown handler called before internal keyboard navigation. Call e.preventDefault() to skip internal handling.

props.name: onChangeQuery
props.description: Callback fired when the search query text changes.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback when the dropdown opens or closes.

props.name: menu
props.description: What the menu shows. role 'listbox' (default) is the result list; its optional render({listbox, query, isBusy, isEmptySearch, close}) places information such as a header or a hint around it, and anything a person acts on stays a result so the arrow keys reach it. role 'dialog' shows render({query, close}) in a dialog named by label that takes focus; Escape, an outside press or close() returns focus to where it was when the menu opened. Astryx owns the layer either way. Switching from listbox to dialog keeps the menu open: call handleRef.open() from onChange.

props.name: handleRef
props.description: Imperative handle: open() opens the menu (a dialog at once; a listbox shows or loads its results) and close() closes it. There is no controlled open state; onOpenChange reports changes.

props.name: inputId
props.description: Legacy input-specific alias for native id. When provided, it takes precedence; otherwise native id is preserved.

props.name: ariaDescribedBy
props.description: Legacy input-specific alias for native aria-describedby. When provided, it takes precedence; otherwise the native attribute is preserved.

props.name: ariaLabelledBy
props.description: Legacy input-specific alias for native aria-labelledby. When provided, it takes precedence; otherwise the native attribute is preserved.

Typeahead.description: A searchable input for selecting a single item from a large or dynamic dataset. Results appear as the user types, with support for async data sources, debounced search, and custom item rendering. Use it when the option list is too large for a Selector dropdown.

practices.text: Provide descriptive placeholder text that hints at what users can search for.
Show suggestions on focus when users benefit from seeing popular or recent options before typing.
Add a search delay for remote data sources to avoid excessive network requests.

For a remote source, show the matches the page already has at once: call `context.update(local)` in `search`, pass `debounceMs={0}`, delay the server request in the source, and return the server answer with the shown rows first.
Use inside InputGroup when the typeahead needs a single-line prefix or suffix addon.
Use for short, static option lists; use Selector for better discoverability.
Use for multi-selection; use Tokenizer instead.
Place multiple Typeaheads adjacent to each other without clear labels differentiating them.
Wrap a disabled Typeahead in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled triggers swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the input.

props.name: searchSource
props.description: Data source providing search and bootstrap methods. `search(query, context)` may call `context.update(items)` to show matches it already has before it returns; the value it returns is the final list, and every list after the first for a query keeps the shown rows first and adds new rows after them.

props.name: value
props.description: Currently selected item, or null if nothing is selected.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when the selection changes.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Input placeholder text.

props.name: hasEntriesOnFocus
props.description: Show bootstrap results on focus before typing.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Show clear button to deselect the current value.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the input. The field keeps its tab stop: it is announced as disabled (aria-disabled), is read-only, and opens and picks nothing.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the input is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus, and the reason describes the field (activation stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled Typeahead in Tooltip, so the reason is attached to the field itself.

props.name: maxMenuItems
props.description: Maximum number of dropdown items to display.

props.name: minQueryLength
props.description: Minimum query length before the search source is queried. Below it no search runs and the menu stays closed.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status object with type and message for error/warning/success states.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip reveals the message in an info-tip button.

props.name: renderItem
props.description: Custom render function for dropdown items. Default renders TypeaheadItem.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text displayed below the label.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Marks the field as required.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Shows an optional indicator on the label.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text shown on the label.

props.name: emptySearchText
props.description: Content shown when the query matched nothing. Takes a ReactNode, so the dead end can carry a link or a create row. Announced in a polite live region as the text it renders, read from the DOM; aria-hidden parts stay out of both, and content that renders no text announces nothing. null counts as not given, like undefined, and falls through to the default; pass an empty string to render nothing.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Auto-focus the input on mount.

props.name: size
props.description: Input and token size.

props.name: debounceMs
props.description: Debounce delay in ms before triggering search. Set to 0 for synchronous sources, and for a source that shows local matches through `context.update` and delays its own server request.

props.name: onChangeQuery
props.description: Callback fired when the search query text changes.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback when the dropdown opens or closes.

props.name: menu
props.description: What the menu shows. role 'listbox' (default) is the result list; its optional render({listbox, query, isBusy, isEmptySearch, close}) places information such as a header or a hint around it, and anything a person acts on stays a result so the arrow keys reach it. role 'dialog' shows render({query, close}) in a dialog named by label that takes focus; Escape, an outside press or close() returns focus to where it was when the menu opened. Astryx owns the layer either way. Switching from listbox to dialog keeps the menu open: call handleRef.open() from onChange.

props.name: handleRef
props.description: Imperative handle: open() opens the menu (a dialog at once; a listbox shows or loads its results) and close() closes it. There is no controlled open state; onOpenChange reports changes.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: SVG icon component displayed at the start of the input.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the element that paints the border and background and holds icons and end controls. Never the native input.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Class name for the visual control box.

props.name: controlStyle
