props.description: Inline styles for the visual control box.

props.name: item
props.description: The search result item to render.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon or avatar to display before the label.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed below the label.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether this item is visually disabled.

props.name: group
props.description: This prop has no effect. Set `item.auxiliaryData.group` on search-source items to group results in Typeahead or BaseTypeahead.

InternationalizationProvider.description: Wraps your app to set the active locale and (optionally) merge additional translation catalogs + per-locale overrides. Astryx components inside the subtree resolve their strings against this context. If no provider is present, components fall back to the shipped English defaults.

practices.text: Use shipped Astryx locale catalogs from `@astryxdesign/core/locales/*` when one exists for your target locale.
Use a same-shape local catalog only when Astryx has not shipped that locale yet or you are testing in-progress translations.
Use real BCP 47 tags such as `fr-FR`, `pt-BR`, or `ar-SA`; regional locales fall back to their base language before English.

Set the `dir` attribute on `<html>` (or a wrapping element) yourself; the provider does not set it. Astryx components mirror layout and directional icons from the DOM `dir`, so an RTL locale won't visually mirror without it. Use `getLocaleDirection(locale)` to derive the value for both the provider and the DOM.

Set `calendar` to show `Calendar`, `DateInput`, `DateRangeInput`, and `DateTimeInput` in another calendar system and write Timestamp, PowerSearch, and Schedule dates in it. A locale never selects the calendar: `fa-IR` shows Gregorian dates until you set `calendar="persian"`, and a `-u-ca-` keyword in `locale`, as in `th-TH-u-ca-buddhist`, keeps Gregorian dates too. Date values stay Gregorian ISO strings.
Cast custom catalog maps to `any`; the i18n package exports `ProviderMessagesByLocale`, `MessagesByLocale`, `Catalog`, and `RuntimeCatalog` for local catalog typing.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP 47 language tag for the active locale (e.g. "en", "pt", "pt-BR", "zh-Hans"). Regional tags fall back to their base language, then to the shipped "en" catalog.

props.name: messages
props.description: Optional map of BCP 47 tag to a rich or generated runtime catalog. Import compact shipped catalogs from `@astryxdesign/core/locales/*.generated.js`; the shipped "en" catalog is always available and does not need to be listed here.

props.name: overrides
props.description: Sparse per-locale key overrides applied on top of shipped defaults. Overrides are locale-keyed so a runtime locale swap picks up the correct set.

props.name: dir
props.description: Explicit text-direction override for the context. When omitted, direction is derived from `locale` via `Intl.Locale.getTextInfo()`. This sets the direction Astryx reads, but it does NOT set the DOM `dir` attribute; you must set `dir` on `<html>` (or a wrapping element) yourself, since Astryx components mirror layout and directional icons from the DOM `dir`, not from this prop. Set both to the same value and keep them in sync.

props.name: calendar
props.description: Calendar system of the subtree, such as 'persian', 'hebrew', or 'buddhist'. `Calendar`, `DateInput`, `DateRangeInput`, and `DateTimeInput` show it, and Timestamp, PowerSearch, and Lab's Schedule write their dates in it. When omitted, the calendar is Gregorian: a locale never selects it, neither by its default calendar nor by a `-u-ca-` keyword. A component's own `calendar` prop takes precedence. Values stay Gregorian ISO dates. Calendars other than gregory, iso8601, buddhist, roc, and japanese need `Temporal`; the context keeps the requested calendar, and where the runtime lacks `Temporal`, these components show Gregorian dates and warn in development. Load a polyfill such as `temporal-polyfill/full/global` on the server and in the browser.

props.name: children
props.description: Content to render with the internationalization provider.

LinkProvider.description: Wraps your app to replace the default <a> tag with a framework-specific link component (e.g. Next.js Link) for client-side routing across all Astryx components.

props.name: component
props.description: Link component to use for all link elements in the subtree (e.g. Next.js Link). It receives accepted `href` and `to` values under the shared navigation rule described on the Link `href` prop. Supported structured destinations, including their `protocol`, are checked without changing object identity. If either supplied destination is rejected, Astryx renders inert content without invoking this component; it does not pass undefined or fall back to the other destination.

props.name: children
props.description: Content to render with the link provider.

MediaTheme.description: Provides token overrides for content rendered on inverted surfaces: media overlays, scrims, toasts, and tooltips. The base behavior flips color-scheme so all light-dark() tokens resolve to the correct side. Only a small set of tokens need explicit overrides beyond that. Themes can further customize component appearance on media surfaces via onDark/onLight in defineTheme(), with both token overrides (e.g. "--color-accent": "#90CAF9") and component overrides (e.g. ghost buttons get a border on dark surfaces).

practices.text: Use for any content placed over a dark background (image overlays, video scrims, dark cards) or other inverted surfaces like toasts and tooltips.

Prefer mode="auto" when the surface color comes from a theme token. A token named "inverted" is not guaranteed to be inverted, and auto measures what was actually painted instead of trusting the name. It can even decide that a surface needs no media context at all.
Pair with a background color: MediaTheme flips the token context but does not add a background. Set backgroundColor on the parent element.
Themes can customize components on media surfaces via onDark.components and onLight.components in defineTheme(). For example, add a border to ghost buttons on dark surfaces.
Use MediaTheme for app-level dark mode: use Theme with mode="dark" or mode="system" instead. MediaTheme is for local surface inversions, not page-wide color scheme.

props.name: mode
props.description: Surface luminance context: dark for content over dark backgrounds (light text, white-tinted interactions), light for content over light backgrounds (dark text, black-tinted interactions), auto to decide from the painted surface (no media context when the ambient text already reads on the surface at 3:1, otherwise the side that reads better), and off to turn it off explicitly. The element renders either way, so a surface can switch contexts without remounting children.

props.name: fallback
props.description: Which side auto uses when the surface cannot be measured: during SSR, on the first client frame, and whenever the backdrop is not knowable from CSS, most often a background-image, whose pixels need sampling (useImageMode) rather than a computed style. Ignored unless mode is auto.

props.name: children
props.description: Content to render with inverted token context. Components inherit the correct colors automatically.

practices.text: Build app themes that are known ahead of time with `astryx theme build`, then import the generated CSS and built theme object.
Use runtime themes when the theme is created or edited in the browser, such as theme editors, user branding, or prototypes.
Token names always start with `--` (e.g. `--color-accent`, `--color-background-surface`). Do not omit the prefix.
Default to runtime themes in SSR production apps. Component overrides inject after hydration instead of shipping as static CSS.

props.name: theme
props.description: Theme object to apply. Prefer built theme objects for static production themes; use runtime `defineTheme()` for dynamic themes. Its `motion` can set `tempo` (0.75–1.5) and `character` (`'crisp' | 'standard' | 'expressive'`).

props.name: mode
props.description: Color mode. System follows OS preference.

props.name: children
props.description: Content to render with the theme.

VisuallyHidden.description: Renders content in the accessibility tree while hiding it visually. Use for accessible names on icon-only controls, aria-live announcement regions, and supplementary screen-reader context. Deliberately has no styling props; the whole point is to stay invisible. `xstyle` is still accepted and ignored, only so code written against 0.7.2 keeps compiling; a planned minor removes it.

practices.text: Use to give icon-only buttons and controls an accessible name that screen readers announce.
Render as a block element (as="div") with aria-live to announce dynamic updates like drag-and-drop or result counts.
Use it to hide content from everyone; it stays in the accessibility tree; use conditional rendering or `hidden` to remove content entirely.
Put interactive controls inside it; the content is not visible and cannot receive pointer input.

props.name: children
props.description: Content exposed to assistive technology while hidden from sight.

props.name: as
props.description: HTML tag to render as. Use a block element for live regions.
